api.name: variant
api.description: Which treatment to use. All of them read the active colour set.

api.name: color
api.description: Named colour set. Drives fill, text, tint and border together. Ignored when tint is set.

api.name: tint
api.description: Any CSS colour, used instead of a named set. Fill, text, hover and border are all derived from it.

api.name: size
api.description: Height, padding, icon size and corner radius as one step. icon-* sizes are square.

api.name: asChild
api.description: Render the single child element instead of a <button>, keeping every style. Useful for links.

api.name: disabled
api.description: Native disabled state; drops opacity and blocks pointer events.

button-group.label: Button Group
button-group.description: Joins controls into one segmented unit — buttons, inputs, selects, or a mix. Inner corners are squared and adjacent borders overlap, so the row reads as a single control rather than a queue of separate ones.
button-group.usage:
import { ButtonGroup } from '@/components/ui/button-group'

  <Button variant="secondary">Copy</Button>
  <Button variant="secondary">Paste</Button>
</ButtonGroup>

<ButtonGroup grow>
  <Input placeholder="Search" />
  <Button>Search</Button>
</ButtonGroup>

api.name: responsive
api.description: Breakpoint a horizontal group becomes a row at; below it the group stacks and welds its top and bottom edges instead of its sides. Defaults to false because a pair of icon buttons is fine at any width — set it for a field-and-button row, which is not. Ignored when orientation is vertical.

api.name: orientation
api.description: Which edges are joined. Vertical squares the top and bottom corners instead of the sides.

api.name: grow
api.description: Fill the width and let fields take the free space — the shape a search box plus a button wants.

api.name: ButtonGroupText
api.description: A non-interactive segment: a unit, a prefix, a counter. Takes the same size scale as the controls beside it.

api.name: ButtonGroupSeparator
api.description: A rule between two segments that share a fill, where the collapsed borders leave no visible seam.

api.name: nested triggers
api.description: Select and Combobox render a wrapper around their trigger, so the corner rules reach one level down as well as at the top level.

api.name: role
api.description: Not "toolbar" — a toolbar implies arrow-key navigation between its controls. These are ordinary tab stops that happen to share edges.

form.label: Form
form.description: A thin bridge between React Hook Form and Field. Field owns the accessibility wiring and knows nothing about any form library; this adds only state and validation.
form.usage:
import { useForm } from 'react-hook-form'
import { zodResolver } from '@hookform/resolvers/zod'
import { z } from 'zod'
import { Form, FormField } from '@/components/ui/form'

const schema = z.object({ email: z.email('Enter a valid email.') })

const form = useForm({ resolver: zodResolver(schema), mode: 'onTouched' })

<Form form={form} onSubmit={save}>
  <FormField name="email" label="Email" required>
    {(field) => <Input {...field} type="email" />}
  </FormField>
  <Button type="submit">Save</Button>
</Form>

api.name: Form form
api.description: The instance from useForm(). Provided to descendants, so nested fields need no prop drilling.

api.name: Form onSubmit
api.description: Runs only after validation passes. The form is noValidate, so the resolver decides — browser bubbles cannot be styled.

api.name: FormField name
api.description: Typed against the schema, so a rename is a compile error rather than a silent no-op.

api.name: FormField children
api.description: Render prop. Half the controls take value/onValueChange and half take checked/onChange, so mapping is the caller's job.

api.name: FormField label / description / required
api.description: Passed through to Field and FieldLabel.

api.name: errors
api.description: The message from the resolver is handed to Field, which is what flips aria-invalid and shows it. There is no second flag.

dropzone.label: Dropzone
dropzone.description: The upload card: click it or drag onto it, and it runs the upload. Hand it onUpload and it moves each file through queued, uploading, done or error, reports progress, and keeps failures on screen with a retry.

api.name: onUpload
api.description: Runs the upload. Resolve to succeed — the value lands on upload.result; throw to fail, and the message shows on the row with a retry.

api.name: FileUpload
api.type: { id, file, name, size, type, lastModified, status, progress, result?, error? }
api.description: The structured payload handed to onUpload. `file` is the browser File — put it straight into a FormData.

api.name: UploadControl
api.description: Pass the signal to fetch so removing a file aborts its request; call onProgress with 0–1 to drive the bar.

api.name: isUploading
api.description: Forces the busy state, for when the request is yours rather than onUpload’s. Shows the spinner and blocks further picking.

api.name: uploadingLabel / doneLabel
api.description: The card names the file in flight and reports the total when it settles.

api.name: accept / multiple
api.description: Both are enforced on drop as well as on pick — a dropped file never went through the picker, so the browser never filtered it.

api.name: maxSize
api.description: Bytes. Rejected before the request is made, so an oversized file never leaves the browser.

api.name: accessibility
api.description: The card is a real button wrapping a hidden file input, so there is one tab stop and drag-and-drop is never the only way in.

input-file.label: Input File
input-file.description: A file picker shaped like an Input that also runs the upload. Hand it onUpload and it moves each file through queued, uploading, done or error, reports progress, and keeps failures on screen with a retry.

api.name: onUpload
api.description: Runs the upload. Resolve to succeed — the value lands on upload.result; throw to fail, and the thrown message shows on the row with a retry.

api.name: FileUpload
api.type: { id, file, name, size, type, lastModified, status, progress, result?, error? }

api.name: UploadControl
api.description: Pass the signal to fetch so removing a file aborts its request; call onProgress with 0–1 to drive the bar.

api.name: onSelect / onUploadsChange
api.description: Selection before any upload starts, and every transition after — for a form that needs the ids.

api.name: maxSize / maxSizeLabel
api.description: Rejected before the request is made, so an oversized file never leaves the browser.

api.name: size / variant
api.description: The same field scales as Input, so the two line up in a form. The trigger is capped at sm, since the xs control is a true pill and reads wrong inside a field.

api.name: showList
api.description: Renders UploadList underneath, with per-file progress, retry and remove.

api.name: accessibility
api.description: The hidden native input stays the focusable control and is named by the visible summary; the ring is drawn on the wrapper with focus-within.

api.name: options
api.description: `{ value, label, description?, disabled? }`.

api.name: value / onValueChange
api.description: Controlled or uncontrolled.

api.name: maxShown
api.description: Chips before collapsing to a count. Rendering every chip makes the trigger grow without limit and pushes the rest of the form around.

api.name: closing
api.description: Multi-select exists because people pick more than one thing; closing after each is the most common complaint about these controls.

mask-input.label: Mask Input
mask-input.description: Formats as you type — card numbers, phone numbers, dates. Hands back the raw characters alongside the formatted text, so a form does not submit "(555) 010-9999" to an API expecting digits.
mask-input.usage:
import { MaskInput } from '@/components/ui/mask-input'

<MaskInput mask="#### #### #### ####" onValueChange={(text, raw) => setCard(raw)} />

api.name: mask
api.description: `#` a digit, `A` a letter, `*` either. Anything else is a literal the component inserts.

api.name: onValueChange
api.description: Both forms, so the display value and the submitted value can differ.

api.name: backspace
api.description: Deleting into a literal removes the character before it, so backspace over the space in "4242 4242" takes a digit rather than sticking.

api.name: paste
api.description: Characters that do not fit a slot are skipped rather than stopping the fill, so pasting "4242-4242" into a digits mask keeps the digits.

time-picker.label: Time Picker
time-picker.description: Pick a time of day from generated slots. The value is always HH:mm in 24-hour form regardless of how it is displayed — the format is presentation, the value is data.
time-picker.usage:
import { TimePicker } from '@/components/ui/time-picker'

<TimePicker value={time} onValueChange={setTime} interval={15} />

api.name: value / onValueChange
api.description: `HH:mm`, 24-hour, whatever the display format.

api.name: interval
api.description: Minutes between options.

api.name: min / max
api.description: Bounds the generated list — business hours, a booking window.

api.name: hour12 / locale
api.description: Display only; formatting goes through Intl.

api.name: no free entry
api.description: Typing a time is a parsing problem with a dozen ambiguous cases ("230", "2.30", "14h"); for scheduling, slots are what people want.

color-picker.label: Color Picker
color-picker.description: A palette first, free entry second. Most product colour pickers choose a label or category colour, where an arbitrary hex is a liability — a gradient invites a colour nobody can read text on.

api.name: value / onValueChange
api.description: Any CSS colour; the palette supplies hex.

api.name: swatches
api.description: Overrides the default twenty. `DEFAULT_SWATCHES` is exported.

api.name: allowCustom
api.description: Adds the hex field and the native picker. The native input is an escape hatch, not the main control — it opens the unstyleable OS picker.

api.name: tick contrast
api.description: Shared with LabelPicker, so the check mark is visible on both a pale yellow and a navy.

range-slider.label: Range Slider
range-slider.description: Two thumbs over one track. Slider is a restyled native input[type=range], which has exactly one thumb by construction — so a range needs a custom control with the ARIA written out.
range-slider.usage:
import { RangeSlider } from '@/components/ui/range-slider'

<RangeSlider min={0} max={1000} step={10} value={range} onValueChange={setRange} />

api.name: value / onValueChange
api.description: Always sorted low-to-high on write.

api.name: onValueCommit
api.description: Fires once on release, for anything expensive to run per frame.

api.name: crossing
api.description: Dragging the low thumb past the high one swaps which is which. Clamping is more common and feels broken — the pointer keeps moving while the thumb stays put.

api.name: accessibility
api.description: Each thumb is a button with role="slider" and its own bounds, so both are tab stops and both announce.

api.name: size
api.description: Reads the shared sliderSize tokens, so it lines up with a plain Slider of the same size.

rating.label: Rating
rating.description: A rating, readable or settable, drawn with monochrome marks. The icon is a prop; read-only renders one image with a text alternative — "4 out of 5" — rather than five separate announcements.
rating.usage:
import { Rating } from '@/components/ui/rating'

<Rating value={rating} onValueChange={setRating} />
<Rating value={4.5} readOnly showValue />

api.name: value / onValueChange
api.description: Clicking the current value clears it back to zero.

api.name: readOnly
api.description: Switches from a radio group to a single labelled image.

api.name: count
api.description: Number of marks.

api.name: icon
api.description: The mark — any lucide icon or your own SVG component. A component, not an element: each mark renders twice, once as the outline and once clipped for the fill, so an element would leave a half value with nothing to clip.

api.name: half values
api.description: Rendered by clipping the icon rather than a second half-filled glyph, so 3.5 stays aligned with 3 on the same grid.

demos.title: Icons and states
demos.code:
<Rating defaultValue={3} />
<Rating defaultValue={4} icon={Star} />
<Rating value={4.5} readOnly showValue />

segmented-control.label: Segmented Control
segmented-control.description: A small set of mutually exclusive choices shown at once, built from real radio inputs in a fieldset — so arrow keys, form submission and screen-reader announcement all work without any script.
segmented-control.usage:
import { SegmentedControl } from '@/components/ui/segmented-control'

<SegmentedControl label="View" options={options} value={view} onValueChange={setView} />

api.name: options
api.description: { value, label, srLabel?, disabled? }. Keep it under about five with short labels.

api.name: radios, not buttons
api.description: It picks a value, so it is a radio group. A row of buttons with aria-pressed gets arrow keys, :checked and form submission wrong.

api.name: vs ButtonGroup / Tabs
api.description: A button group is independent actions; tabs switch a visible panel and carry aria-controls. This sets a value.

api.name: indicator
api.description: Positioned by index rather than a background on the selected item, so it slides instead of blinking and there is one thing to animate.

api.name: fullWidth
api.description: Fill the container, splitting the width evenly.

phone-input.label: Phone Input
phone-input.description: A country selector and a national number that together produce E.164 — the shape every telephony API wants. Honest about not being a validator.
phone-input.usage:
import { PhoneInput } from '@/components/ui/phone-input'

<PhoneInput value={phone} onChange={setPhone} defaultCountry="GB" />

api.name: value
api.description: `+441632960961` — digits and a leading plus. Storing the pretty version means every consumer re-parses it and they disagree about how.

api.name: not a validator
api.description: Real validation is a per-country length and prefix table that changes as regulators allocate ranges. That is libphonenumber, and it is 200 kB+. This checks a plausible length and reports it through `onValidChange` without blocking typing.

api.name: vs MaskInput
api.description: Formatting is per country and often per prefix inside one. A fixed `(___) ___-____` is wrong for most of the world and blocks valid numbers.

api.name: countries
api.description: A short default is exported as `COMMON_COUNTRIES`. The right list is usually "the countries you ship to", not all 249.

api.name: autoComplete
api.description: Set so a password manager can fill it, with `inputMode="tel"` for the phone keypad.

currency-input.label: Currency Input
currency-input.description: A money field whose value is an integer number of minor units, formatted only while unfocused. Reads its decimal count from Intl, so zero-decimal currencies work without a special case.
currency-input.usage:
import { CurrencyInput } from '@/components/ui/currency-input'

<CurrencyInput value={cents} onChange={setCents} currency="EUR" />

api.name: value
api.description: `1234` is $12.34. Floats cannot represent most decimal fractions, so a total assembled from float prices drifts by a cent — and every payment API takes integer minor units for that reason.

api.name: zero-decimal currencies
api.description: JPY, KRW and VND have no minor unit. The decimal count is resolved per currency rather than assumed to be two.

api.name: formatting
api.description: Reformatting under the caret is the classic money-input bug: you type `1`, it becomes `$1.00`, and the caret jumps behind the decimals.

api.name: type
api.description: A number input lets the scroll wheel change the amount, rejects grouping separators, and its spinners are meaningless for money.

api.name: min / max
api.description: Clamped on blur. Also in minor units.

signature-pad.label: Signature Pad
signature-pad.description: A canvas you sign with a finger, stylus or mouse. Strokes are kept as points and redrawn, so undo, resize and export all work — and stylus pressure varies the line.

api.name: value
api.description: Points, not pixels. Drawing straight to the canvas with no model makes undo impossible and loses the drawing on resize.

api.name: pointer events
api.description: Mouse, finger and pen through one path, with `pressure` from a stylus varying the width. `touch-action: none` is essential or the first stroke scrolls the page.

api.name: device pixel ratio
api.description: The backing store is scaled up and the context scaled down; a canvas sized in CSS pixels is visibly soft, and a signature is a thing people zoom into.

api.name: not a digital signature
api.description: Fine as a record that someone signed; proves nothing cryptographically. For non-repudiation, sign a hash of the document with a key.

api.name: onSign
api.description: Flattened image on demand, via `toBlob`.

transfer.label: Transfer
transfer.description: Two lists and the movement between them, for choosing a subset from a large pool. Both sides are searchable — filtering the target is what makes a 200-item selection usable.
transfer.usage:
import { Transfer } from '@/components/ui/transfer'

<Transfer items={items} value={selected} onChange={setSelected} />

api.name: items / value
api.description: { value, label, keywords?, disabled? }. `value` holds what is on the right.

api.name: vs MultiSelect
api.description: Past about a dozen, chips wrap into a wall you cannot scan, search or sort — and "did I already add Maria?" stops being answerable at a glance.

api.name: both sides searchable
api.description: Filtering the source is obvious. Filtering the target is what most implementations leave out.

api.name: selection
api.description: The rows are no longer where you left them, so keeping them ticked would be misleading.

api.name: titles
api.description: Headings for the two panels.

cascader.label: Cascader
cascader.description: A regular hierarchy picked one level at a time, in side-by-side columns — so the path stays readable and the siblings you passed are still visible.
cascader.usage:
import { Cascader } from '@/components/ui/cascader'

<Cascader options={regions} value={path} onChange={setPath} />

api.name: options / value
api.description: The value is the path from the root: `['eu', 'de', 'ber']`.

api.name: columns
api.description: For a real classification, columns show where you are and what the siblings were — which a tree of disclosure triangles hides as soon as it scrolls.

api.name: vs Tree
api.description: Use `Tree` when the shape is uneven, when several branches must be open at once, or when depth varies wildly. This is for regular hierarchies two to four levels deep.

api.name: changeOnSelect
api.description: The difference between "pick a city" and "pick anywhere, at any level".

api.name: expandOnHover
api.description: Browsing opens the next column without committing anything.

tree-select.label: Tree Select
tree-select.description: A tree in a popover with real tri-state parents. Checking a branch checks its subtree, the value holds only leaves, and searching keeps the ancestors of every match.
tree-select.usage:
import { TreeSelect } from '@/components/ui/tree-select'

<TreeSelect nodes={scopes} value={selected} onChange={setSelected} />

api.name: nodes / value
api.description: The value holds leaves only — a parent in the list would leave every consumer guessing whether it implies its children.

api.name: tri-state
api.description: A partly-chosen parent is neither checked nor unchecked. Rendering it as unchecked is a lie people act on: they tick it and silently replace a careful selection with everything.

api.name: indeterminate
api.description: Not an HTML attribute, so it cannot be expressed in JSX — it is set through a ref callback, with `aria-checked="mixed"` carrying the same fact.

api.name: search
api.description: A result with its path cut off is unplaceable: you cannot tell which "General" you found. Matching branches are force-opened.

api.name: summary
api.description: Summarises the selection on the trigger.

emoji-picker.label: Emoji Picker
emoji-picker.description: A grouped, searchable grid with recents, rendered as text rather than sprites. One tab stop with arrow-key movement, and it never touches localStorage.
emoji-picker.usage:
import { EmojiPicker } from '@/components/ui/emoji-picker'

<EmojiPicker recent={recent} onSelect={(emoji) => react(emoji.char)} />

api.name: emoji
api.description: A curated default is exported as `COMMON_EMOJI`. A full set with keywords is ~200 kB of JSON that needs updating every Unicode release; pass your own if you need it.

api.name: text, not sprites
api.description: Already installed, already right for the platform, scale as text, cost nothing to load. Sprite sheets buy identical rendering everywhere, at the cost of shipping and maintaining the sheet.

api.name: recent
api.description: Persisted by the caller. A picker that writes to localStorage itself cannot be server-rendered predictably and puts a key in a browser nobody chose.

api.name: roving tabindex
api.description: Arrow keys move within the grid, crossing group boundaries in reading order. Eight tab stops a row is unusable.

api.name: columns
api.description: Grid width. Also the arrow-key row size.

card.label: Card
card.description: A surface that groups related content. Header and footer are optional and draw their own dividers — a Card holding only a CardBody is just a padded box.
card.usage:
import {
  Card,
  CardHeader,
  CardTitle,
  CardDescription,
  CardBody,
  CardFooter,
} from '@/components/ui/card'

<Card>
  <CardHeader>
    <CardTitle>Deployment</CardTitle>
    <CardDescription>Last run 4 minutes ago.</CardDescription>
  </CardHeader>
  <CardBody>Build 1482 finished on main.</CardBody>
  <CardFooter>
    <Button size="sm">Re-run</Button>
  </CardFooter>
</Card>

api.name: variant
api.description: Bordered surface, filled, or outline with no fill.

api.name: size
api.description: Section padding. Reaches header, body and footer through context, so one prop re-pads the whole card.

api.name: CardHeader / CardFooter
api.description: Optional. Each draws its own divider, so omitting them leaves no stray rule.

api.name: CardBody
api.description: Grows to fill. The only section a Card needs.

api.name: CardTitle / CardDescription
api.description: Heading and secondary line, normally inside CardHeader.

api.name: CardHeader / CardBody / CardFooter size
api.description: Overrides the inherited padding for one section.

demos.title: Full composition
demos.code:
<Card>
  <CardHeader>
    <CardTitle>Deployment</CardTitle>
    <CardDescription>Last run 4 minutes ago.</CardDescription>
  </CardHeader>
  <CardBody>Build 1482 finished on main.</CardBody>
  <CardFooter>
    <Button size="sm">Re-run</Button>
  </CardFooter>
</Card>

group.label: Group
group.description: A recessed container that holds a set of cards. Padding and gap are the same value, and the corner radius is concentric with the cards inside it.
group.usage:
import { Group } from '@/components/ui/group'
import { Card, CardBody } from '@/components/ui/card'

<Group>
  <Card><CardBody>Notifications</CardBody></Card>
  <Card><CardBody>Appearance</CardBody></Card>
</Group>

api.name: responsive
api.description: Breakpoint a horizontal group becomes a row at. Below it the cards stack, so a row of three never squeezes into thirds of a phone screen. `false` keeps it a row at every width.

api.name: orientation
api.description: Stack the cards or lay them in a row. Horizontal wraps.

api.name: size
api.description: Padding and gap together — 12, 18 or 24px. Each size also picks the matching concentric radius.

api.name: even
api.description: Give every child an equal share of the main axis. Mostly for horizontal groups.

api.name: radius
api.description: Card radius plus the group padding, so the gap between the two curves stays even into the corners. Tunable in index.css.

code-block.label: Code Block
code-block.description: Syntax-highlighted source with an optional title or file path, copy, inline editing, line numbers and collapsing.
code-block.usage:
import { CodeBlock } from '@/components/ui/code-block'

<CodeBlock
  filePath="src/components/ui/button.tsx"
  language="tsx"
  lineNumbers
  code={source}
/>

api.name: footer
api.description: A control bar under the code — a Run button, a language switch, a status line. Rendered below the expand row, so "show more" stays attached to the code it expands.

api.name: code
api.description: The source to render. Acts as the initial value when editable.

api.name: language
api.description: Grammar to highlight with. Each one loads as its own chunk.

api.name: title
api.description: Free-form header label. Falls back to the language name.

api.name: filePath
api.description: A path in the same header slot as title, with the directory muted and the file emphasized.

api.name: showLanguage
api.description: Language chip on the right. On whenever the header has a label.

api.name: copyable
api.description: Copy button, showing a checkmark for 1.5s.

api.name: editable
api.description: Type into the block; highlighting follows every keystroke via a transparent overlay.

api.name: onCodeChange
api.description: Fires on every edit.

api.name: resettable
api.description: Revert button, shown only once the code differs from the prop.

api.name: lineNumbers
api.description: Counter gutter down the left edge.

api.name: wrap
api.description: Soft-wrap long lines instead of scrolling horizontally.

api.name: highlightLines
api.description: 1-based lines to emphasize with an accent background and ring bar.

api.name: maxLines
api.description: Collapse past this many lines behind an animated Show more toggle.

api.name: header
api.description: Force the header on or off. On whenever it would hold anything.

demos.title: Footer controls
demos.code: Ready } />

badge.label: Badge
badge.description: A short status or category marker. Unlike a field, a badge exists to be noticed, so it keeps the full colour system and the tint escape hatch.

api.name: variant
api.description: Solid, tinted, outline or text-only. All read the active colour set. Choosing one: secondary for almost everything — it is the tinted default and stays legible on any surface; default (solid) only where a badge must be the loudest thing in view; outline when the badge sits on an already-tinted fill and another tint would compete; ghost for a count that should recede.

api.name: color
api.description: Named colour set, shared with Button.

api.name: tint
api.description: Any CSS colour, used instead of a named set.

api.name: size
api.description: Height, padding and text size.

api.name: shape
api.description: A true pill, or the squircle used elsewhere in the kit.

api.name: icon
api.description: Rendered inside the badge. Sized automatically from the badge size — 12px at sm and default, 14px at lg.

api.name: iconPosition
api.description: Which side the icon sits on. Ignored with asChild, where the caller owns the children.

api.name: asChild
api.description: Render the child element instead of a <span> — for a badge that is also a link.

demos.title: With an icon
demos.code:

<Badge icon={<X />} iconPosition="end" color="destructive">Failed</Badge>
<Badge icon={<GitBranch />} variant="outline">main</Badge>

avatar.label: Avatar
avatar.description: An image standing in for a person, with a fallback that always renders. Initials are derived from the name, and a broken image falls through to them.
avatar.usage:
import { Avatar } from '@/components/ui/avatar'

<Avatar src={user.photo} name="Ada Lovelace" />

api.name: AvatarBadge position
api.description: Corner to pin to. The short forms `tr`, `tl`, `br` and `bl` are accepted too.

api.name: AvatarBadge tone
api.description: Presence colour, or a filled chip when the badge carries content.

api.name: AvatarBadge ring
api.description: Ring in the surface colour. Not decoration — a dot the same colour as what sits behind it disappears.

api.name: AvatarBadge label
api.description: Accessible name. Without one a bare status dot is announced as nothing, so it is marked aria-hidden instead.

api.name: AvatarWithBadge
api.description: The positioning wrapper. Avatar clips its own overflow to round the image, so a badge inside it would be cut off at exactly the corner it sits on.

api.name: src
api.description: Image URL. On a load error the component falls back to initials instead of showing a broken image.

api.name: name
api.description: Alt text, and the source of the derived initials. "Ada Lovelace" becomes "AL".

api.name: fallback
api.description: Overrides the derived initials.

api.name: size
api.description: Footprint, with the initials scaled to match.

api.name: shape
api.description: Circle, or the kit squircle.

api.name: AvatarGroup max
api.description: Show this many, then a +N chip for the rest.

table.label: Table
table.description: Rows and columns of structured data. The wrapper scrolls rather than the page, so a wide table never forces horizontal scroll on the whole document.
table.usage: import { Table, TableHeader, TableBody, TableRow, TableHead, TableCell } from '@/components/ui/table' Invoice INV-001

api.name: Table containerClassName
api.description: Styles the scrolling wrapper; className styles the <table> itself.

api.name: TableRow data-state
api.description: Marks a row as selected, which tints its background.

api.name: TableHeader / TableBody / TableFooter
api.description: Map to thead, tbody and tfoot. The footer is tinted and divided.

api.name: TableCaption
api.description: Rendered below the table, per caption-side.

data-grid.label: Data Grid
data-grid.description: Sorting and selection over Table, driven by a column definition. The sort is stable and never mutates your array, so re-sorting on an equal column leaves settled rows where they were.
data-grid.usage:
import { DataGrid, type DataGridColumn } from '@/components/ui/data-grid'

const columns: DataGridColumn<Row>[] = [
  { key: 'id', header: '#', sortable: true },
  { key: 'status', header: 'Status', render: (row) => <Badge>{row.status}</Badge> },
]

<DataGrid columns={columns} rows={rows} rowKey={(row) => row.id} selectable />

api.name: columns
api.description: `{ key, header, render?, sortValue?, sortable?, align?, hideOnMobile?, width? }`.

api.name: rowKey
api.description: Stable identity, used for React keys and for selection.

api.name: selectable / selected / onSelectedChange
api.description: Header checkbox selects the page and goes indeterminate on a partial selection.

api.name: defaultSort
api.description: Initial sort. Clicking a header cycles ascending, descending, off.

api.name: sortValue
api.description: For anything not directly comparable — a formatted date, a status rank.

api.name: hideOnMobile
api.description: Drops the column below `sm` instead of letting the table scroll sideways for a nice-to-have field.

stat.label: Stat
stat.description: One measurement: label, value and how it moved. Which direction counts as healthy is a prop, because a rise in incidents is not a rise in deployments.
stat.usage:
import { Stat } from '@/components/ui/stat'

<Stat label="Deployments" value={1482} delta={12.4} />
<Stat label="Open incidents" value={3} delta={2} goodDirection="down" />

api.name: label / value
api.description: What is measured, and the measurement.

api.name: delta
api.description: Signed change. The sign picks the arrow; the absolute value is printed, since the arrow already carries direction.

api.name: goodDirection
api.description: Which way is healthy. Colours the delta green or red accordingly; `none` keeps it neutral.

api.name: deltaSuffix
api.description: Unit printed after the delta.

api.name: chart
api.description: Usually a Sparkline, rendered under the value.

api.name: size
api.description: Scales the value type and the card padding together.

api.name: bordered
api.description: Draw the card. Turn off inside a container that already provides one.

api.name: animate
api.description: Count to the value on mount and on every change. Only applies when `value` is a number — a preformatted string has nothing to count through.

sparkline.label: Sparkline
sparkline.description: A microchart with no axes, legend or dependency — plain SVG over a normalised range, sized by whatever box you put it in.

api.name: values
api.description: The series. A single value renders one centred point; a flat series is centred rather than dividing by a zero range.

api.name: variant
api.description: Stroke, filled stroke, or discrete columns.

api.name: color
api.description: Any CSS colour. Inherits the surrounding text colour by default, so it themes for free.

api.name: baseline
api.description: Floor for the fill and bars. Defaults to the lowest value in the series.

api.name: strokeWidth
api.description: Kept even under the horizontal stretch by non-scaling-stroke.

chart.label: Chart
chart.description: A small line, area or bar plot in plain SVG. Not a charting library — everything here is a scale and a path, which is the right trade for six numbers on a dashboard card.
chart.usage:
import { Chart } from '@/components/ui/chart'

<Chart series={series} labels={months} variant="area" />

api.name: series
api.description: `{ name, values, color? }`. Colours fall back to a palette by index.

api.name: variant
api.description: Bars group per index across series.

api.name: labels
api.description: X labels, rendered below the plot rather than inside the stretched SVG.

api.name: min / max
api.description: Pin the scale. Defaults span zero to the highest value, so bar heights stay honest.

api.name: grid / axis / legend
api.description: Legend defaults on for more than one series.

api.name: scaling
api.description: Stretched by preserveAspectRatio:none so it fills its container without measuring; strokes use non-scaling-stroke to stay even under that stretch.

gauge.label: Gauge
gauge.description: A radial meter — the circular counterpart to Progress. Drawn with stroke-dasharray rather than an arc path, so the sweep is one number and there is no arc-flag maths to get wrong.

api.name: value / max
api.description: Reported as a real progressbar with aria-valuenow — a ring of SVG is otherwise invisible to a screen reader.

api.name: size / thickness
api.description: Rendered size in pixels; geometry is a fixed 100-unit viewBox so it stays independent of that.

api.name: tone
api.description: Any CSS colour. Defaults to a threshold ramp — green, amber above 75%, red above 90%.

api.name: label / hint / showValue
api.description: Caption under the ring, small text inside it, and whether the percentage is drawn.

demos.title: Thresholds
demos.code:
<Gauge value={38} label="Memory" />
<Gauge value={82} label="Disk" />
<Gauge value={96} label="Quota" />

donut.label: Donut
donut.description: Parts against a whole. Arcs are stroke-dasharray on a circle rather than wedge paths — one number per slice, and no arc-flag branch at the halfway point.
donut.usage:
import { Donut } from '@/components/ui/donut'

<Donut slices={slices} centerValue="748 kB" centerLabel="bundle" />

api.name: slices
api.description: `{ label, value, color? }`. Percentages are computed from the total.

api.name: thickness
api.description: 0 renders a pie rather than a donut.

api.name: minSlice
api.description: Anything smaller folds into "Other" — fourteen one-percent wedges communicate less than five and a remainder.

api.name: accessibility
api.description: Lists every slice with its share. A ring with "62%" in the middle tells a screen reader nothing about the other 38.

funnel.label: Funnel
funnel.description: Conversion through ordered stages, with both the overall rate and the step rate. A funnel showing only the overall rate hides which single step is losing people.

api.name: stages
api.description: `{ label, value, hint? }`, in order.

api.name: showStepRate
api.description: Adds the rate against the previous stage and how many dropped.

api.name: bar width
api.description: Proportional to the count, not the step rate — a stage keeping 90% of a tiny cohort should not look wider than one keeping 40% of everyone.

heatmap-grid.label: Heatmap Grid
heatmap-grid.description: A calendar heatmap — weeks as columns, weekdays as rows. UptimeStrip is the one-dimensional case; this is the grid.

api.name: cells
api.description: `{ date, value, detail? }`. Gaps are filled with zero-value days so the grid stays continuous.

api.name: levels
api.description: Intensity buckets. A smooth gradient makes neighbouring 11px squares look identical.

api.name: week alignment
api.description: Padded to a week boundary at both ends; without that the first column starts on the wrong weekday and every row is shifted a day.

typography.label: Typography
typography.description: Prose styling for content you did not author element by element — rendered markdown, a CMS body, a changelog. Headings start at h2, since the page already has its h1.

api.name: size
api.description: Base text size; the scale within the block is relative.

api.name: rhythm
api.description: Spacing comes from `* + *` rules rather than a margin on every element, which is why prose blocks usually have too much space after headings and too little between list items.

api.name: headings
api.description: A prose block is page content; shipping its own h1 gives the document two.

api.name: PROSE
api.description: The class string, exported for applying to an element you already control.

kanban.label: Kanban
kanban.description: Columns of cards, movable between them. Drag-and-drop is pointer-only, so every card also moves with the arrow keys — a board you can only drag excludes keyboard users from its main action.

api.name: columns
api.description: `{ id, title, cards, limit? }` where a card is `{ id, title, meta?, accent? }`.

api.name: onMove
api.description: The board never reorders anything itself — moving optimistically and having the server reject it is worse than a moment of latency.

api.name: keyboard
api.description: Moves a focused card between columns.

api.name: renderCard
api.description: Replace the card body while keeping the drag behaviour.

description-list.label: Description List
description-list.description: Key/value metadata as a real <dl>, so a screen reader announces each term with its value. Columns on wide screens, stacked on narrow ones.

api.name: columns
api.description: Term beside value from `sm` up. At phone width a split leaves both halves too narrow, so it stacks below that regardless.

api.name: divided
api.description: Hairline between pairs.

api.name: DescriptionPairs
api.description: Convenience wrapper taking `items={[{ term, details }]}` for a flat list.

fmt.label: Fmt
fmt.description: One component for every formatted value — dates, numbers, currency, bytes, durations, relative times — so the locale is a single decision rather than three developers reaching for toLocaleString, toFixed and padStart on one screen.
fmt.usage:
import { Fmt } from '@/components/ui/fmt'

<Fmt type="date" value={date} format="DD.MM.YYYY HH:mm" />
<Fmt type="currency" value={1234.5} currency="EUR" />
<Fmt type="number" value={1234567.891} decimals={2} />
<Fmt type="bytes" value={748100} />

api.name: type
api.description: What the value is.

api.name: format (date)
api.description: A pattern like 'DD.MM.YYYY HH:mm', or one of short/medium/long/full. Tokens follow moment/dayjs: MM is the month, mm is the minute — 'HH:MM:SS' prints the month where you wanted minutes.

api.name: format (currency)
api.description: Maps to Intl currencyDisplay.

api.name: currency / decimals / grouping
api.description: ISO 4217 code, fraction digits, thousands separators.

api.name: now
api.description: Reference point for relative times. Pass it to keep a render deterministic.

api.name: animate
api.description: Count to the value instead of printing it. Off by default — a column of forty figures counting at once is noise. Turn it on where the number is the content: a headline, a total, a figure that moves while you watch. Ignored for dates and relative times.

api.name: output element
api.description: Dates and relative times render a <time> with an ISO dateTime, so the machine-readable value travels with the display one. Everything else is a span with tabular figures.

api.name: helpers
api.description: Exported for use outside JSX.

demos.title: Every type
demos.code:
<Fmt type="date" value={d} format="DD.MM.YYYY HH:mm:ss" />
<Fmt type="date" value={d} format="MMMM D, YYYY" />
<Fmt type="number" value={1234567.891} decimals={2} />
<Fmt type="currency" value={1234.5} currency="EUR" />
<Fmt type="percent" value={0.982} decimals={1} />
<Fmt type="bytes" value={748100} />
<Fmt type="duration" value={3792} />
<Fmt type="relative" value={twoHoursAgo} />

separator.label: Separator
separator.description: A rule between sections, horizontal or vertical, optionally with a label set into it.

api.name: orientation
api.description: Direction of the rule. Vertical stretches to its container.

api.name: label
api.description: Text set into the rule, e.g. "or". Horizontal only.

api.name: decorative
api.description: Hidden from assistive tech, which is right for a purely visual rule. Set false when it separates genuinely distinct regions.

skeleton.label: Skeleton
skeleton.description: A placeholder shape for content that has not arrived. The pulse animates opacity only, so it stays inside the kit motion rule, and stops under prefers-reduced-motion.
skeleton.usage:
import { Skeleton } from '@/components/ui/skeleton'

<Skeleton className="h-8 w-40" />
<Skeleton shape="text" lines={3} />

api.name: shape
api.description: Corner treatment: control radius, a text line, or a circle.

api.name: lines
api.description: Render this many stacked lines. The last one is short, so it reads as a paragraph rather than a block.

api.name: className
api.description: Where the size comes from — a skeleton has no intrinsic dimensions.

demos.title: Shapes
demos.code:
<Skeleton className="h-8 w-48" />
<Skeleton shape="text" className="w-64" />
<Skeleton shape="circle" className="size-10" />

aspect-ratio.label: Aspect Ratio
aspect-ratio.description: Hold a box at a fixed ratio while its width is fluid. Modern CSS aspect-ratio, so no padding-top hack.
aspect-ratio.usage: import { AspectRatio } from '@/components/ui/aspect-ratio'

api.name: ratio
api.description: Width divided by height.

kbd.label: Kbd
kbd.description: A keyboard key. Splits on "+" so a chord can be written as one string.

api.name: keys
api.description: Chord written as one string, split on "+".

api.name: children
api.description: Used instead of `keys` when you want full control.

calendar.label: Calendar
calendar.description: A date grid in single or range mode, with presets, times, dropdown captions and multiple months. No date library — the grid, weekday names and times all come from Intl.

api.name: mode
api.description: Range mode drafts the selection: the first click anchors, the pointer paints a preview, the second click or the end of a drag commits.

api.name: selected / defaultSelected
api.description: Controlled and uncontrolled. Clicking the selected day in single mode clears it.

api.name: onSelect
api.description: A Date in single mode, a DateRange in range mode. Can be called with undefined when cleared.

api.name: presets
api.description: Quick ranges beside the grid. Range mode only. `defaultPresets()` gives today, last 7, last 30, this and last month.

api.name: numberOfMonths
api.description: Months side by side, each with its own caption.

api.name: month / defaultMonth / onMonthChange
api.description: The visible month, controlled or not.

api.name: captionLayout
api.description: A static heading, or month and year selects for jumping years at a time.

api.name: showTime / timeStep
api.description: Adds hour and minute selects. Picking a new day keeps the time already chosen.

api.name: fromDate / toDate
api.description: Bounds. Days outside them are disabled, and the arrows stop at the edge.

api.name: disabled
api.description: Arbitrary per-day rule — weekends, holidays, booked dates.

api.name: weekStartsOn
api.description: Any weekday, not just Sunday or Monday.

api.name: renderDay / footer
api.description: Custom day content (cells grow to fit) and an arbitrary footer.

demos.title: Range with presets and two months

carousel.label: Carousel
carousel.description: A horizontally scrolling row of slides, built on CSS scroll-snap rather than a transform track — so touch swiping, momentum and keyboard scrolling all keep working.

api.name: children
api.description: One node per slide. The count drives the dots and the snap maths.

api.name: slidesToShow
api.description: How many slides fit at once. Widths are computed from this and the gap.

api.name: gap
api.description: Space between slides, in px.

api.name: showControls / showDots
api.description: Arrows and position dots below the track.

empty.label: Empty
empty.description: The state a list is in before it has anything in it. An icon, a reason and a next action are what make the empty case useful rather than merely honest.
empty.usage:
import { Empty } from '@/components/ui/empty'

<Empty
  icon={<Folder />}
  title="No projects yet"
  description="Create your first project to get started."
  action={<Button size="sm">New project</Button>}
/>

api.name: icon / title / description
api.description: The three parts of a useful empty state.

api.name: action
api.description: The next step — usually the button that creates the missing thing.

api.name: bordered
api.description: Dashed outline. Turn it off inside a card that already has one.

demos.title: Search with no results
demos.code: <Empty icon={<Search />} title="No matches" description="Try a different term." />

tabs.label: Tabs
tabs.description: Switch between panels in the same context. Full WAI-ARIA keyboard support: arrows rove, Home and End jump, and only the active tab is in the tab order.
tabs.usage:
import { Tabs, TabsList, TabsTrigger, TabsContent } from '@/components/ui/tabs'

<Tabs defaultValue="overview">
  <TabsList>
    <TabsTrigger value="overview">Overview</TabsTrigger>
    <TabsTrigger value="activity">Activity</TabsTrigger>
  </TabsList>
  <TabsContent value="overview">…</TabsContent>
  <TabsContent value="activity">…</TabsContent>
</Tabs>

api.name: value / defaultValue
api.description: Controlled and uncontrolled selection, on Tabs.

api.name: onValueChange
api.description: Fires with the newly selected tab.

api.name: orientation
api.description: Layout direction, and which arrow keys move between tabs.

api.name: activationMode
api.description: Automatic selects as focus moves; manual waits for Enter or Space.

api.name: variant
api.description: Set it once on Tabs and the list, the triggers and the panel all follow. Setting it on a child still wins, which is how it was written before the root took the prop.

api.name: browser
api.description: The connected look: the active tab and the panel are one fill with nothing drawn between them, and two masked flares carve the strip away at the bottom corners. No borders anywhere — a bordered version has to hide one border with another and comes apart at every zoom level.

api.name: transition
api.description: The panel cross-fades on switch and does not move. Travel on a panel root means a transform, and a transform is a containing block for any fixed layer inside it — a popover opened from a tab would land in the wrong place. The tab shape morphs instead, flares included.

api.name: TabsTrigger value
api.description: Required. Matches the TabsContent it controls.

demos.title: A tab group
demos.code:
<Tabs defaultValue="dashboard" variant="browser">
  <TabsList className="items-end">
    <GroupChip>Work</GroupChip>
    <TabsTrigger value="dashboard">Dashboard</TabsTrigger>
    <TabsTrigger value="issues">Issues · 12</TabsTrigger>
    <TabsTrigger value="docs">Docs</TabsTrigger>
  </TabsList>
  <TabsContent value="dashboard">…</TabsContent>
</Tabs>

accordion.label: Accordion
accordion.description: A stack of collapsible sections. Each header is a real button inside a heading, which is what makes the set navigable by heading in a screen reader.
accordion.usage:
import { Accordion, AccordionItem, AccordionTrigger, AccordionContent } from '@/components/ui/accordion'

<Accordion type="single" defaultValue={['what']}>
  <AccordionItem value="what">
    <AccordionTrigger>What is in the kit?</AccordionTrigger>
    <AccordionContent>…</AccordionContent>
  </AccordionItem>
</Accordion>

api.name: type
api.description: Whether opening a section closes the previous one.

api.name: collapsible
api.description: With type="single", whether the open section can be closed again.

api.name: value / defaultValue
api.description: Open sections. An array in both modes, so switching type needs no change.

api.name: onValueChange
api.description: Fires with the new set of open sections.

api.name: AccordionItem value
api.description: Required. Identifies the section.

collapsible.label: Collapsible
collapsible.description: A single panel that expands and collapses. The open height is measured rather than assumed, because height: auto cannot be transitioned.
collapsible.usage:
import { Collapsible, CollapsibleTrigger, CollapsibleContent } from '@/components/ui/collapsible'

<Collapsible>
  <CollapsibleTrigger>Advanced options</CollapsibleTrigger>
  <CollapsibleContent>…</CollapsibleContent>
</Collapsible>

api.name: open / defaultOpen
api.description: Controlled and uncontrolled state.

api.name: onOpenChange
api.description: Fires on every change.

api.name: CollapsibleTrigger showChevron
api.description: Rotating chevron on the trailing edge.

api.name: CollapsibleTrigger asChild
api.description: Use your own element as the trigger. Suppresses the chevron.

breadcrumb.label: Breadcrumb
breadcrumb.description: The trail back up the hierarchy. An ordered list in a labelled nav, with the current page marked aria-current and deliberately not linked.
breadcrumb.usage:
import {
  Breadcrumb,
  BreadcrumbList,
  BreadcrumbItem,
  BreadcrumbLink,
  BreadcrumbSeparator,
  BreadcrumbPage,
} from '@/components/ui/breadcrumb'

<Breadcrumb>
  <BreadcrumbList>
    <BreadcrumbItem>
      <BreadcrumbLink href="/">Home</BreadcrumbLink>
    </BreadcrumbItem>
    <BreadcrumbSeparator />
    <BreadcrumbItem>
      <BreadcrumbPage>Breadcrumb</BreadcrumbPage>
    </BreadcrumbItem>
  </BreadcrumbList>
</Breadcrumb>

api.name: Breadcrumb
api.description: Labelled landmark wrapping the trail.

api.name: BreadcrumbList
api.description: Ordered, because the sequence carries meaning.

api.name: BreadcrumbLink
api.description: A navigable ancestor. Accepts any anchor props, including asChild-style routing via a custom element.

api.name: BreadcrumbPage
api.description: The current page: aria-current="page" and not a link, since linking to where you already are is noise.

api.name: BreadcrumbSeparator
api.description: Presentational and aria-hidden. Defaults to a chevron; pass children to replace it.

api.name: BreadcrumbEllipsis
api.description: Stands in for collapsed middle segments.

stepper.label: Stepper
stepper.description: Progress through a fixed sequence. One `current` index drives the common case; any step can override its own status for a failure or a skip in the middle.

api.name: steps
api.description: `{ id, label, description?, status?, icon? }`. A `status` overrides what `current` would imply.

api.name: current
api.description: Index of the active step. Everything before it reads as complete.

api.name: orientation
api.description: Axis.

api.name: responsive
api.description: Breakpoint a horizontal stepper becomes a row at. Below it the stages stack — four labelled stages across a phone gives each about seventy pixels.

api.name: status
api.description: Per-step override. Active shows a spinner, complete a tick, failed a cross, skipped a struck-through label.

timeline.label: Timeline
timeline.description: A vertical run of events sharing one rail — deploys, incidents, review activity, an agent run. The connector stops at the last item instead of dangling past it.
timeline.usage:
import { Timeline, TimelineItem } from '@/components/ui/timeline'

<Timeline>
  <TimelineItem title="Deployed to production" time="2m ago" tone="success" />
  <TimelineItem title="Checks passed" time="6m ago" tone="info" />
</Timeline>

api.name: TimelineItem title
api.description: The event. Required — an item with only a body has nothing to scan.

api.name: TimelineItem time
api.description: Right-aligned from `sm` up, and under the title on narrow screens.

api.name: TimelineItem tone
api.description: Marker colour.

api.name: TimelineItem pending
api.description: Draw the marker as an outline, for an event that has not happened yet.

api.name: TimelineItem icon
api.description: Replaces the default dot.

api.name: TimelineContent
api.description: A framed body under an event — a log excerpt, a diff, a message.

demos.title: Deploy history
demos.code:
<Timeline>
  <TimelineItem title="Deployed to production" time="2m ago" tone="success" icon={<Rocket />}>
    <TimelineContent>astralyx-ui@1.4.2 · 42s</TimelineContent>
  </TimelineItem>
  <TimelineItem title="Build passed" time="4m ago" tone="info" icon={<Package />} />
  <TimelineItem title="Queued" time="5m ago" tone="muted" pending />
</Timeline>

toolbar.label: Toolbar
toolbar.description: A group of controls that arrow keys move between — the ARIA role ButtonGroup deliberately does not claim, because claiming it without implementing it is worse than not claiming it.
toolbar.usage:
import { Toolbar, ToolbarSeparator } from '@/components/ui/toolbar'

<Toolbar>
  <Toggle size="sm"><Bold /></Toggle>
  <ToolbarSeparator />
  <Toggle size="sm"><List /></Toggle>
</Toolbar>

api.name: orientation
api.description: Decides which arrow keys move focus and sets aria-orientation.

api.name: focus
api.description: Recomputed on each key rather than cached on mount — toolbars gain and lose buttons as selection changes.

api.name: ToolbarSeparator
api.description: A hairline between groups, with the right role and orientation.

menubar.label: Menubar
menubar.description: An application menu bar. What makes it a menu bar rather than a row of dropdowns: once one menu is open, moving along the bar opens the next instead of merely focusing it.

api.name: menus
api.description: `{ id, label, items }` where an item is `{ id, label, shortcut?, disabled?, separatorBefore?, onSelect? }`.

api.name: keyboard
api.description: Left and Right belong to the bar, Up and Down to the open menu. The bar is one tab stop.

api.name: hover
api.description: Only while a menu is already open — hovering a closed bar does nothing.

navigation-menu.label: Navigation Menu
navigation-menu.description: A site nav bar with mega-menu panels and hover intent — a short open delay so crossing the bar does not flash panels, and a longer close delay so the panel is reachable.

api.name: entries
api.description: `{ id, label, href?, content? }` — content makes it a panel trigger, href a plain link.

api.name: openDelay / closeDelay
api.description: Once any panel is open, switching between triggers is immediate: the delay only decides whether you meant to open at all.

api.name: NavigationMenuSection / NavigationMenuLink
api.description: A titled column, and a title-plus-description link inside a panel.

table-of-contents.label: Table of Contents
table-of-contents.description: An anchor list that tracks which heading is on screen, through IntersectionObserver rather than scroll offsets. Reads the DOM by default, so it works for rendered markdown.
table-of-contents.usage:
import { TableOfContents } from '@/components/ui/table-of-contents'

<TableOfContents selector="h2, h3" container="#doc" />

api.name: items
api.description: Supply headings directly, or omit and let it read the DOM.

api.name: selector / container
api.description: What to collect and where. Headings need ids.

api.name: scroll-spy
api.description: The rootMargin pulls the detection band to the top quarter of the viewport — without it the highlight sits one or two headings ahead of what you are reading.

api.name: useHeadings
api.description: Exported, for building your own list.

virtual-list.label: Virtual List
virtual-list.description: Renders only the rows in view. DataGrid and LogViewer both render every row they are given, which is fine until a few thousand and then stalls the main thread.

api.name: items / rowHeight
api.description: Fixed height by design: variable heights need measurement, a cache and a scroll correction pass, and wrong estimates make the scrollbar jump under the pointer.

api.name: renderItem
api.description: The index is the real one in the full list, not the slice.

api.name: overscan
api.description: Rows rendered beyond the viewport so a fast scroll does not expose blank space.

api.name: onEndReached
api.description: Infinite scrolling. Guarded by item count, so it fires once per batch rather than on every scroll event near the bottom.

tree.label: Tree
tree.description: A collapsible hierarchy with real keyboard navigation — arrow keys move by what is visible, one tab stop for the whole tree, and ARIA that says where each row sits in its branch.

api.name: nodes
api.description: Recursive: `{ id, label, icon?, meta?, children?, disabled? }`.

api.name: expanded / defaultExpanded / onExpandedChange
api.description: Controlled or uncontrolled expansion, by node id.

api.name: selected / onSelect
api.description: Selection. Clicking a branch toggles it; clicking a leaf selects it.

api.name: keyboard
api.description: Up and down move over visible rows. Right opens a branch then steps into it; Left closes it, then climbs to the parent.

api.name: guides
api.description: Indent guides.

pagination.label: Pagination
pagination.description: Move between pages of results. The windowing rule — how many neighbours to show and where the gaps fall — is exported as pageItems, so it can be reused or tested on its own.

api.name: page
api.description: Current page, 1-based. Controlled — the component holds no state.

api.name: count
api.description: Total number of pages.

api.name: onPageChange
api.description: Fires with the requested page. Out-of-range requests are filtered out first.

api.name: siblings
api.description: Neighbours shown either side of the current page. First and last are always present.

api.name: size
api.description: Button size for the controls.

api.name: compact
api.description: Drop the numbers and show "page / count" between the arrows.

api.name: pageItems
api.description: The exported windowing function behind the row.

sidebar.label: Sidebar
sidebar.description: Two sidebars from one set of parts: the app frame, a transparent rail beside a rounded content panel, and a static nav that lives inside a page. Either can be pinned to the left or the right, two can share one frame, and a rail collapses to icons or to nothing at all.
sidebar.usage:
import {
  Sidebar, SidebarContent, SidebarGroup, SidebarGroupLabel,
  SidebarHeader, SidebarInset, SidebarMenu, SidebarMenuButton,
  SidebarMenuItem, SidebarProvider, SidebarTrigger,
} from '@/components/ui/sidebar'

<SidebarProvider>
  <Sidebar>
    <SidebarHeader>…</SidebarHeader>
    <SidebarContent>
      <SidebarGroup>
        <SidebarGroupLabel>Workspace</SidebarGroupLabel>
        <SidebarMenu>
          <SidebarMenuItem>
            <SidebarMenuButton icon={<Home />} isActive>Home</SidebarMenuButton>
          </SidebarMenuItem>
        </SidebarMenu>
      </SidebarGroup>
    </SidebarContent>
  </Sidebar>

  <SidebarInset>
    <SidebarTrigger />
    …
  </SidebarInset>
</SidebarProvider>

api.name: SidebarProvider variant
api.description: `app` is the product frame that owns the window, collapses to a rail and paints its own fixed ground. `page` is navigation inside a page — a settings nav, a docs section — which never collapses, has no trigger and no shortcut, takes its height from whatever contains it, and is painted in the page theme. One prop rather than three booleans, because they are not independent: a sidebar that does not own the window has nothing to collapse into and no ground of its own to paint.

api.name: Sidebar position
api.description: Which edge to pin to. Two sidebars can share one provider — navigation on the left, an inspector on the right — and they open independently. The order is set from the prop, not from the markup, so a right sidebar written before the content still lands after it.

api.name: Sidebar collapsedTo
api.description: What is left when it collapses. `icon` keeps the 52px rail, which is right for navigation: every destination stays one click away and the layout never reflows. `nothing` gives the width back, which is right for a detail panel — an inspector nobody is reading should not cost a strip of the window. Hidden rather than unmounted, so the trigger’s `aria-controls` keeps resolving.

api.name: SidebarTrigger position / label
api.description: Which panel the button toggles, and what to call it. Two triggers in one header both announcing “Expand sidebar” is a coin toss for anyone who cannot see which is which, so `label` names the panel instead.

api.name: SidebarProvider open / defaultOpen / onOpenChange
api.description: Controlled or uncontrolled rail state. A boolean sets both sides; an object like `{ left: true, right: false }` sets the ones it names, and a side the caller does not name keeps looking after itself. `onOpenChange` is told which side moved. Below the md breakpoint both rails are pinned collapsed and these are ignored — at 36px it is already the mobile layout, so there is nothing to overlay.

api.name: SidebarMenuButton icon
api.description: Leading icon, sized to 16px by the row. It stays on the rail centre line in both states, so nothing shifts sideways as the label appears.

api.name: SidebarMenuButton isActive
api.description: Marks the current page. Fills the row with the secondary surface.

api.name: SidebarMenuButton asChild
api.description: Render a router link instead of a button, keeping the row styling.

api.name: SidebarMenuButton tooltip
api.description: Shown on hover while collapsed. Defaults to the row label. The label itself becomes sr-only rather than unmounting, so the accessible name survives the collapse.

api.name: useSidebar()
api.description: Rail state for custom chrome. `locked` is true below md, where SidebarTrigger renders nothing.

api.name: grid
api.description: Gutter, collapsed rail and expanded width. The rail is a 36px control unit plus the same 8px gutter either side — that gutter is load-bearing, since the scrolling content clips a row focus ring at its padding box. The 10px row inset is (36 − 16) / 2, which holds the icon on the rail centre line in both states.

api.name: shortcut
api.description: Toggles the rail while the frame is mounted and the viewport is at least md.

demos.title: One on each side
Inside a page, static
demos.code:
// Navigation within a page — a settings nav, a docs section, a wizard.
// Never collapses, so there is no trigger and no Cmd-B, and the rows are
// painted in the page theme rather than on the rail's fixed black.
<SidebarProvider variant="page">
  <Sidebar>
    <SidebarContent className="px-0">
      <SidebarGroup>
        <SidebarGroupLabel>Account</SidebarGroupLabel>
        <SidebarMenu>…</SidebarMenu>
      </SidebarGroup>
    </SidebarContent>
  </Sidebar>
  <SidebarInset>…</SidebarInset>
</SidebarProvider>

scroll-area.label: Scroll Area
scroll-area.description: A scrollable region with a themed scrollbar, styled through the standard scrollbar properties rather than a JavaScript overlay — so native momentum and keyboard scrolling stay intact.

api.name: orientation
api.description: Which axis scrolls.

api.name: className
api.description: Where the height comes from — a scroll area needs a bounded size to scroll at all.

resizable.label: Resizable
resizable.description: Two panels with a draggable divider. Sizes are percentages, so the split survives a container resize — and the handle is a real slider, so arrow keys resize it too.
resizable.usage:
import { Resizable } from '@/components/ui/resizable'

<Resizable defaultSize={40} minSize={20} maxSize={80}>
  <aside>…</aside>
  <main>…</main>
</Resizable>

api.name: responsive
api.description: Breakpoint below which the panels stack, since two columns on a phone leave each about 180px. Unlike the other responsive components this is a real orientation change rather than a CSS one — the pointer maths, the arrow keys and the ARIA orientation all depend on which axis is being dragged.

api.name: orientation
api.description: Which way the panels split.

api.name: defaultSize
api.description: Percentage taken by the first panel.

api.name: minSize / maxSize
api.description: Clamps, so a panel can never be dragged to nothing.

api.name: onResize
api.description: Fires with the new percentage.

api.name: keyboard
api.description: Arrows move by 2%, Shift+arrows by 10%, Home and End jump to the limits.

bottom-nav.label: Bottom Nav
bottom-nav.description: The mobile tab bar — three to five destinations, pinned to the bottom where thumbs are, with the home-indicator safe area accounted for.
bottom-nav.usage:
import { BottomNav } from '@/components/ui/bottom-nav'

<BottomNav items={items} value={tab} onChange={setTab} />

api.name: items
api.description: { value, label, icon, href?, badge?, disabled? }.

api.name: bottom
api.description: Held one-handed, the top of a phone is the hardest region to reach. A top nav bar on mobile costs a reach or a second hand.

api.name: safe area
api.description: Added to the padding, so the bar clears the home indicator. Without it the last row of pixels is not tappable — the most common defect in hand-rolled tab bars.

api.name: destinations, not actions
api.description: A tab bar with "Share" in it is a toolbar wearing the wrong clothes. Past five, targets fall below ~44px and labels truncate to nonsense.

api.name: aria-current
api.description: The navigation equivalent of aria-selected. Signalling the current page with colour alone says nothing to a screen reader.

back-to-top.label: Back To Top
back-to-top.description: Appears once you have scrolled the nearest scrolling ancestor — which it finds itself — and it moves focus, not just the viewport.

api.name: visibility
api.description: A passive scroll listener, coalesced to one read per frame and setting state only when the answer changes. The obvious alternative — an IntersectionObserver on an absolutely positioned sentinel — is cheaper and wrong: the sentinel resolves against the nearest positioned ancestor, so a button rendered at the foot of a page measures the card it sits in and never appears.

api.name: scroller
api.description: Walks up to the first ancestor that actually scrolls, so it works in a document-scrolling app and in one whose page is a scrolling main beside a fixed rail. `targetRef` overrides the search.

api.name: prefers-reduced-motion
api.description: Smooth-scrolling a long page is exactly the large-field motion that triggers vestibular symptoms, so it drops to an instant jump. `scroll-behavior: smooth` with no media query is the common bug.

api.name: focus
api.description: Moving the viewport without moving focus leaves the next Tab at the bottom of the page you just left.

api.name: tabIndex
api.description: A focusable control nobody can see is a trap.

api.name: targetRef
api.description: Name the scrolling element instead of letting it be found.

api.name: showAfter
api.description: Pixels of scroll before it appears. `0` shows it straight away.

story.label: Story
story.description: A full-screen sequence of panels over a darkened page. A dialog underneath — same overlay, focus trap, Escape and scroll lock — but it advances on its own, and everything else follows from that.

api.name: panels
api.description: { id, content, duration? }. Content is a ReactNode, so a panel is not limited to an image — a chart, a form or a changelog entry all work.

api.name: timing
api.description: Progress is recomputed from the animation frame rather than counted down on an interval. A story left in a background tab would otherwise race through every panel and be finished when you came back.

api.name: pausing
api.description: Holding pauses — the gesture from the apps this comes from. Focus inside a panel pauses too, or a panel with a link is unusable while tabbing. prefers-reduced-motion starts it stopped.

api.name: index / onIndexChange
api.description: Controlled position. Uncontrolled by default, resetting to the first panel each time it opens.

api.name: width / height / ratio
api.description: One dimension plus a ratio, never both: with both set, max-height biting on a short window clamps the height alone and squashes the shape. By default it fills the available height, since a fixed 400px box on a desktop reads as a dialog rather than a story.

api.name: maxWidth / maxHeight
api.description: Caps, so the fixed box still fits a small window.

api.name: onFinish
api.description: After the last panel. Defaults to closing.

api.name: keyboard
api.description: The tap zones are real buttons, so the sequence is navigable without a pointer.

dialog.label: Dialog
dialog.description: A modal window, built on the native <dialog> element — so the focus trap, background inerting, Escape handling and top-layer stacking come from the platform rather than from JavaScript.
dialog.usage:
import {
  Dialog,
  DialogTrigger,
  DialogContent,
  DialogHeader,
  DialogTitle,
  DialogBody,
} from '@/components/ui/dialog'

<Dialog>
  <DialogTrigger asChild>
    <Button>Open</Button>
  </DialogTrigger>
  <DialogContent>
    <DialogHeader>
      <DialogTitle>Rename project</DialogTitle>
    </DialogHeader>
    <DialogBody>…</DialogBody>
  </DialogContent>
</Dialog>

api.name: open / defaultOpen
api.description: Controlled and uncontrolled open state, on Dialog.

api.name: onOpenChange
api.description: Fires on every change, including Escape and backdrop dismissal.

api.name: size
api.description: Maximum width of the panel.

api.name: showClose
api.description: Corner close button.

api.name: dismissable
api.description: Whether a backdrop press closes the dialog. Escape always works.

api.name: DialogTrigger asChild
api.description: Render your own element as the trigger instead of a bare button.

alert-dialog.label: Alert Dialog
alert-dialog.description: A modal that interrupts to confirm something consequential. Unlike Dialog it has no backdrop dismissal and no corner close — a destructive confirmation should take a deliberate answer.
alert-dialog.usage:
import {
  AlertDialog, AlertDialogTrigger, AlertDialogContent, AlertDialogHeader,
  AlertDialogTitle, AlertDialogDescription, AlertDialogFooter,
  AlertDialogCancel, AlertDialogAction,
} from '@/components/ui/alert-dialog'

<AlertDialog>
  <AlertDialogTrigger asChild><Button color="destructive">Delete</Button></AlertDialogTrigger>
  <AlertDialogContent>
    <AlertDialogHeader>
      <AlertDialogTitle>Delete this project?</AlertDialogTitle>
      <AlertDialogDescription>This cannot be undone.</AlertDialogDescription>
    </AlertDialogHeader>
    <AlertDialogFooter>
      <AlertDialogCancel>Cancel</AlertDialogCancel>
      <AlertDialogAction color="destructive">Delete</AlertDialogAction>
    </AlertDialogFooter>
  </AlertDialogContent>
</AlertDialog>

api.name: role
api.description: Set automatically. Tells assistive tech this needs a response, not just attention.

api.name: AlertDialogCancel
api.description: Outline button that closes without acting. Rendered first in DOM order so it is the safer default.

api.name: AlertDialogAction
api.description: Confirms and closes. Takes every Button prop, including color="destructive".

api.name: dismissal
api.description: No backdrop click and no close button, by design. Escape still works — trapping someone in a modal is worse.

sheet.label: Sheet
sheet.description: A panel that slides in from an edge. Same native <dialog> machinery as Dialog, pinned to one side — so it inherits the focus trap and Escape handling.
sheet.usage:
import { Sheet, SheetTrigger, SheetContent, SheetHeader, SheetTitle, SheetBody } from '@/components/ui/sheet'

<Sheet>
  <SheetTrigger asChild><Button>Filters</Button></SheetTrigger>
  <SheetContent side="right">
    <SheetHeader><SheetTitle>Filters</SheetTitle></SheetHeader>
    <SheetBody>…</SheetBody>
  </SheetContent>
</Sheet>

api.name: side
api.description: Which edge the panel is pinned to, and the direction it enters from.

api.name: open / defaultOpen
api.description: Controlled and uncontrolled open state.

api.name: onOpenChange
api.description: Fires on every change, including Escape.

api.name: showClose / dismissable
api.description: Corner close button, and whether a backdrop press closes.

api.name: width
api.description: Any CSS length. Applies to a left or right sheet.

api.name: height
api.description: Any CSS length, for a top or bottom sheet.

api.name: edges
api.description: A sheet meets the viewport on three sides, so it draws no outline — a border would only be a line down the middle of the screen.

drawer.label: Drawer
drawer.description: A bottom sheet you can drag away. Built on a native dialog, so focus containment and inerting the page come from the platform rather than a hand-rolled trap.
drawer.usage:
import { Drawer, DrawerHeader, DrawerTitle } from '@/components/ui/drawer'

<Drawer open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
  <DrawerHeader><DrawerTitle>Filters</DrawerTitle></DrawerHeader>
  …
</Drawer>

api.name: open / onOpenChange
api.description: Controlled only — the drawer never closes itself without telling you.

api.name: dismissal
api.description: A flick closes it without dragging the full height; anything shorter and slower snaps back.

api.name: drag
api.description: Transition is off while the finger is down — animating a value you are also setting every frame lags behind the pointer.

api.name: parts
api.description: Same shape as Dialog and Sheet.

tour.label: Tour
tour.description: Guided coach marks over the real interface. Steps point at selectors, so a tour is data next to the copy it belongs to rather than refs threaded through every component it visits.
tour.usage:
import { Tour } from '@/components/ui/tour'

<Tour open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} steps={steps} />

api.name: steps
api.description: `{ target, title, content, side? }` where target is a CSS selector.

api.name: missing targets
api.description: A step whose element is absent is passed over rather than shown floating — targets disappear behind flags and closed panels all the time.

api.name: spotlight
api.description: A ring drawn with a huge outline dims everything else in one element, and leaves the target fully interactive because nothing covers it.

api.name: onFinish
api.description: Fires on Done, on dismiss, and when no step can be shown.

popover.label: Popover
popover.description: Rich content anchored to a trigger. Positioned with a fixed-position popper that flips when it would overflow, and dismissed by Escape or an outside press.

api.name: open / defaultOpen
api.description: Controlled and uncontrolled open state.

api.name: onOpenChange
api.description: Fires on every change.

api.name: side
api.description: Preferred side. Flips to the opposite one when it would overflow the viewport.

api.name: align
api.description: Alignment along the cross axis. Clamped to stay on screen.

api.name: offset
api.description: Gap between trigger and panel, in px.

dropdown-menu.label: Dropdown Menu
dropdown-menu.description: A menu of actions hung off a trigger. Unlike Select this is a list of commands, not a value — items are buttons, the menu closes on activation, and focus returns to the trigger.
dropdown-menu.usage:
import {
  DropdownMenu,
  DropdownMenuTrigger,
  DropdownMenuContent,
  DropdownMenuItem,
} from '@/components/ui/dropdown-menu'

<DropdownMenu>
  <DropdownMenuTrigger asChild><Button>Actions</Button></DropdownMenuTrigger>
  <DropdownMenuContent>
    <DropdownMenuItem onSelect={edit}>Edit</DropdownMenuItem>
  </DropdownMenuContent>
</DropdownMenu>

api.name: open / defaultOpen
api.description: Controlled and uncontrolled open state.

api.name: side / align / offset
api.description: Same popper placement options as Popover.

api.name: DropdownMenuItem onSelect
api.description: Fires on activation, before the menu closes.

api.name: DropdownMenuCheckboxItem
api.description: A menu item that carries state. Uses role="menuitemcheckbox".

api.name: DropdownMenuLabel / DropdownMenuSeparator / DropdownMenuShortcut
api.description: Section heading, divider, and right-aligned key hint.

tooltip.label: Tooltip
tooltip.description: A short hint on hover or focus. Focus opens it immediately — a keyboard user has already committed — while pointer hover waits, so sweeping across a toolbar does not fire a row of them.
tooltip.usage:
import { Tooltip } from '@/components/ui/tooltip'

<Tooltip content="Copy to clipboard">
  <Button size="icon"><Copy /></Button>
</Tooltip>

api.name: content
api.description: What the tooltip says.

api.name: children
api.description: The trigger. Cloned rather than wrapped, so the tooltip adds no element to the layout.

api.name: side
api.description: Preferred side; flips when it would overflow.

api.name: delay
api.description: Pointer-hover delay in ms. Focus ignores it.

hover-card.label: Hover Card
hover-card.description: A preview card shown on hover — richer than a tooltip, and pointer-only. There is a close delay as well as an open delay, so the pointer can travel into the card without it vanishing.
hover-card.usage: import { HoverCard } from '@/components/ui/hover-card' }> @{user.handle}

api.name: content
api.description: What the card shows.

api.name: children
api.description: The trigger, cloned rather than wrapped.

api.name: openDelay / closeDelay
api.description: The close delay is what lets the pointer travel into the card.

api.name: keyboard
api.description: Deliberately pointer-only — the content is supplementary. Use Popover when it must be reachable by keyboard.

context-menu.label: Context Menu
context-menu.description: A menu opened by right-click, positioned at the pointer. It has no element to anchor to — the anchor is a point — so it clamps against the viewport rather than flipping.

api.name: items
api.description: { id, label, icon?, shortcut?, disabled?, destructive?, separatorBefore?, onSelect? }

api.name: children
api.description: The region that responds to right-click.

api.name: positioning
api.description: Opens down-and-right from the cursor, pulled back inside the viewport when it would overflow.

command.label: Command
command.description: A command palette: type to filter, arrows to move, Enter to run. Items are data rather than children, because filtering has to reorder and hide them.
command.usage:
import { CommandDialog } from '@/components/ui/command'

<CommandDialog open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} items={commands} />

api.name: items
api.description: { id, label, group?, icon?, shortcut?, keywords?, disabled?, onSelect? }

api.name: item.keywords
