api.description: Extra search terms that are not shown — "find open" makes "Search files" match "open".

api.name: item.group
api.description: Section heading. Groups collapse when every item in them is filtered out.

api.name: ranking
api.description: A prefix match on the label ranks above a match anywhere else in the item.

api.name: CommandDialog
api.description: The palette in a native <dialog>, which is how it is normally used.

popconfirm.label: Popconfirm
popconfirm.description: A confirmation anchored to the control that triggered it, for reversible or single-item actions — so the row you are asking about stays visible.
popconfirm.usage:
import { Popconfirm } from '@/components/ui/popconfirm'

<Popconfirm title="Remove this?" onConfirm={remove}>
  <Button>Remove</Button>
</Popconfirm>

api.name: children
api.description: The trigger. Cloned with a ref and the ARIA wiring, so it must accept one.

api.name: vs AlertDialog
api.description: If it can be undone, or affects one item, confirm in place. If it destroys something irrecoverable or several things at once, take over the screen — the interruption is the feature.

api.name: in a table
api.description: A modal covers the very row you are asking about, so "which one was it?" is hidden behind the question.

api.name: not modal
api.description: `role="alertdialog"` so it is announced, focus moves to confirm and returns to the trigger, Escape cancels — but the rest of the page stays reachable.

api.name: better still
api.description: Where you can, act immediately and offer an Undo toast. A confirmation people click through reflexively protects nobody.

alert.label: Alert
alert.description: A prominent message that stays on the page. Keeps the colour system, and picks its ARIA role from severity — a destructive alert interrupts, the rest wait their turn.
alert.usage:
import { Alert } from '@/components/ui/alert'

<Alert color="amber" icon={<AlertTriangle />} title="Quota almost reached">
  You have used 92% of your monthly builds.
</Alert>

api.name: variant
api.description: Tinted panel, outline, or solid fill.

api.name: color
api.description: Named colour set. destructive also switches role to "alert".

api.name: tint
api.description: Any CSS colour, used instead of a named set.

api.name: icon
api.description: Leading icon, aligned to the first line of the title.

api.name: title
api.description: Bold first line. Children become the body.

demos.title: Severities
demos.code:
<Alert color="green" icon={<CheckCircle2 />} title="Deployed" />
<Alert color="amber" icon={<AlertTriangle />} title="Quota almost reached" />
<Alert color="destructive" icon={<AlertTriangle />} title="Build failed" />

banner.label: Banner
banner.description: A page-level announcement strip. Distinct from Alert, which belongs to the content around it — a banner spans the page and belongs to the session.
banner.usage:
import { Banner } from '@/components/ui/banner'

<Banner tone="warning" title="Scheduled maintenance" dismissible>
  The API will be unavailable on Sunday from 02:00 UTC.
</Banner>

api.name: tone
api.description: Icon and tint.

api.name: dismissible / onDismiss
api.description: Hides itself and reports; persistence is the caller’s.

api.name: action
api.description: A single control, right-aligned before the dismiss button.

api.name: role
api.description: Not `alert` — an assertive live region interrupts a screen reader mid-sentence, which is right for a form error and wrong for a maintenance notice.

toast.label: Toast
toast.description: Transient messages that stack and dismiss themselves. A provider plus a useToast() hook rather than a global singleton, so the queue lives in React state and two regions can coexist.

api.name: ToastProvider position
api.description: Corner the region is anchored to. Bottom positions stack upward.

api.name: ToastProvider max
api.description: Oldest toasts fall off once this many are showing.

api.name: toast(options)
api.description: Queues a toast and returns its id.

api.name: options.duration
api.description: Milliseconds before auto-dismiss. 0 keeps it until dismissed.

api.name: options.color
api.description: Tints the title.

api.name: dismiss(id)
api.description: Removes a toast early.

demos.title: Queue and stacking
demos.code:
const { toast } = useToast()
toast({ title: 'Deployment finished', color: 'green' })

progress.label: Progress
progress.description: How far along a task is. Omit the value for an indeterminate bar, which sweeps rather than fills — the one honest way to say "working, duration unknown".

api.name: value
api.description: 0–100, clamped. Omit entirely for an indeterminate bar.

api.name: size
api.description: Track thickness.

api.name: color / tint
api.description: Fill colour, from a named set or any CSS colour.

api.name: showValue
api.description: Render the percentage beside the track.

spinner.label: Spinner
spinner.description: An indeterminate busy indicator. Rotation is the one exception the motion rule has to allow — a still spinner says nothing. It stops under prefers-reduced-motion.
spinner.usage:
import { Spinner } from '@/components/ui/spinner'

<Spinner size="sm" label="Loading results" />

api.name: size
api.description: Diameter and border weight.

api.name: label
api.description: Screen-reader text. The element is role="status", so this is what gets announced.

result.label: Result
result.description: The whole-page outcome — not found, forbidden, server error, done. Announced on render, so a client-side route change to an error page is not silent for a screen reader.
result.usage:
import { Result } from '@/components/ui/result'

<Result status="404" title="No such page" actions={<Button>Go home</Button>} />

api.name: status
api.description: 'success' | 'error' | 'warning' | 'info' | '404' | '403' | '500'. Sets an icon and tone; never the copy.

api.name: vs Empty
api.description: Empty means "this worked, there is nothing here yet" and invites a first action. A result reports how a request ended, often one the user cannot fix. Using an empty state for a 403 tells someone to create what they are not allowed to see.

api.name: announced
api.description: Errors are assertive, the rest polite — an SPA that renders an error page silently is the standard failure.

api.name: actions
api.description: A result with no way onward is a dead end that sends people to the back button.

api.name: details
api.description: Collapsed. Stack traces and request ids — whatever a support ticket would want.

demos.title: A 404 with a way out
demos.code: <Result status="404" title="We could not find that page" actions={<Button>Go home</Button>} />

wallet-connect.label: Wallet Connect
wallet-connect.description: Connect button and connected account in one control. Wrong-network outranks showing a balance — a figure from the wrong ledger is worse than none, because it looks authoritative.

api.name: address
api.description: Absent renders the connect button.

api.name: wrongNetwork
api.description: Takes priority over the connected view — no balance is shown from an unsupported chain.

api.name: connecting
api.description: A distinct state: wallet prompts open in another window and can sit unanswered, so the button stops inviting a second click.

api.name: onConnect / onDisconnect / onSwitchNetwork
api.description: The component performs no wallet calls itself.

wallet-address.label: Wallet Address
wallet-address.description: An address shortened for display but never for copying. The truncation floor is security-relevant: attackers generate lookalikes sharing the first and last characters, so `chars` cannot go below six.
wallet-address.usage:
import { WalletAddress } from '@/components/ui/wallet-address'

<WalletAddress address={address} href={explorerUrl} />
<WalletAddress address={address} name="vitalik.eth" />

api.name: address
api.description: The full value. Copy always yields this, never what is displayed.

api.name: chars
api.description: Leading characters, clamped to a minimum of 6 — too few makes address-poisoning lookalikes indistinguishable.

api.name: name
api.description: ENS or label, shown instead of the address. It never replaces the address for copying: names are re-registrable and are not identity.

api.name: href
api.description: Block explorer link.

api.name: shortenAddress
api.description: Exported, with the same floor applied.

token-amount.label: Token Amount
token-amount.description: A balance formatted from base units without ever touching a float. 1 ETH is 10¹⁸ wei, which exceeds Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER by two orders of magnitude — a balance that passes through a JavaScript number is silently wrong.
token-amount.usage:
import { TokenAmount } from '@/components/ui/token-amount'

<TokenAmount value="1234567890123456789" decimals={18} symbol="ETH" />
<TokenAmount value={usdcBalance} decimals={6} symbol="USDC" fiat={2500} />

api.name: value
api.description: Base units. A string keeps it exact — never a number, which loses precision above 2^53.

api.name: decimals
api.description: 18 for most ERC-20s, 8 for BTC, 6 for USDC.

api.name: precision / trim
api.description: Fraction digits shown. Truncated, never rounded up — displaying more than is held produces a failed transaction.

api.name: fiat / fiatCurrency
api.description: Converted value, shown alongside.

api.name: signed
api.description: Colour and sign by direction, for a delta rather than a balance.

api.name: formatUnits / splitUnits
api.description: Exported. The split is done on the digit string — padding and slicing is exact at any magnitude.

demos.title: Precision at scale
demos.code:
<TokenAmount value="999999999999999999" decimals={18} precision={18} symbol="ETH" />
<TokenAmount value="123456789012345678901234" decimals={18} symbol="ETH" />

token-select.label: Token Select
token-select.description: A token picker with balances and search. Symbols are not unique — anyone can deploy a contract called "USDC" — so unverified tokens are segregated, badged, and shown by contract address rather than the name they claim.
token-select.usage:
import { TokenSelect } from '@/components/ui/token-select'

<TokenSelect tokens={tokens} value={token} onValueChange={setToken} />

api.name: tokens
api.description: `{ address, symbol, name?, icon?, balance?, balanceValue?, fiat?, verified? }`.

api.name: verified
api.description: `false` moves the token below a divider with a warning and shows its address instead of its claimed name.

api.name: balanceValue
api.description: Used only for ordering — held tokens sort first, since the one you want is usually one you have.

api.name: search
api.description: Pasting a contract address finds it directly.

chain-select.label: Chain Select
chain-select.description: A network switcher. Testnets are labelled and grouped below mainnets — transacting on the wrong network is the most expensive user error in this space, and an unlabelled list invites it.
chain-select.usage:
import { ChainSelect } from '@/components/ui/chain-select'

<ChainSelect chains={chains} value={chainId} onValueChange={switchChain} />

api.name: chains
api.description: `{ id, name, color?, testnet?, icon?, symbol? }`.

api.name: value
api.description: Chain id. An id absent from the list renders the unsupported state rather than an empty trigger.

api.name: ordering
api.description: Testnets are sorted below and given their own heading, so one never sits between two production chains.

network-status.label: Network Status
network-status.description: RPC health: block height, latency, sync state. Staleness is derived from the age of the last block — a stuck node answers cheerfully with an old height, so "connected" from the node proves nothing.
network-status.usage:
import { NetworkStatus } from '@/components/ui/network-status'

<NetworkStatus chain="Ethereum" blockHeight={21840112} lastBlockAt={last} latency={84} />

api.name: lastBlockAt / blockTime
api.description: Three missed block times counts as stale — stuck, not merely slow.

api.name: latency
api.description: Milliseconds. Over a second reads as degraded.

api.name: blockHeight / peers
api.description: Reported as given.

portfolio-balance.label: Portfolio Balance
portfolio-balance.description: Total value with its allocation. The hide toggle is part of the component, not an app-level bolt-on — people check balances on trains. Allocation is computed from the values, never taken as a percentage prop.

api.name: holdings
api.description: `{ id, symbol, value, amount?, change24h?, color?, icon? }` where value is fiat.

api.name: hidden / onHiddenChange
api.description: Masks every figure. Controlled or uncontrolled.

api.name: groupBelow
api.description: Share below which a holding folds into "Other" — forty one-pixel slivers say less than six slices and a remainder.

api.name: allocation
api.description: From the values themselves; a bar that does not add to 100 is the kind of thing people screenshot.

transaction-list.label: Transaction List
transaction-list.description: Wallet activity grouped by day. Direction is derived against the connected account, not passed in — the same transfer is a send for one wallet and a receive for another, and a self-transfer is both.

api.name: transactions
api.description: `{ hash, from, to, amount?, fiat?, time, kind?, failed?, href? }`.

api.name: account
api.description: Required. Direction is computed against it, which is the only way a self-transfer renders correctly.

api.name: failed
api.description: Still shown — it consumed gas and is on-chain; hiding it leaves the balance unexplained.

swap-panel.label: Swap Panel
swap-panel.description: The pay/receive form of a token swap. Price impact is surfaced rather than buried behind a details toggle, and above a threshold the action is disabled outright.
swap-panel.usage:
import { SwapPanel } from '@/components/ui/swap-panel'

<SwapPanel from={from} to={to} priceImpact={0.8} minimumReceived="1,240 USDC" onSwap={swap} />

api.name: from / to
api.description: `{ symbol, amount, fiat?, balance?, icon? }`.

api.name: priceImpact
api.description: Percentage. Coloured above `impactWarn` (3) and the action is disabled above `impactBlock` (15).

api.name: minimumReceived
api.description: An amount, not just a slippage percentage — "0.5%" is abstract, an amount is what the user agrees to.

api.name: onSwap / onFlip / onSettings
api.description: The panel performs no routing or quoting of its own.

demos.title: Healthy and blocked
demos.code:
<SwapPanel from={from} to={to} priceImpact={0.4} />
<SwapPanel from={from} to={to} priceImpact={18.5} />

transaction-status.label: Transaction Status
transaction-status.description: A transaction from submitted to final. Confirmations are progress toward a threshold, not a tick at one block — chains reorganise, and "done" at one confirmation teaches a habit that eventually costs money.
transaction-status.usage:
import { TransactionStatus } from '@/components/ui/transaction-status'

<TransactionStatus hash={hash} state="mined" confirmations={4} required={12} href={explorer} />

api.name: state
api.description: Reverted is distinct from a failed submission: it was mined and consumed gas, and collapsing the two hides that the user paid.

api.name: confirmations / required
api.description: Rendered as progress toward settlement.

api.name: href
api.description: Block explorer link for the hash.

gas-tracker.label: Gas Tracker
gas-tracker.description: Gas tiers with what each actually costs. Gwei alone is not a decision — the same gas price costs four times more for a swap than a transfer, which is why gasLimit is a prop.
gas-tracker.usage:
import { GasTracker } from '@/components/ui/gas-tracker'

<GasTracker tiers={tiers} gasLimit={120000} nativePrice={ethUsd} onSelect={setTier} />

api.name: tiers
api.description: `{ id, label, price, wait?, recommended? }` where price is gwei.

api.name: gasLimit
api.description: Units of gas for the transaction being priced — 21000 is a bare transfer.

api.name: nativePrice
api.description: Fiat price of the native token. Without it the cost is shown in the native unit.

api.name: wait
api.description: Shown beside the price: the trade is time against money, and a price with no time shows one side.

token-approvals.label: Token Approvals
token-approvals.description: Spending allowances granted to contracts, with revoke. An unlimited approval is stated as "unlimited" rather than rendered as 2²⁵⁶−1, which reads like a display bug — it is a standing permission to move the whole balance, forever.

api.name: approvals
api.description: `{ id, token, spender, spenderName?, allowance?, unlimited?, lastUsed?, atRisk? }`.

api.name: unlimited
api.description: Badged as a risk rather than shown as a number.

api.name: atRisk
api.description: Fiat value currently exposed under the approval — the figure that makes it concrete.

api.name: onRevoke
api.description: Confirmed inline beside the row, since a modal hiding which approval is being revoked is how the wrong one goes.

staking-panel.label: Staking Panel
staking-panel.description: A staking position: stake, rewards, APY and unlock. APY is labelled variable unless told otherwise, because it almost always is — a bare percentage reads as a fixed-term rate.
staking-panel.usage:
import { StakingPanel } from '@/components/ui/staking-panel'

<StakingPanel token="stETH" staked="12.4 ETH" rewards="0.284 ETH" apy={3.82} unbonding="21 days" />

api.name: staked / rewards
api.description: Formatted amounts — pair with TokenAmount for exactness.

api.name: apy / apyFixed
api.description: Variable by default, with a note saying so. Only set `apyFixed` when the rate genuinely cannot move.

api.name: unbonding / unlockProgress
api.description: The unbonding period gets equal weight to the yield — it is the part that actually constrains the user.

api.name: onStake / onUnstake / onClaim
api.description: Actions are reported; the panel performs no transactions.

demos.title: Position
demos.code: <StakingPanel token="stETH" staked="12.4 ETH" apy={3.82} unbonding="21 days" />

price-ticker.label: Price Ticker
price-ticker.description: A live price with its change. The flash on update is colour only — a ticker that moves makes the whole page twitch — and it compares against the previous rendered price, not the day’s direction.
price-ticker.usage:
import { PriceTicker } from '@/components/ui/price-ticker'

<PriceTicker symbol="BTC" price={price} change={2.41} history={history} />

api.name: price / change
api.description: Change is a percentage over `window`.

api.name: precision
api.description: Defaults by magnitude — a $0.000042 token needs eight digits where a $67,000 one needs two.

api.name: flash
api.description: Compares against the previous rendered price held in a ref. Deriving it from the day’s change would flash green on every tick of an up day.

api.name: history
api.description: Rendered as a Sparkline tinted by direction.

market-table.label: Market Table
market-table.description: A market list with price, change, volume and cap. Rank is the caller’s, never the row index — a re-sorted table that renumbers from one destroys the identifier people use to talk about a market.
market-table.usage:
import { MarketTable } from '@/components/ui/market-table'

<MarketTable markets={markets} onStar={star} onSelect={open} />

api.name: markets
api.description: `{ id, rank?, symbol, name, price, change24h?, volume24h?, marketCap?, history?, starred? }`.

api.name: onStar
api.description: Watchlist state is reported, never held — a starred asset belongs to an account, not a table that forgets on unmount.

api.name: columns
api.description: Volume drops below `sm`, cap below `md`, the sparkline below `lg`. The table also scrolls rather than crushing.

api.name: price precision
api.description: Sub-dollar assets get four digits; large caps use compact notation.

candlestick-chart.label: Candlestick Chart
candlestick-chart.description: OHLC candles with a volume strip. Unlike every other chart here it does not stretch — a stretched candle varies its body width with the container while the wick stays one unit, and the body-versus-wick reading stops working.

api.name: candles
api.description: `{ time, open, high, low, close, volume? }`.

api.name: axis padding
api.description: The scale is padded to the extremes of the wicks, not the bodies — otherwise the highest high clips exactly when it matters.

api.name: doji
api.description: A body with equal open and close still draws a visible line rather than a zero-height rect.

order-book.label: Order Book
order-book.description: Bids and asks with cumulative depth. The bar is the running total from the top of book, not the size at that level — what matters when taking liquidity is how much sits between you and a price.
order-book.usage:
import { OrderBook } from '@/components/ui/order-book'

<OrderBook bids={bids} asks={asks} quoteSymbol="USD" baseSymbol="BTC" />

api.name: bids / asks
api.description: `{ price, size }`. Sorted internally, so the caller need not.

api.name: depth bars
api.description: Per-level bars are the common mistake and misrepresent the book — this is a running sum on one shared scale across both sides.

api.name: layout
api.description: So the spread sits in the middle, which is the convention traders read without thinking.

nft-card.label: NFT Card
nft-card.description: A token tile: media, collection, price. Broken media resolves to a placeholder rather than collapsing the tile — IPFS gateways fail constantly and a grid that reflows on every 404 is unusable.
nft-card.usage:
import { NftCard } from '@/components/ui/nft-card'

<NftCard name="Astral #1420" collection="Astralyx" verified price="2.4 ETH" image={url} />

api.name: name / tokenId / collection
api.description: Identity of the item and its collection.

api.name: verified
api.description: Applies to the collection, never the item. Copied collections are the standard scam here, and a tick beside an item name implies something nobody checked.

api.name: image
api.description: A load failure swaps in a placeholder; the tile keeps its aspect ratio either way.

api.name: price / lastSale / rarity
api.description: Formatting is the caller’s — pair with TokenAmount.

demos.title: Grid
demos.code: <NftCard name="Astral" tokenId="1420" collection="Astralyx Genesis" verified price="2.4 ETH" />

mint-panel.label: Mint Panel
mint-panel.description: Supply, price and quantity, with the total shown before the button. A price of "0.08 ETH" beside a quantity of 5 is not a number anyone should be multiplying in their head at a mint.
mint-panel.usage:
import { MintPanel } from '@/components/ui/mint-panel'

<MintPanel minted={3820} supply={5000} price={0.08} priceLabel="ETH" />

api.name: minted / supply
api.description: Drives the progress bar and the sold-out state.

api.name: maxPerWallet / alreadyMinted
api.description: The cap is enforced against what is already held, not just the quantity in the box.

api.name: price / priceLabel
api.description: A number so the total can be computed and shown before the button.

bridge-status.label: Bridge Status
bridge-status.description: A cross-chain transfer as its two legs. Not one progress bar: the legs fail independently and the second cannot begin until the first is final, so a single bar implies a state that does not exist.
bridge-status.usage:
import { BridgeStatus } from '@/components/ui/bridge-status'

<BridgeStatus source={source} destination={destination} amount="0.5 ETH" />

api.name: source / destination
api.description: `{ chain, state, detail?, progress?, href? }`.

api.name: detail
api.description: Names what is being waited on. "Pending" for twenty minutes is the most common bridge support ticket; "waiting for 64 confirmations" is the same wait without the anxiety.

api.name: estimate
api.description: Expected total time.

liquidity-position.label: Liquidity Position
liquidity-position.description: A concentrated-liquidity position with its range. In-range versus out-of-range is the headline — a position outside its range earns nothing, and a card showing only "fees earned" while it stopped earning last week is misleading.
liquidity-position.usage:
import { LiquidityPosition } from '@/components/ui/liquidity-position'

<LiquidityPosition pair="ETH / USDC" minPrice={2800} maxPrice={3600} currentPrice={3284} />

api.name: minPrice / maxPrice / currentPrice
api.description: In-range is derived from these, never passed as a flag.

api.name: range bar
api.description: With padding either side, so an out-of-range price stays visible and "just inside" looks different from "about to exit".

api.name: fees / value / apr
api.description: Formatting is the caller’s — pair with TokenAmount.

governance-proposal.label: Governance Proposal
governance-proposal.description: A proposal with its tally. Quorum is tracked separately from the majority because they are separate tests — a 92% "for" reads as passing right up until it fails for turnout.
governance-proposal.usage:
import { GovernanceProposal } from '@/components/ui/governance-proposal'

<GovernanceProposal id="AIP-42" title="…" state="active" forVotes={820000} againstVotes={64000} quorum={1200000} />

api.name: forVotes / againstVotes / abstainVotes
api.description: Abstain counts toward quorum but never toward the majority — folding it into "against" gets the outcome wrong.

api.name: quorum
api.description: Always rendered, including once met.

api.name: state
api.description: Voting controls appear only while active.

validator-list.label: Validator List
validator-list.description: Validators with commission, uptime and voting power. Flags membership of the smallest set controlling a third of the stake, and sorts ascending by default — the conventional descending sort pushes delegators toward whoever is already largest.

api.name: validators
api.description: `{ id, name, avatar?, commission, uptime?, votingPower, jailed? }`.

api.name: concentration
api.description: Marks the validators making up the smallest set that controls a third of the stake — the threshold that matters for halting a chain.

api.name: sort
api.description: Descending by voting power is the conventional order and it pushes delegators toward whoever is already largest.

api.name: onSelect
api.description: Omit for a read-only table.

seed-phrase.label: Seed Phrase
seed-phrase.description: A recovery phrase, blurred until revealed. Deliberately hostile to convenience: no copy button and no selection, because a seed phrase on the clipboard is readable by every page visited afterwards.
seed-phrase.usage:
import { SeedPhrase } from '@/components/ui/seed-phrase'

<SeedPhrase words={words} />
<SeedPhrase words={words} confirmIndices={[2, 7, 11]} onConfirm={next} />

api.name: words
api.description: 12 or 24 words. Never copyable and not selectable while hidden.

api.name: revealed / onRevealedChange
api.description: Blurred by default — these are read in cafés and on video calls, so revealing is a decision rather than the default.

api.name: confirmIndices
api.description: 0-based positions to ask back, which is the only way to establish the phrase was written down rather than clicked past.

api.name: no clipboard
api.description: There is no copy button. Clipboard managers persist to disk and every subsequent page can read it.

notification-inbox.label: Notification Inbox
notification-inbox.description: A notification list grouped by day, with unread state. Unread is reported, never assumed — a panel that marks everything read on render clears what the user never saw.
notification-inbox.usage:
import { NotificationInbox } from '@/components/ui/notification-inbox'

<NotificationInbox notifications={items} onRead={markRead} onReadAll={markAllRead} />

api.name: notifications
api.description: `{ id, title, description?, time, read?, actor?, icon?, onSelect? }`.

api.name: onRead / onReadAll
api.description: Reading happens when someone acts, which is the caller’s call to make.

api.name: grouping
api.description: "When" is the axis people scan a notification list along — the same reason CommitList groups.

api.name: filter
api.description: Local to the component; it never mutates the list.

user-menu.label: User Menu
user-menu.description: The account button for a header or sidebar footer. The identity is repeated inside the panel, because on a collapsed rail the trigger is a bare avatar.
user-menu.usage:
import { UserMenu } from '@/components/ui/user-menu'

<UserMenu name="Ada Lovelace" email="ada@astralyx.dev" plan="Team" actions={actions} />

api.name: name / email / plan
api.description: Shown on the trigger and repeated in the panel.

api.name: actions
api.description: `{ id, label, icon?, shortcut?, destructive?, separatorBefore?, onSelect? }`.

api.name: compact
api.description: Avatar only, for a collapsed rail. The name stays as the accessible label.

api.name: composition
api.description: Built on it rather than reimplementing a popover, so dismissal and keyboard behaviour come from the component that already handles them.

presence.label: Presence
presence.description: Who else is here. The overflow count carries its own tooltip listing the rest — a "+5" that cannot tell you who is unhelpful in exactly the moment you care.

api.name: peers
api.description: `{ id, name, status?, color? }` with status one of active, idle or away.

api.name: max
api.description: Avatars before the overflow chip.

api.name: status
api.description: The only thing that changes, so someone going idle does not reflow the row.

mention-input.label: Mention Input
mention-input.description: A textarea with @-mention autocomplete. The trigger only fires at a word boundary, so an email address does not open the menu halfway through every address anyone types.
mention-input.usage:
import { MentionInput } from '@/components/ui/mention-input'

<MentionInput options={people} value={body} onValueChange={setBody} />

api.name: options
api.description: `{ id, label, description?, avatar? }`.

api.name: onMention
api.description: Fires on insert, for collecting the mentioned ids alongside the text.

api.name: trigger
api.description: Any prefix — `#` for issues, `/` for commands.

api.name: positioning
api.description: Not to the caret: caret coordinates in a textarea need a measured mirror element and break on wrap, and a menu under the field is understood immediately.

countdown.label: Countdown
countdown.description: Time remaining until a deadline, ticking. It counts toward a Date rather than decrementing a number, because setInterval is throttled in a background tab — a decremented timer drifts and then confidently shows the wrong number.

api.name: to
api.description: The deadline. Recomputed from the clock on every tick, so an interval that fired late — or not at all, in a suspended tab — cannot make it drift.

api.name: onExpire
api.description: Fires once, at zero. It never renders negative time; that reads as a bug rather than as elapsed time.

api.name: showSeconds
api.description: Also sets the tick rate: 1s when seconds are shown, 15s when they are not. Waking the main thread every second to redraw a number that changes every minute is a battery cost with nothing to show for it.

api.name: showDays
api.description: Off folds days into hours, so a two-day countdown does not read as 00:12:09.

api.name: now
api.description: A fixed reference instead of the clock — for tests and deterministic server rendering.

api.name: format
api.description: Receives { days, hours, minutes, seconds, total }.

copy-button.label: Copy Button
copy-button.description: Copies a string and says so. Extracted after the same clipboard-plus-timer was written four times in this kit — CodeBlock, Terminal, EnvVars and Message all route through it now.
copy-button.usage:
import { CopyButton } from '@/components/ui/copy-button'

<CopyButton value={snippet} />
<CopyButton value={() => buildExpensiveText()} showLabel />

api.name: value
api.description: A function is read at click time — for text that is expensive to build or that changes after render.

api.name: showLabel
api.description: Render the label beside the icon. When off it is still the accessible name, which is what changes to "Copied" — a tick replacing a clipboard is invisible to a screen reader.

api.name: label / copiedLabel
api.description: Wording for both states.

api.name: useClipboard
api.description: The underlying hook: clears its timeout on unmount, restarts rather than stacks on a second copy, and reports `error` when the write is rejected instead of claiming success.

composer.label: Composer
composer.description: A live playground: drive a set of props and watch the generated source follow. Assembled from the kit’s own controls, so anything awkward about Select, Switch or NumberInput surfaces here first.

api.name: controls
api.description: One per prop: `select`, `boolean`, `text`, `number` or `color`. Each names the prop it drives and its default.

api.name: render
api.description: Draws the live result from the current state.

api.name: code
api.description: The snippet shown beneath the preview. Omit it for a preview with no source.

api.name: state / onStateChange
api.description: Controlled mode, for keeping two composers in sync — a light and a dark preview of one configuration.

api.name: tall
api.description: A taller preview box, for anything with real height.

api.name: fullscreen
api.description: The expand button in the panel header. A composer driving something small does not need it — the room was never the constraint there.

api.name: filling the screen
api.description: The real thing where the browser allows it, so the page chrome goes too and Escape is handled for us. iPhone Safari exposes no element fullscreen and a request can simply be refused, so a refusal covers the viewport instead rather than leaving a button that does nothing. Leaving it is read back from `fullscreenchange`, not assumed from the click that started it.

api.name: independence
api.description: The component knows nothing about the documentation registry; the registry describes its specs in terms of these types, not the reverse.

logo.label: Logo
logo.description: A brand mark that follows the room it has: the full artwork while the rail is open, the square mark once it collapses. Falls back to the product name, and to its initials when only 52px are left.
logo.usage:
import { Logo } from '@/components/ui/logo'

<Logo
  icon="/mark.svg"
  full="/logo.svg"
  alt="Acme"
  fallbackText="Acme"
/>

api.name: icon
api.description: The square mark, shown once the rail collapses. A URL renders as an image; anything else renders as given.

api.name: full
api.description: The full artwork, shown while there is room for it.

api.name: alt
api.description: The accessible name, set on the container so a reader hears it once whichever rendition is showing. Empty means decorative — use that when the product name is already written beside it.

api.name: fallbackText
api.description: Drawn when there is no artwork or an image fails to load. Collapsed it becomes initials, because a name does not fit in 52px.

api.name: collapsed
api.description: Overrides the sidebar. Left off, the switch is CSS keyed to the rail's `data-state`, so the component needs no context and works outside one.

api.name: accessibility
api.description: Both renditions are in the DOM when the switch is left to CSS, so the name is on the container and the contents are presentational. Two copies of a logo are one logo.

api.name: both renditions
api.description: Leaving the switch to CSS puts both images in the document, and a browser fetches both. Pass `collapsed` when you already have the state — then only one renders.

demos.title: No artwork — the name, then its initials
demos.code:
<Logo alt="Acme Corp" fallbackText="Acme Corp" />
<Logo alt="Acme Corp" fallbackText="Acme Corp" collapsed />

demos.title: A URL that does not resolve falls through to the text

theme-toggle.label: Theme Toggle
theme-toggle.description: Switches the document between light and dark. Uncontrolled by default: it reads the class already on the element rather than flashing to its own idea of the default on mount.

api.name: dark / onDarkChange
api.description: Controlled mode. Omit both and it manages itself.

api.name: target
api.description: The class goes on the root, never a wrapper: `.dark` defines the token values on the element it lands on, so a descendant cannot switch a subtree back.

api.name: variant / size
api.description: Passed through to Button.

api.name: persistence
api.description: The toggle does not remember the choice — it has no idea where your app keeps state. Store it, and re-apply the class from an inline script in <head> so the page does not paint the wrong palette first. Without both halves, every reload falls back to whatever the HTML shipped with.

demos.title: Remembering the choice

page-header.label: Page Header
page-header.description: The masthead a page opens with: eyebrow, title, lead and a meta row. Extracted after four pages in this catalogue had each grown their own copy and drifted apart.
page-header.usage:
import { PageHeader } from '@/components/ui/page-header'

<PageHeader
  eyebrow={<Breadcrumb>…</Breadcrumb>}
  title="Components"
  description="Every primitive in the kit."
  meta={<Badge size="sm">142 components</Badge>}
/>

api.name: title
api.description: Rendered as the page h1, balanced across lines.

api.name: eyebrow
api.description: The line above the title — a breadcrumb, a source path, a section label.

api.name: description / meta
api.description: Lead paragraph, and a row beneath it for counts, badges or links.

skip-link.label: Skip Link
skip-link.description: The first tab stop: jump past the navigation to the content. Invisible until focused, which is the whole design.
skip-link.usage:
import { SkipLink } from '@/components/ui/skip-link'

<SkipLink href="#main" />
…
<main id="main" tabIndex={-1}>…</main>

api.name: href
api.description: The target. It needs `tabIndex={-1}` or the click scrolls the page but leaves focus on the link, so the next Tab starts from the top again.

api.name: visibility
api.description: Appears on focus rather than sliding in from off-screen — a state change, not motion.

visually-hidden.label: Visually Hidden
visually-hidden.description: Hidden from sight, present for screen readers. The clip technique — not display:none or visibility:hidden, both of which remove the element from the accessibility tree entirely.

api.name: asChild
api.description: Apply to an element that already carries its own classes.

api.name: technique
api.description: Identical to Tailwind sr-only; the component exists so the intent is legible in the markup.

live-announcer.label: Live Announcer
live-announcer.description: Imperative screen-reader announcements for things with no visible region of their own — a background save finishing, a filter narrowing a list.
live-announcer.usage:
import { LiveAnnouncer, useAnnouncer } from '@/components/ui/live-announcer'

<LiveAnnouncer>
  <App />
</LiveAnnouncer>

const announce = useAnnouncer()
announce('Filter applied, 12 results')

api.name: announce(message, politeness)
api.description: Defaults to polite. Assertive interrupts whatever is being read — right for an error, wrong for "maintenance on Sunday".

api.name: two regions
api.description: Politeness cannot be changed on a live region after the fact, so each gets its own and the message goes to the matching one.

api.name: repeat handling
api.description: Setting identical text twice is not a mutation and would not be announced; a zero-width counter forces the change without altering what is spoken.

error-boundary.label: Error Boundary
error-boundary.description: Catches a render error in its subtree and shows a fallback. The one component here that must be a class — getDerivedStateFromError has no hook equivalent.

api.name: resetKeys
api.description: Clears the error when any entry changes. Without it, clearing re-renders the same children with the same props and throws again immediately.

api.name: fallback
api.description: Replaces the default panel.

api.name: onError
api.description: Wire your own telemetry. The component deliberately reports nowhere on its own.

qr-code.label: QR Code
qr-code.description: A QR code encoded in the browser and drawn as SVG. No dependency and no network round trip — which matters, because the two things people encode most are a TOTP secret and a wallet address.
qr-code.usage:
import { QrCode } from '@/components/ui/qr-code'

<QrCode value="https://ui.astralyx.dev" level="M" size={160} />

api.name: value
api.description: Encoded in byte mode, versions 1–10 — 271 bytes at level L, 213 at M. Past that it throws rather than truncating a secret.

api.name: nothing leaves the page
api.description: The usual shortcut is an `` at a QR-as-a-service URL, which hands a TOTP secret or a payment address to a third party and writes it into their access log.

api.name: level
api.description: Higher recovers more damage and holds less. `H` is worth it when a logo covers the middle or it is printed on something that creases.

api.name: mask selection
api.description: The real spec, not a fixed pattern. Scanners genuinely fail on a bad mask, and "mask 0 always" makes a code that reads on one phone and not another.

api.name: quietZone
api.description: Four modules is the spec minimum, and a code butted against a coloured background is the most common reason a QR will not scan.

api.name: SVG, not canvas
api.description: Sharp at any size and in print, no raster memory, and it survives a server render — canvas needs an effect, a ref and a device-pixel-ratio dance.

api.name: darkColor / lightColor
api.description: Near-black on white regardless of theme, deliberately. Inverting them defeats most scanners.

cookie-consent.label: Cookie Consent
cookie-consent.description: A consent banner with reject as easy as accept, nothing pre-ticked, and no cookie written by the component itself — the arrangement regulators have repeatedly ruled is the compliant one.
cookie-consent.usage:
import { CookieConsent } from '@/components/ui/cookie-consent'

<CookieConsent onSave={(accepted) => persist(accepted)} policyHref="/privacy" />

api.name: reject
api.description: Not a style choice. Consent must be freely given, and hiding refusal behind an extra click — or greying it beside a bright "Accept all" — has been found to invalidate it. "Accept" plus "Manage" is the most-fined pattern on the web.

api.name: categories
api.description: Nothing optional starts on: pre-ticked boxes are explicitly not consent. `necessary` is locked on and excluded from the choice.

api.name: writes nothing
api.description: Storage and script loading are the caller’s job. A component that quietly sets its own cookie is doing the exact thing it is meant to be asking about.

api.name: not modal
api.description: Announced and reachable, but focus is not trapped — a banner people cannot escape is its own accessibility failure.

api.name: policyHref
api.description: Links the privacy policy inline with the description.

pipeline.label: Pipeline
pipeline.description: CI stages left to right with parallel jobs stacked inside each. A stage is as bad as its worst job, so its state is derived rather than being another field to keep in sync.

api.name: stages
api.description: `{ id, name, jobs }` where a job is `{ id, name, status, duration?, onSelect? }`.

api.name: stageStatus
api.description: Exported roll-up: failure beats running beats pending. Use it for a summary elsewhere so both agree.

api.name: onSelect
api.description: Makes a job a button. Jobs without one render as plain rows rather than dead buttons.

api.name: layout
api.description: Scrolls horizontally instead of wrapping — a pipeline read out of order is meaningless — and stacks to one column below md.

service-status.label: Service Status
service-status.description: The rows of a status page. The headline banner is derived from the services — a status page whose headline can disagree with its own rows is worse than none.

api.name: services
api.description: `{ id, name, state, description?, history?, uptime? }`.

api.name: state
api.description: Each row carries a dot and a labelled badge, never colour alone.

api.name: overallState
api.description: Exported. Worst state wins, so one outage cannot be reported as all-operational.

api.name: history
api.description: Rendered with UptimeStrip inside each row.

uptime-strip.label: Uptime Strip
uptime-strip.description: A run of per-period bars: uptime history or a contribution heatmap. One primitive for both, since they are the same picture — buckets coloured by state or by intensity.
uptime-strip.usage:
import { UptimeStrip } from '@/components/ui/uptime-strip'

<UptimeStrip buckets={days} label="API" summary="99.94%" />

api.name: buckets
api.description: `{ label, status?, value?, detail? }`. Give `status` for a state strip or `value` (0–1) for a heatmap.

api.name: status
api.description: A missing bucket renders as an explicit gap rather than being dropped, which keeps the axis honest.

api.name: label / summary
api.description: Caption row above the bars.

api.name: layout
api.description: Bars flex rather than taking a fixed width, so ninety days compress on a phone instead of scrolling.

resource-meter.label: Resource Meter
resource-meter.description: Used against a cap: build minutes, storage, seats, rate limits. Unlike Progress it can exceed 100%, because a quota can be 130% used and hiding that is how a bill becomes a surprise.
resource-meter.usage:
import { ResourceMeter } from '@/components/ui/resource-meter'

<ResourceMeter label="Build minutes" used={8420} cap={10000} />

api.name: used / cap
api.description: The bar clamps at full; the printed percentage does not, so an overage is stated rather than hidden.

api.name: unit
api.description: How both numbers are written — routed through Fmt.

api.name: tone
api.description: Any CSS colour. Defaults to a ramp: blue, amber above 80%, red above 95% or over cap.

api.name: size
api.description: Bar and label scale.

demos.title: Quotas
demos.code:
<ResourceMeter label="Build minutes" used={8420} cap={10000} />
<ResourceMeter label="Storage" used={49_500_000_000} cap={50_000_000_000} unit="bytes" />
<ResourceMeter label="Bandwidth" used={640} cap={500} />

incident-card.label: Incident Card
incident-card.description: An incident: severity, state, owner, age. Severity is a left edge rather than a tinted surface, because a list of ten red cards is unreadable and the stripe scales to a queue.
incident-card.usage:
import { IncidentCard } from '@/components/ui/incident-card'

<IncidentCard
  title="Elevated error rate on checkout"
  severity="sev2"
  startedAt={startedAt}
  assignee="Ada Lovelace"
/>

api.name: severity
api.description: Drives the edge colour and the badge.

api.name: state
api.description: Resolved dims the card.

api.name: startedAt / resolvedAt
api.description: Duration is computed from these, so an open incident ages on its own rather than showing a stale string.

api.name: now
api.description: Reference point for the age. Pass it to keep a render deterministic.

api.name: assignee / services
api.description: Owner avatar and the affected components.

demos.title: Queue
demos.code:
<IncidentCard title="…" severity="sev1" startedAt={t1} />
<IncidentCard title="…" severity="sev3" state="resolved" startedAt={t2} resolvedAt={t3} />

env-vars.label: Env Vars
env-vars.description: Environment variables with secrets masked until asked for. Reveal is per-row and never sticky — nothing survives a remount, so a shared screen cannot leak what someone expanded an hour ago.

api.name: vars
api.description: `{ key, value, secret?, scopes?, updated? }`.

api.name: secret
api.description: Masks the value and adds a reveal toggle. The mask is a fixed width, since the length of a secret is itself a hint about what it is.

api.name: scopes
api.description: Environments the variable applies to, shown as badges.

api.name: copy
api.description: Copies the real value even while masked — the common reason to open one of these is to paste it somewhere.

health-checks.label: Health Checks
health-checks.description: Endpoint probes with status, latency and history. A 200 that takes four seconds reads as degraded — a probe list that only reports the status code is why slow outages get noticed by customers first.

api.name: checks
api.description: `{ id, name, url?, status, latency?, latencyThreshold?, code?, history?, region? }`.

api.name: latencyThreshold
api.description: Above it a healthy response is reported as degraded.

api.name: effectiveStatus
api.description: Exported, so a summary elsewhere agrees with the row.

api.name: history
api.description: Recent latencies as a sparkline — a single number cannot say whether 400ms is normal or the start of something.

cron-schedule.label: Cron Schedule
cron-schedule.description: Scheduled jobs: when each next runs and how the last went. An overdue job — next run in the past with nothing running — is called out, since that is the failure a schedule list exists to catch.

api.name: jobs
api.description: `{ id, name, expression, description?, nextRun?, lastRun?, lastStatus?, lastDuration?, paused? }`.

api.name: overdue
api.description: Next run in the past, not paused, nothing running. Invisible if you only render the timestamp.

api.name: times
api.description: "in 4 hours" and "2 hours ago" are the actual questions; the absolute time is in the title attribute.

feature-flag.label: Feature Flag
feature-flag.description: A flag with its rollout percentage and targeting rules. The kill switch is a separate control from the rollout — during an incident, turning it off must be one action, not a slider drag.

api.name: enabled / onEnabledChange
api.description: The kill switch, deliberately independent of the rollout.

api.name: rollout / onRolloutChange
api.description: 0–100. Disabled while the flag is off; the bar is drawn even at 100% so "fully rolled out" and "off" are distinct states.

api.name: rules
api.description: `{ id, condition, label, enabled? }` — targeting shown as data, not editable here.

api.name: environment
api.description: Badge on the header, since the same flag exists per environment.

traffic-split.label: Traffic Split
traffic-split.description: Traffic weights across versions — canary or blue/green. Weights that do not total 100 are called out rather than silently rescaled, because a config adding to 97 is a real state during an edit.

api.name: targets
api.description: `{ id, label, weight, version?, color?, canary? }`.

api.name: shortfall
api.description: A total other than 100 is stated above the bar; the segments still render proportionally so the picture stays readable.

api.name: labels
api.description: Inside only above 12% width — a 3% canary has no room for text but is exactly the segment you are watching.

file-tree.label: File Tree
file-tree.description: Files and directories as a tree. Uses the ARIA tree pattern with roving focus — arrow keys move between rows, so a repository with 200 files does not cost 200 tab stops.

api.name: nodes
api.description: { name, children?, meta?, badge?, defaultOpen? }. Children make a node a directory.

api.name: value / onSelect
api.description: Selected path, joined with "/". Controlled or uncontrolled.

api.name: showMeta
api.description: Right-hand column — a commit message, a size, a timestamp.

api.name: keyboard
api.description: Up and down move between rows, left and right collapse and expand, Home and End jump.

api.name: icons
api.description: Chosen from the file extension, so callers pass names rather than icons.

commit-list.label: Commit List
commit-list.description: A history, grouped by day. The grouping is the point — a flat list of forty commits is unreadable, and "when" is the axis people actually scan along.

api.name: commits
api.description: { sha, message, author, date, status?, verified?, additions?, deletions?, body? }

api.name: grouping
api.description: Order within a day is preserved exactly as given — the component groups, it never re-sorts.

api.name: locale
api.description: Drives the date headings and times through Intl.

api.name: onSelect
api.description: Fires from both the message and the short-sha button.

deploy-list.label: Deploy List
deploy-list.description: Deployments, newest first. A running deploy shows an indeterminate bar rather than a fabricated percentage — a number nobody can compute is worse than admitting you cannot.

api.name: deploys
api.description: { id, environment, status, branch, commit, message, author, duration?, when, url? }

api.name: status
api.description: Drives the badge colour, and whether the progress bar appears.

api.name: environment
api.description: Each gets its own colour, so the target is readable at a glance.

api.name: onRedeploy
api.description: Adds a redeploy action to every row when provided.

branch-select.label: Branch Select
branch-select.description: A branch and tag picker. A Combobox underneath — repositories routinely have hundreds of branches, so search is not optional — with the default branch pinned first and tags labelled.

api.name: branches
api.description: { name, kind?, isDefault?, protected? }

api.name: ordering
api.description: Default branch first, then branches, then tags — the order people scan in.

api.name: value / onValueChange
api.description: Controlled and uncontrolled, same as Combobox.

diff-stat.label: Diff Stat
diff-stat.description: Added and removed line counts with the five-square bar. The squares are proportional but never empty — one line changed in a thousand still lights one square.

api.name: additions / deletions
api.description: Line counts. The bar is proportional to their ratio.

api.name: showCounts
api.description: Numbers beside the squares.

api.name: squares
api.description: How many squares the bar has.

diff-view.label: Diff View
diff-view.description: A unified or side-by-side diff. Takes parsed hunks rather than a patch string, with parseUnifiedDiff exported alongside for when you only have the text.
diff-view.usage:
import { DiffView, parseUnifiedDiff } from '@/components/ui/diff-view'

<DiffView
  file={{ path: 'src/lib/styles.ts', hunks: parseUnifiedDiff(patch) }}
  view="split"
/>

api.name: file
api.description: `{ path, previousPath?, status?, hunks }`. Additions and deletions are counted from the hunks rather than passed in, so the header can never disagree with the body.

api.name: view
api.description: Split pairs removals with additions positionally inside each hunk — what a side-by-side view actually shows, without a word-level diff algorithm.

api.name: collapsible / defaultOpen
api.description: Fold the file behind its header, for a review with many files.

api.name: parseUnifiedDiff
api.description: Parses standard unified-diff text, tracking old and new line numbers across hunks.

api.name: DiffViewList
api.description: Several files in one review, sharing a view mode.

terminal.label: Terminal
terminal.description: Console output with ANSI colour. Follow-tail sticks to the bottom only while the reader is already there, so scrolling up to read something is never undone by the next line.
terminal.usage:
import { Terminal } from '@/components/ui/terminal'

<Terminal title="npm run build" content={output} follow showLineNumbers />

api.name: content / lines
api.description: Raw output split on newlines, or the lines directly when you already have them.

api.name: follow
api.description: Stick to the bottom as output grows — but only while the reader is within a couple of dozen pixels of it.

api.name: showLineNumbers
api.description: Gutter numbering.

api.name: copyable / title
api.description: Header row with a copy button that reports back for a moment after copying.

api.name: ANSI support
api.description: Colour, bold, dim and reset. Cursor movement and screen clearing are dropped rather than half-implemented — honouring them needs a screen buffer, and this is an append-only transcript.

log-viewer.label: Log Viewer
log-viewer.description: Structured logs with level filters, search and counts. Matches are highlighted in place rather than filtering the list down, so a search shows where the hits are in context.

api.name: entries
api.description: `{ id, level, message, time?, source? }` with level one of debug, info, warn, error.

api.name: searchable
api.description: Filter box. The hit is marked inside the message.

api.name: filterable
api.description: Per-level toggles, each showing that level total so you can see what you are hiding.

api.name: locale
api.description: Formats timestamps through Intl.

json-viewer.label: JSON Viewer
json-viewer.description: A collapsible view of a parsed value. Collapsed nodes show their size, because "three entries or three thousand" is the question you have before expanding one.

api.name: value
api.description: A parsed value, not a string — re-serialising to re-parse loses everything that only exists in memory.

api.name: defaultExpandedDepth
api.description: How many levels start open.

code-search.label: Code Search
code-search.description: Search hits grouped by file, with the match marked inside its line. Ranges are clamped on render, because a wrong highlight is worse than none — it looks right.
code-search.usage:
import { CodeSearch } from '@/components/ui/code-search'

<CodeSearch files={files} query="controlSize" onOpen={openInEditor} />

api.name: files
api.description: `{ path, language?, matches }` where a match is `{ line, text, range? }`.

api.name: range
api.description: 0-based, end-exclusive, within the match text. Clamped on render so an off-by-one from a 1-based backend cannot silently mark the wrong span.

api.name: query
api.description: Fallback locator when a match carries no range.

api.name: onOpen
api.description: Makes each hit a button — jump to the file in an editor.

shortcut-sheet.label: Shortcut Sheet
shortcut-sheet.description: A keyboard reference grouped by area. Presentational by design — it never binds the keys, because the component that shows a cheat sheet is not the one that owns the handlers.

api.name: groups
api.description: `{ label, shortcuts }` where a shortcut is `{ keys: string[], label }`.

api.name: keys
api.description: The modifier chain stays data, so the same array can drive a matcher elsewhere rather than being re-parsed from a string.

api.name: columns
api.description: Two columns from `sm` up.

status-checks.label: Status Checks
status-checks.description: The CI check list on a pull request. The summary states the blocking outcome rather than the raw tally, because "3 failing" says nothing about whether you can merge.

api.name: checks
api.description: `{ id, name, status, description?, duration?, required?, detail? }`.

api.name: status
api.description: Each carries its own icon and colour, so the outcome never depends on colour alone.

api.name: required
api.description: Only required failures make the rollup say the PR is blocked; optional ones are labelled and counted but do not.

api.name: detail
api.description: Expandable body — a log excerpt, usually. Checks without one show no disclosure control.

test-results.label: Test Results
test-results.description: A test run with suites, tests and failure output. Failures expand by default and passes stay collapsed — nobody opens a report to read what passed.

api.name: suites
api.description: `{ id, name, tests }` where a test is `{ id, name, status, duration?, error? }`.

api.name: suiteStatus
api.description: Exported roll-up. Derived, so a suite cannot claim to pass while containing a failure.

api.name: error
api.description: Rendered under the test on a tinted ground — a Terminal, usually.

stack-trace.label: Stack Trace
stack-trace.description: A parsed exception with its frames. Library frames collapse behind a count — a stack is typically three frames of your code buried in forty of the framework’s.
stack-trace.usage:
import { StackTrace } from '@/components/ui/stack-trace'

<StackTrace name="TypeError" message={error.message} frames={frames} raw={error.stack} />

api.name: frames
api.description: `{ fn, file, line?, column?, app?, source? }`. `app: false` marks a library frame.

api.name: source
api.description: Excerpt shown when a frame is expanded, with the failing line marked. The first app frame opens by default.

api.name: raw
api.description: The original text, for the copy button.

blame-view.label: Blame View
blame-view.description: Every line attributed to the commit that last touched it. Consecutive lines from one commit collapse into a single gutter entry — a blame view that repeats itself hides where one commit ends and the next begins.

api.name: lines
api.description: `{ line, content, sha, author, date, summary? }`, in file order.

api.name: grouping
api.description: Runs of one commit share a gutter entry; the rest of the run is blank.

api.name: age ramp
api.description: Newer commits are hotter, so "old and stable versus new and suspect" is answerable without reading a date.

api.name: onSelectCommit
api.description: Each gutter entry is a button.

dependency-list.label: Dependency List
dependency-list.description: Packages with their update and vulnerability state. Severity outranks staleness in the sort, because ordering by how out of date things are buries a critical advisory behind forty patch bumps.

api.name: dependencies
api.description: `{ name, current, latest?, update?, dev?, vulnerability?, homepage? }`.

api.name: update
api.description: Derived from the version pair when omitted. Major versus patch is the difference between a sprint and an afternoon, so "12 outdated" is not the useful number.

api.name: updateKind
api.description: Exported. Returns null for anything unparseable rather than guessing.

api.name: sort
api.type: severity, then update size, then name
api.description: Fixed — this is a triage order, not a preference.

pull-request-card.label: Pull Request Card
pull-request-card.description: A pull request at a glance — state, branches, checks, reviewers. State is shown as an icon and a word, never colour alone.
pull-request-card.usage:
import { PullRequestCard } from '@/components/ui/pull-request-card'

<PullRequestCard number={412} title="Add squircle corners" state="open" />

api.name: number / title / state
api.description: open, draft, merged or closed.

api.name: branch / baseBranch
api.description: Rendered as a source → target pair.

api.name: additions / deletions
api.description: Passed through to DiffStat.

api.name: reviewers
api.description: Names, rendered as a stacked AvatarGroup.

api.name: checks
api.description: Slot for a StatusChecks summary or any other node.

api.name: updated
api.description: Shown as a relative time through Fmt.

demos.title: States
demos.code:
<PullRequestCard number={412} title="…" state="open" />
<PullRequestCard number={408} title="…" state="merged" />

review-thread.label: Review Thread
review-thread.description: A review conversation anchored to a line of code, with the line shown as context. Resolving is always a callback — a resolved thread is server truth other reviewers see.

api.name: path / line / snippet
api.description: The anchor. A thread detached from its line is unreadable, and re-finding that line is the main cost of reviewing in a browser.

api.name: comments
api.description: `{ id, author, body, time?, pending? }`.

api.name: resolved / onResolve
api.description: Resolution is never local state — it is shared truth, so the component only reports the intent.

api.name: onReply
api.description: Adds the reply box. Omit it for a read-only thread.

label-picker.label: Label Picker
label-picker.description: Coloured repository labels, picked from a searchable list. Chip text is derived from the fill by luminance, since a label set imported from a forge only gives you a background colour.
label-picker.usage:
import { LabelPicker } from '@/components/ui/label-picker'

<LabelPicker labels={labels} selected={selected} onSelectedChange={setSelected} />

api.name: labels
api.description: `{ id, name, color, description? }` where colour is any CSS colour.

api.name: selected / onSelectedChange
api.description: Controlled selection by id.

api.name: readableInk
api.description: Exported helper. Picks black or white from Rec. 709 luma — `color-mix` cannot answer "is this light or dark", and relative `oklch()` cannot branch.

api.name: LabelChip
api.description: The chip on its own, for rendering labels outside the picker.

release-list.label: Release List
release-list.description: A changelog as a document — each version an article with a real heading, so it can be linked to and navigated by heading. Never sorts, since "newest first" cannot be derived from semver once pre-releases exist.

api.name: releases
api.description: `{ version, date?, current?, tag?, notes?, sections? }`.

api.name: sections
api.description: Grouped bullets — Added, Fixed, Changed.

api.name: locale
api.description: Date formatting through Intl.

commit-graph.label: Commit Graph
commit-graph.description: The branch graph beside a commit list. Lanes are held by the commit each one is waiting for, which is what keeps a branch on a single vertical line instead of drifting sideways at every merge.

api.name: commits
api.description: `{ sha, message, parents, author?, date?, refs? }`, newest first.

api.name: parents
api.description: The first parent inherits the lane; each additional one opens a lane and draws the merge curve. A commit with two parents renders as a hollow node.

api.name: layout
api.description: One SVG per row rather than a single tall one, so rows keep ordinary DOM content beside the graph and stay selectable.

node-canvas.label: Node Canvas
node-canvas.description: A pannable, zoomable canvas of draggable nodes and the edges between them — the substrate for an agent pipeline, a retrieval chain or a build DAG. Nodes are real DOM, so you put your own components inside them.

api.name: nodes / edges
api.description: Positions are graph units, not pixels. A node carries a `type` naming its component and a `data` payload; nothing about how it looks lives in the graph, so it survives JSON.

api.name: nodeTypes
api.description: Your node components, by `node.type`. Write them as ordinary components — a form, a chart, a whole query builder — and the graph only carries the name. Declare the map at module scope: a component created during render is a new component type each time, which remounts every node and takes focus out of the field being typed in.

api.name: useCanvasNode
api.type: () => { node, selected, dragging, update, remove, connect }
api.description: Read at any depth inside a node. `update({ data })` writes the node back without a callback threaded down from the top, which is what lets a node own its own state.

api.name: interactive content
api.description: A press that lands on a control reaches the control, not the drag: inputs, buttons, switches, links, sliders and anything marked `data-nodrag` are skipped. Keys belong to the node only while the node itself has focus, so a space types, Backspace edits and the arrows move the caret. A scrollable region inside a node keeps its own wheel.

api.name: data-drag-handle
api.description: Mark a title bar with it and the policy inverts — only that strip drags the node. What a node whose whole surface is a form needs, because there is no leftover pixel to grab. Presence, not a selector prop: a selector that matches nothing produces a node that silently cannot be moved.

api.name: dragThreshold
api.description: A drag begins on movement, not on contact, and nothing is captured until then. That is what keeps a click a click, so a button inside a node fires and a slider keeps the pointer capture it took for itself.

api.name: onRemoveEdge
api.description: Detaching a connection. Hovering a wire reveals a × at its midpoint; it is a real button, so a keyboard reaches it too. Omit and edges are inert.

api.name: renderNode
api.description: Draws any node without a registered type. Still supported, and still the shortest path for a graph of one shape.

api.name: onNodesChange
api.description: Dragging and arrow-key nudges. Omit it and the canvas is read-only, though nodes stay focusable.

api.name: onConnect
api.description: Drag from a node’s trailing port onto another node — dropping anywhere on it counts, not only on the 12px dot. Also what makes the ports render at all. A self-link, a duplicate, and a target marked `connectable: false` are refused before you are asked.

api.name: isValidConnection
api.description: The domain rule on top of those. Whether a cycle is legal is yours to decide — a state machine wants them, a build DAG does not.

api.name: snapToGrid
api.description: Rounds to `grid` while dragging and nudging. The dots implied an alignment model the canvas did not have.

api.name: onAddConnected
api.description: The + on a node: create a step already wired to it. A real button, so chaining has a keyboard path even though dragging a wire does not.

api.name: onAddNode / onDropNode
api.description: Double-click empty canvas, and drops from NodePalette. Both receive graph coordinates, already corrected for pan and zoom.

api.name: onRemoveNode
api.description: Backspace or Delete with a node focused, unless the node sets deletable: false.

api.name: zoom / pan
api.description: Zoom is anchored to the pointer, so the point under the cursor stays put. minZoom, maxZoom, defaultPan and defaultZoom are all props.

api.name: keyboard
api.description: Every node is a tab stop; arrows nudge by `nudge` units and Shift by ten times that. Precise placement is easier this way than with a pointer. Keys are only the canvas’s while the node itself holds focus.

api.name: accessibility
api.description: Not `role="button"`. A button’s contents are presentational to a screen reader, so every field inside a node used to vanish from the accessibility tree — and a node whose body is a form is not a button.

api.name: touch
api.description: The viewport sets `touch-action: none` so a drag is never stolen by a scroll, and that intersects down the tree — so a scrollable region inside a node cannot be flicked with a finger, and there is no pinch-zoom. The wheel and the pointer paths are complete.

  edges={edges}
  nodeTypes={{ blank: BlankNode }}

/>

inspector.label: Inspector
inspector.description: The properties panel for whatever is selected — the other half of a canvas. Driven by a field schema rather than by children, because the fields change with the selection and writing that as JSX means a switch statement per kind at the call site.
inspector.usage:
import { Inspector } from '@/components/ui/inspector'

<Inspector sections={sections} value={node.data} onChange={updateNode} title={node.name} />

api.name: sections
api.description: { label?, fields }. Fields are text, textarea, number, boolean, select or readonly.

api.name: value / onChange
api.description: One onChange for the whole object, not one per field. A (key, value) callback pushes the merge onto every caller, and the merge is where the stale-closure bugs live.

api.name: title / description
api.description: Panel heading — usually the selected thing’s name.

api.name: emptyLabel
api.description: Pass an empty sections array alongside it.

api.name: accessibility
api.description: Every control is wired to its label and hint through Field’s context, so ids and aria-describedby are generated rather than hand-managed.

agent-card.label: Agent Card
agent-card.description: One agent’s definition as a card: the model behind it, the tools it may reach for, and whether it is allowed to run. Tools are listed by name rather than counted, because a count tells you nothing about blast radius.

api.name: name / description / model
api.description: The model id is shown verbatim — an agent’s behaviour is tied to the exact one, not to a family.

api.name: tools / maxTools
api.description: Listed by name. `delete_customer` in that list is what makes someone look twice; “6 tools” is not.

api.name: status
api.description: Kept separate from `enabled`: an agent can be switched on and still be failing, and folding the two hides that case.

api.name: enabled / onToggle
api.description: Renders the switch. Omit `enabled` entirely for a read-only card.

api.name: selected / onSelect
api.description: For a roster that drives a detail panel. The switch stops propagation, so toggling does not also select.

api.name: actions / icon
api.description: Trailing slot and the leading glyph — a menu, a Run button, an avatar.

api.name: statusLabels / toggleLabel
api.description: Every string is a prop.

tool-picker.label: Tool Picker
tool-picker.description: The catalogue of tools an agent may call, with a switch on each. Destructive capabilities are marked rather than hidden — the whole risk of an agent is a capability nobody noticed it had.
tool-picker.usage:
import { ToolPicker } from '@/components/ui/tool-picker'

<ToolPicker tools={tools} value={enabled} onValueChange={setEnabled} />

api.name: tools
api.description: { id, name, description?, group?, destructive?, disabled?, disabledReason?, meta? }.

api.name: value / onValueChange
api.description: Controlled — the caller owns the enabled set, because it is usually part of a larger form.

api.name: destructive
api.description: Puts a warning badge on the row. For anything that deletes, refunds or sends.

api.name: searchable
api.description: Matches name, group and description — people look for tools by what they do at least as often as by what they are called.

api.name: group
api.description: Headings, in the order the tools appear. Empty groups collapse rather than leaving a bare heading.

api.name: summary
api.description: Caption under the list. Counted from the data, so it cannot disagree with the rows.

tool-schema.label: Tool Schema
tool-schema.description: A tool’s parameter schema, rendered as something a person can read. Required, type and default get their own column, because those are the three questions anyone actually has about a parameter.

api.name: schema
api.description: Reads type, description, enum, default, required, properties and items. Other keywords are ignored rather than half-supported.

api.name: $ref
api.description: Deliberately. Following one means fetching or bundling a document this component cannot see; rendering an unresolved ref as an empty object would be worse than saying so.

api.name: defaultDepth
api.description: Levels open on first render. A deep schema fully expanded is the same wall of JSON in a different font.

api.name: name / description
api.description: Heading above the parameters.

api.name: requiredLabel / optionalLabel / emptyLabel
api.description: Every string is a prop.

run-controls.label: Run Controls
run-controls.description: The transport bar for an agent run: start, pause, step, stop, replay. Which buttons exist is derived from status, so the invalid combinations — running and paused, replay while live — cannot be expressed.
run-controls.usage:
import { RunControls } from '@/components/ui/run-controls'

<RunControls status={status} step={step} totalSteps={12} onPause={pause} onStep={stepOnce} onStop={stop} />

api.name: status
api.description: The single source of truth. The button set is derived from it rather than from a pile of booleans at the call site.

api.name: onStep
api.description: Only offered while paused — stepping means nothing from a running clock. It is what makes an agent debuggable: you see what it was *about* to do.

api.name: onStop
api.description: Available whenever anything is live, including while stopping. A wedged run is exactly when you need it and exactly when a disabled button traps you.

api.name: step / totalSteps / elapsed
api.description: Progress readout. `elapsed` is pre-formatted — this component does not own your locale.

api.name: children
api.description: Trailing slot — a model picker, a spend cap, a link to the trace.

agent-tasks.label: Agent Tasks
agent-tasks.description: The plan an agent is working from, as it works through it. Not a trace of what happened — a list of what it intends to do, which is what lets you see it heading somewhere wrong while there is still time to stop it.

api.name: tasks
api.description: { id, title, status, steps?, note? } where status is 'pending' | 'active' | 'done' | 'failed' | 'skipped'.

api.name: one active task
api.description: An agent reporting three tasks in progress has lost track of its plan. Later actives are demoted to pending rather than all being drawn live, which would hide the bug.

api.name: steps
api.description: Deliberately not a tree. A plan that needs deep nesting is a plan the agent will not finish.

subagent-tree.label: Subagent Tree
subagent-tree.description: The tree of subagents a run spawned and what each is costing. Cost aggregates up the tree — a parent that spent 400 tokens itself and fanned out to children that spent 90,000 is cheap by its own line and ruinous in total.

api.name: agents
api.description: { id, name, task?, status?, tokens?, duration?, children? }. `tokens` is that agent alone, excluding its children.

api.name: subtreeTokens
api.description: Exported. A node plus every descendant — the number that actually matters on a parent, and the one a per-node readout hides.

api.name: vs HandoffTrail
api.description: A handoff is one agent passing to the next. This is a parent fanning out to several at once; drawing that as a list loses who spawned whom.

trace-waterfall.label: Trace Waterfall
trace-waterfall.description: An agent run as a waterfall of spans. Bars are positioned against the whole run rather than each row’s own width, which is what makes concurrency visible — two tools that ran in parallel look identical to two that ran in sequence until you share the axis.

api.name: spans
api.description: { id, name, start, duration, kind?, error?, meta?, children? }. start and duration are milliseconds from the beginning of the run.

api.name: total
api.description: The run window. Defaults to the furthest span end, including nested ones.

api.name: kind
api.description: Drives the bar colour. An unknown kind falls back to neutral rather than throwing.

api.name: minimum bar
api.description: A span too short to draw still gets a sliver — “it ran and was instant” and “it never ran” must not look the same.

api.name: defaultDepth
api.description: Levels open on first render. Forty retrieval spans under one node are unreadable expanded.

api.name: formatDuration
api.description: Defaults to ms under a second, then seconds.

demos.title: A run with a parallel fan-out and a failure

stream-inspector.label: Stream Inspector
stream-inspector.description: A model’s token stream event by event, with the timing between them. An average tokens-per-second hides both numbers that matter — time to first token, and the stalls after it.

api.name: events
api.description: { id, at, kind, content? } where kind is 'start' | 'text' | 'tool' | 'thinking' | 'stop' | 'error'. `at` is ms from the start of the request.

api.name: stallMs
api.description: A gap longer than this is marked inline, in the sequence, where it can be traced to the event that caused it — usually a tool call the stream paused for.

api.name: collapseText
api.description: A stream is thousands of two-character deltas; a row each makes the tool-call boundaries impossible to find, which is the only reason to open this.

api.name: time to first token
