api.description: From the first text or thinking event, shown in the header.

demos.title: A stream that paused for a tool call

context-window.label: Context Window
context-window.description: What is in the context right now and how much room is left. Segments are drawn to scale against the window, not against what is used — a bar normalised to the used total always looks full, which is exactly backwards.
context-window.usage:
import { ContextWindow } from '@/components/ui/context-window'

<ContextWindow limit={200_000} reserved={8_000} segments={segments} />

api.name: segments / limit
api.description: { id, label, tokens, color? } against the model’s full window. Free space is the information, so the bar is scaled to the window.

api.name: reserved
api.description: Held back for the reply, drawn hatched as unavailable. Showing it as headroom lies about how much you can add.

api.name: warnAt
api.description: Fraction of the limit past which the readout turns destructive.

api.name: minimum segment
api.description: “The system prompt is small” and “there is no system prompt” must not look identical.

guardrail-list.label: Guardrail List
guardrail-list.description: The safety checks around a run and how each one landed, ordered by consequence rather than by execution. A skipped check is its own state — “we did not scan” and “the scan found nothing” are opposite facts.
guardrail-list.usage:
import { GuardrailList } from '@/components/ui/guardrail-list'

<GuardrailList guardrails={rails} summary={(c) => `${c.block} blocked, ${c.warn} warnings`} />

api.name: guardrails
api.description: { id, name, outcome, detail?, stage?, meta? }.

api.name: outcome
api.description: Five states, not three. Skipped and pending are distinct from passing, and collapsing them is how an unchecked output ships.

api.name: sorted
api.description: Worst first. A screen that buries the one blocked check among fifteen green rows is complete and useless.

api.name: summary
api.description: Tallies come from the data, so a summary cannot disagree with the rows under it.

api.name: outcomeLabels
api.description: Override any wording.

sandbox-policy.label: Sandbox Policy
sandbox-policy.description: The permissions an agent actually runs under — filesystem, network and process execution. Built to make the dangerous configuration look dangerous: an allow-list of `/` is functionally no sandbox, and it says so.

api.name: scopes
api.description: { id, kind: 'filesystem' | 'network' | 'exec', mode, allow?, deny?, enabled?, label?, description? }.

api.name: mode
api.description: Blocked, allow-list, or unrestricted. Only the middle one renders its allow list.

api.name: wide-open detection
api.description: `/`, `*`, `**`, `~` and `0.0.0.0/0` in an allow-list are flagged — they are “everything” wearing an allow-list costume.

api.name: deny before allow
api.description: Every real sandbox evaluates deny first. Showing the lists side by side invites the assumption that an allow entry re-opens what a deny closed.

api.name: no scopes
api.description: An empty policy renders as a warning: the agent runs with the host’s own permissions.

handoff-trail.label: Handoff Trail
handoff-trail.description: Who handled a request, in order, and why each handover happened. The hardest question in a multi-agent system is “why did this agent answer”, and the answer is never in one agent’s transcript — it is in the chain.

api.name: handoffs
api.description: { id, to, human?, reason?, at?, failed?, meta? }. `reason` is the point of the component — a chain without reasons explains nothing.

api.name: human
api.description: A handover to a person is a first-class hop, not a status field. Escalation is usually what the system is judged on.

api.name: failed
api.description: Marks a handover caused by a failure rather than by routing.

api.name: live
api.description: Marks the last hop as still holding the request, so a running trail does not read as finished.

api.name: at
api.description: Pre-formatted. This component does not own your locale.

agent-memory.label: Agent Memory
agent-memory.description: What an agent has remembered and where each piece came from. Distinct from retrieval: these are injected into every future run whether relevant or not, which is why a person has to be able to inspect and delete them.
agent-memory.usage:
import { AgentMemory } from '@/components/ui/agent-memory'

<AgentMemory entries={entries} onPin={pin} onForget={forget} />

api.name: entries
api.description: { id, content, source, at?, importance?, pinned?, kind? }.

api.name: source
api.description: Required in the type, not optional. A memory with no provenance cannot be audited, and an agent that has silently learned something wrong is exactly what this screen exists for.

api.name: pinned
api.description: Sorts first and is exempt from eviction — the things a person asserted, as opposed to what the agent inferred.

api.name: onForget
api.description: Deleting a memory is a normal operation, not an admin one.

budget-guard.label: Budget Guard
budget-guard.description: Spend and token caps against what a run has consumed. A soft limit warns and a hard limit stops — collapsing them into one bar is how a team ends up believing they have a spend cap when what they have is a notification.
budget-guard.usage:
import { BudgetGuard } from '@/components/ui/budget-guard'

<BudgetGuard budgets={[{ id: 'spend', label: 'Spend', used: 18_40, soft: 20_00, hard: 25_00 }]} />

api.name: budgets
api.description: { id, label, used, soft?, hard?, format?, note? }.

api.name: soft vs hard
api.description: Soft warns, hard stops. A hard limit is a wall on the track and turns the row destructive when passed; a soft one is a dashed threshold.

api.name: bar scale
api.description: So the length being read is “room left before it stops”. Scaling to the soft limit makes a run look finished with half its budget left.

api.name: no budgets
api.description: An empty list renders as “this run is uncapped”, not as an empty box.

demos.title: One budget past its warning threshold

retry-policy.label: Retry Policy
retry-policy.description: A retry policy and the attempts it produced. A policy shown alone reads as reasonable right up until you see it fired four times in ninety milliseconds — the attempt list is what proves the policy running is the one configured.
retry-policy.usage:
import { RetryPolicy } from '@/components/ui/retry-policy'

<RetryPolicy maxAttempts={4} baseDelayMs={500} factor={2} jitter={0.3} attempts={attempts} />

api.name: maxAttempts / baseDelayMs / factor / maxDelayMs
api.description: The policy. The projected schedule is computed from it, so a policy that would wait eleven minutes on its last attempt says so before anyone ships it.

api.name: jitter
api.description: Rendered as a range, not a point. A delay shown as “2s” hides whether jitter is configured at all — and without it a thousand clients retry in lockstep and turn one outage into two.

api.name: attempts
api.description: { attempt, at?, outcome, waitedMs?, error? }. The history that proves the configured policy is the one running.

prompt-diff.label: Prompt Diff
prompt-diff.description: Two versions of a prompt with what changed between them. Prompts are the source code of an agent and almost never treated that way — the reason a run regressed is usually a sentence somebody rewrote three days ago.

api.name: before / after
api.description: The two versions. Diffed by line.

api.name: algorithm
api.description: Deliberately simple. Prompts are short and edited in place; pulling in a diff library for forty lines would be the wrong trade for a kit that ships its source into other people’s repos.

api.name: context
api.description: Unchanged lines kept around each change. Longer runs collapse to a marker — the point of the view is the change.

api.name: summary
api.description: Optional caption under the diff.

demos.title: A prompt that grew two rules

eval-board.label: Eval Board
eval-board.description: Which model to ship, and what is still broken — as a ranking plus a case list rather than a grid. Chips carry their own model name, so there is no column header to align to and nothing that scrolls sideways at four models.
eval-board.usage:
import { EvalBoard } from '@/components/ui/eval-board'

<EvalBoard models={models} cases={cases} onSelectCase={openCase} />

api.name: models / cases
api.description: EvalCase is { id, name, description?, results } keyed by model id. A missing entry is “not run”, which is distinct from skipped.

api.name: why not a matrix
api.description: A column per model starts scrolling sideways at three, needs a sticky first column to stay readable, and turns every cell into a coloured block whose glyph is too small to carry meaning. A ranking plus labelled chips wraps at any width.

api.name: scores
api.description: From the results, never a prop. Skips and not-run are excluded from the denominator — a model is not penalised for a case that never ran against it.

api.name: partialWeight
api.description: What a partial earns when scoring.

api.name: flagUniversalFailures
api.description: A case no model passed is usually a broken test rather than four broken models — flagged inline as a badge, not as a sentence that doubles the row height.

api.name: onSelectCase
api.description: Makes each case row a button for drilling in. Omit and the rows are static.

tool-latency.label: Tool Latency
tool-latency.description: Per-tool latency and failure rate — the ops view of a tool fleet. Bars are drawn from p95, not the mean: a tool averaging 200ms that spikes to nine seconds one call in twenty is the one blowing your timeout, and the mean hides it.

api.name: tools
api.description: { name, p50, p95, calls, errorRate?, meta? }. Durations in milliseconds, errorRate as 0–1.

api.name: bar scale
api.description: Scaled across the set, so the worst row is the longest bar. Scaling each to its own maximum would draw every tool full and rank nothing.

api.name: errorThreshold
api.description: A threshold, not a gradient: above it is a problem, below it is noise, and a smooth ramp makes 0.4% and 4% look like neighbours.

api.name: sorted
api.description: Slowest p95 first. Sorts a copy — the caller’s array is never mutated.

demos.title: A fleet with one bad upstream

mcp-server-card.label: MCP Server Card
mcp-server-card.description: One MCP server: what it is, how it is attached, and what it brought with it. Leads with the transport and the actual command line, because a server named “filesystem” tells you nothing and `--root /` tells you everything.
mcp-server-card.usage:
import { McpServerCard } from '@/components/ui/mcp-server-card'

<McpServerCard
  name="filesystem"
  target="npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem /Users/ada/work"
  transport="stdio"
  status="connected"
  capabilities={{ tools: 8, resources: 214, prompts: 0 }}
  onReconnect={reconnect}
/>

api.name: target
api.description: The command line or endpoint, on its own full-width row, wrapping rather than truncating. The first version clipped it mid-flag — a card that claims one field matters most and then cuts it off is arguing against itself.

api.name: copyTarget
api.description: A copy button beside the command. Off for an endpoint nobody needs on the clipboard.

api.name: transport
api.description: How it is attached. Shown as a badge beside the status.

api.name: status
api.description: A failed server stays in the list — silently dropping it is how a client quietly loses half its capabilities with no indication why.

api.name: capabilities
api.description: Counted per kind, never totalled — forty resources is a search index; three tools might be a shell. Zeroes stay visible but dimmed, so an absent capability does not look like an unreported one.

api.name: alignment
api.description: Footers line up across a grid even when only some cards carry an error block — the usual way a card grid goes ragged.

api.name: error
api.description: Handshake or runtime failure, rendered prominently rather than as a tooltip.

api.name: onReconnect
api.description: Renders the retry. Stops propagation, so it does not also select the card.

demos.title: A fleet, one of them broken

mcp-server-picker.label: MCP Server Picker
mcp-server-picker.description: A catalogue of servers you could install. Installing one is running someone else’s code with your credentials, so the card leads with publisher and verification rather than with the blurb — which is written by the person asking to be trusted.
mcp-server-picker.usage:
import { McpServerPicker } from '@/components/ui/mcp-server-picker'

<McpServerPicker servers={catalogue} onInstall={(server) => showCommand(server)} />

api.name: servers
api.description: { id, name, publisher, description?, target?, verified?, installs?, tags?, installed? }.

api.name: provenance first
api.description: Publisher and verification sit above the description. The description is marketing copy from the party asking for trust.

api.name: installed
api.description: Hiding them makes the catalogue lie about what exists, and “which of these do I already have” is the second question anyone asks.

api.name: onInstall
api.description: A callback, not an installer. A catalogue that installs on click is a supply-chain problem with a nice UI — hosts usually show the command instead.

demos.title: Three verified publishers and one that is not

mcp-config-editor.label: MCP Config Editor
mcp-config-editor.description: The mcpServers config with the mistakes people actually make called out. The usual failure parses cleanly and the server silently never appears — the error is in the shape, not the syntax, so a JSON editor catches none of it.

api.name: servers
api.description: The mcpServers object. Rendered as JSON, inspected as a shape.

api.name: checks
api.description: No command or url; a bare command that only resolves from your shell’s PATH; a secret pasted inline; a filesystem server with no arguments, which usually means rooted at /.

api.name: inspectMcpConfig
api.description: Exported, so a save handler can run the same checks before writing the file.

api.name: advisory only
api.description: A config being edited is invalid most of the time. A component that refuses to render until it is valid is useless while typing.

mcp-roots.label: MCP Roots
mcp-roots.description: The roots a client has granted its servers — the closest thing MCP has to a permission boundary, and invisible in most clients. A root covering a whole home directory is drawn as a warning rather than as another grey row.
mcp-roots.usage:
import { McpRoots } from '@/components/ui/mcp-roots'

<McpRoots roots={roots} onAdd={add} onRemove={remove} />

api.name: roots
api.description: { uri, name?, servers?, readOnly? }. `servers` absent or empty means every connected server.

api.name: broad detection
api.description: `/`, a bare `~`, and `/Users/<name>` or `/home/<name>` cover everything a person owns. Exported so a save handler can check before granting.

api.name: scoping
api.description: A root granted to every server is a different fact from one granted to a single trusted server, and a flat path list cannot tell them apart.

api.name: no roots
api.description: Rendered as “servers can see nothing”, rather than as an empty box that could mean either thing.

mcp-capability-matrix.label: MCP Capability Matrix
mcp-capability-matrix.description: Which server provides which capability, and where two of them collide. MCP names are not namespaced by the protocol, so two servers exposing `search` is decided by your client’s merge order — silently. A per-server list can never show that.
mcp-capability-matrix.usage:
import { McpCapabilityMatrix } from '@/components/ui/mcp-capability-matrix'

<McpCapabilityMatrix servers={servers} capabilities={caps} resolve={(row) => row.providers[0]} />

api.name: servers / capabilities
api.description: CapabilityRow is { name, kind?, providers, description? }. More than one provider is a collision.

api.name: resolve
api.description: Which provider wins — usually your client’s merge order. The losers are marked Shadowed rather than looking equally available.

api.name: why a grid
api.description: The clash only exists across servers, so no per-server view can show it. That is the entire reason this renders a matrix.

mcp-resource-list.label: MCP Resource List
mcp-resource-list.description: The resources a server exposes, addressed by URI. The URI is always shown in full and is what search matches first — “SSH key” and file:///Users/me/.ssh/id_rsa are the same resource, and only one of them makes anyone look twice.
mcp-resource-list.usage:
import { McpResourceList } from '@/components/ui/mcp-resource-list'

<McpResourceList resources={resources} value={attached} onValueChange={setAttached} />

api.name: resources
api.description: { uri, name?, description?, mimeType?, server?, size? }.

api.name: value / onValueChange
api.description: Selected URIs. Omit both for a read-only catalogue — the rows stop being buttons rather than becoming inert ones.

api.name: searchable
api.description: Matches URI, name and MIME type, URI first.

api.name: showServer
api.description: Which server offered it — matters as soon as more than one is connected.

mcp-prompt-list.label: MCP Prompt List
mcp-prompt-list.description: The prompts a server offers, with the arguments each one takes. How much has to be filled in is visible without expanding, because that is what decides which prompt you pick.
mcp-prompt-list.usage:
import { McpPromptList } from '@/components/ui/mcp-prompt-list'

<McpPromptList prompts={prompts} onSelect={(p) => insertIntoComposer(p)} />

api.name: prompts
api.description: { name, description?, server?, arguments? } where each argument is { name, description?, required? }.

api.name: onSelect
api.description: Usually inserts the prompt into a composer. Omit to render the list read-only.

api.name: argument summary
api.description: Count and required-count sit on the collapsed row. A prompt needing three inputs and one needing none are chosen differently.

rpc-console.label: RPC Console
rpc-console.description: The JSON-RPC wire between a client and an MCP server. Requests and responses are paired by id, which is what produces the latency figure and what makes an unanswered request visible — the single most useful thing this view can show.

api.name: messages
api.description: { key, direction, method?, id?, kind?, payload?, error?, at?, durationMs? }. `key` is row identity — several messages share a JSON-RPC id.

api.name: pairing
api.description: An outbound request with no inbound response sharing its id is flagged “no reply”. A flat log renders that as an ordinary row.

api.name: notifications
api.description: They have no id by definition, so they are marked as their own kind rather than looking like an orphaned request.

api.name: onlyProblems
api.description: Errors and unanswered requests only.

demos.title: A handshake, a refusal and a request still in flight

tool-approval.label: Tool Approval
tool-approval.description: The consent prompt before a tool runs. The arguments are shown in full above the buttons, because “Allow issue_refund?” asks you to approve a function name — what matters is that it wants to move £3,400.
tool-approval.usage:
import { ToolApproval } from '@/components/ui/tool-approval'

<ToolApproval
  tool="issue_refund"
  origin="billing-mcp"
  destructive
  args={call.arguments}
  onDecide={(decision) => resolve(decision)}
/>

api.name: args
api.description: Rendered in full, above the buttons. This is the thing actually being approved; the tool name is the label on the envelope.

api.name: onDecide
api.description: Three outcomes, not two. “Always” is a standing grant and says what it will do next time rather than reading as a faster yes.

api.name: destructive
api.description: Puts the weight on the approve action rather than on cancel, so the emphasis matches the actual risk.

api.name: deny styling
api.description: Declining a tool call is always safe; running one may not be. Styling deny as the dangerous choice inverts that.

api.name: no auto-approve
api.description: There is no timeout and no default focus on approve.

tool-result.label: Tool Result
tool-result.description: What a tool actually returned, rendered by content type. An MCP result is a list of blocks that can mix text, images and embedded resources — JSON.stringify turns a returned screenshot into four thousand characters of base64.
tool-result.usage:
import { ToolResult } from '@/components/ui/tool-result'

<ToolResult tool="search_docs" content={result.content} isError={result.isError} durationMs={120} />

api.name: content
api.description: Blocks of { type: 'text' | 'json' | 'image' | 'resource' }. Each is rendered as what it is — an image is a picture, not base64.

api.name: isError
api.description: Part of the payload, not the transport: MCP reports tool failure with a successful response carrying isError. A UI that only styles transport errors shows a failed call as a success.

api.name: maxBlocks
api.description: Collapses the rest behind a disclosure.

api.name: copying
api.description: Those are the blocks anyone wants on the clipboard.

tool-diff.label: Tool Diff
tool-diff.description: What changed in a tool’s contract between two server versions, with breaking changes classified rather than just listed. Adding an optional parameter and making one required are both edits to `properties`; only one breaks every existing call.
tool-diff.usage:
import { ToolDiff } from '@/components/ui/tool-diff'

<ToolDiff tool="read_file" before={old.inputSchema} after={next.inputSchema} />

api.name: before / after
api.description: The two input schemas. Compared one level deep, which is where tool parameters live.

api.name: breaking rules
api.description: Removals, newly-required fields, type changes and removed enum values break. Additions, relaxed requirements and description edits do not.

api.name: type changes
api.description: Even integer → number. The caller is a model that was shown the old schema and will keep producing the old shape.

api.name: diffToolSchemas
api.description: Exported, so CI can fail a server upgrade that breaks a contract.

api.name: changes
api.description: Supply your own comparison instead of the built-in one.

demos.title: A server upgrade that breaks three things

schema-form.label: Schema Form
schema-form.description: A form generated from a JSON Schema, so a person can invoke a tool by hand. The counterpart to Tool Schema: that one explains the parameters, this one collects them — together they are how you test an MCP tool without writing a client.

api.name: schema
api.description: Handles the subset tool definitions actually use: string, number, integer, boolean, enum, and string arrays entered one per line.

api.name: nested objects
api.description: Deliberately. A generated form for a deep schema is worse than a JSON editor, and CodeBlock already is one.

api.name: validation
api.description: Submit is never disabled for missing fields. A dead button that will not say why is the worst version of a form — the missing names are listed instead.

api.name: busy
api.description: Disables every control while the call is in flight.

mcp-sampling.label: MCP Sampling
mcp-sampling.description: A server asking the client to run a model on its behalf. Sampling inverts the usual direction — the server sends the request, your model and your budget answer it — so the messages are shown verbatim before the buttons.
mcp-sampling.usage:
import { McpSampling } from '@/components/ui/mcp-sampling'

<McpSampling server="git" messages={request.messages} maxTokens={512} onApprove={run} onDeny={deny} />

api.name: messages
api.description: Shown verbatim, in the server’s order, above the buttons. A server you installed for file search can ask for a completion; unless the client shows it, nobody sees what was sent.

api.name: maxTokens
api.description: What the request will cost. Absent is flagged as unbounded rather than defaulted quietly.

api.name: approve styling
api.description: This is a server spending your budget on its own initiative. The emphasis belongs on reading it first.

demos.title: A server asking for a completion

mcp-elicitation.label: MCP Elicitation
mcp-elicitation.description: A server asking the user for structured input mid-run. Useful, and a good phishing surface — the prompt text is written by the server and appears wearing your client’s chrome, so the requesting server is named outside its own copy.
mcp-elicitation.usage:
import { McpElicitation } from '@/components/ui/mcp-elicitation'

<McpElicitation server="postgres" message={request.message} schema={request.schema} onSubmit={reply} />

api.name: server
api.description: Named at the top, outside the server’s own message. “Your session expired, re-enter your token” is indistinguishable from the client asking unless the client says who is asking.

api.name: credential refusal
api.description: A field named like a password, key, token, secret or seed phrase is stripped from the schema before the form is built, and the request is flagged. No legitimate elicitation needs one.

api.name: credentialFields
api.description: Exported, so a client can refuse the request outright rather than rendering it.

api.name: message
api.description: Untrusted text from the server. Rendered, never interpreted.

demos.title: A request that also asks for an API key

prompt-variables.label: Prompt Variables
prompt-variables.description: A prompt template with its slots filled in, beside the exact text the model receives. Variables are parsed out of the template rather than declared separately, so they cannot drift out of sync with it.
prompt-variables.usage:
import { PromptVariables } from '@/components/ui/prompt-variables'

<PromptVariables template={template} values={values} onChange={setValues} />

api.name: template
api.description: `{{name}}` marks a slot. The variable list is derived from this — there is no second list to fall out of step with it.

api.name: values / onChange
api.description: Controlled. Unfilled slots are highlighted in the preview instead of being silently interpolated as empty strings.

api.name: preview
api.description: The literal text that will be sent. A view that renders slots as chips is prettier and answers a different question.

api.name: multiline / multilineAfter
api.description: Which slots get a textarea, and the length past which one is chosen automatically.

prompt-versions.label: Prompt Versions
prompt-versions.description: A prompt’s history with what each change did to the score. The pairing is the point: a history without outcomes says what happened, a score chart without edits says something changed, and neither answers which edit made it worse.
prompt-versions.usage:
import { PromptVersions } from '@/components/ui/prompt-versions'

<PromptVersions versions={versions} onCompare={(a, b) => openDiff(a, b)} />

api.name: versions
api.description: { id, label, at?, author?, note?, score?, live? }. Newest first — order is preserved because position in the sequence is information.

api.name: deltas
api.description: Not against the best. Regression hunting walks backwards one step at a time; a delta against a distant high-water mark makes everything after it look equally bad.

api.name: live
api.description: Marked in place rather than sorted to the top — moving it hides how many versions have shipped since.

api.name: onCompare
api.description: Usually opens a PromptDiff between a version and the one before it.

few-shot-editor.label: Few-Shot Editor
few-shot-editor.description: The worked examples in a prompt, as editable pairs rather than one long string. Structured pairs can be counted, reordered, costed and switched off one at a time — a textarea holding six examples supports none of that.
few-shot-editor.usage:
import { FewShotEditor } from '@/components/ui/few-shot-editor'

<FewShotEditor examples={examples} onChange={setExamples} estimateTokens={estimate} />

api.name: examples / onChange
api.description: { id, input, output, disabled? }. Controlled.

api.name: disabled
api.description: Kept in the list, excluded from the prompt. “Does this example help?” is answered by toggling, not by cutting the text out and pasting it back.

api.name: reordering
api.description: Order carries weight with a model — recency inside the prompt matters — and two buttons work on a keyboard, by touch and in a screen reader, which a drag handle does not.

api.name: estimateTokens
api.description: Drives the budget readout. Counts only enabled examples.

token-inspector.label: Token Inspector
token-inspector.description: Text broken into tokens, so a prompt’s cost stops being a mystery number. Tokenisation is not words — `astralyx` is three tokens — and people shorten prose while a JSON blob below costs ten times more.
token-inspector.usage:
import { TokenInspector } from '@/components/ui/token-inspector'

<TokenInspector tokens={tokenise(prompt)} pricePerThousand={0.003} showIds />

api.name: tokens
api.description: Required. This component renders; it does not tokenise — real tokenisation needs the model’s vocabulary, a multi-megabyte table, and an approximation would produce numbers people quote in budgets.

api.name: limit
api.description: Tokens past this index are drawn as over the limit — for showing what a context ceiling would truncate.

api.name: pricePerThousand / formatCost
api.description: Turns the count into money.

api.name: whitespace
api.description: Spaces render as · and newlines as ↵. Whitespace is a token too, and an invisible one reads as a gap in the sequence.

prompt-input.label: Prompt Input
prompt-input.description: The composer for a chat: a growing textarea, attached context as removable chips, and a toolbar. Enter sends, Shift+Enter adds a newline, and IME composition is checked first.

api.name: value / onValueChange
api.description: Controlled and uncontrolled text.

api.name: onSubmit
api.description: Fires on Enter or the send button. Never fires while empty or busy.

api.name: busy / onStop
api.description: Swaps send for stop and blocks submission while a reply is streaming.

api.name: context
api.description: { id, label, icon?, detail? }, rendered as removable chips above the field.

api.name: toolbar
api.description: Leading toolbar slot — a context picker, a model select, an attach button.

api.name: maxLength
api.description: Budget. The counter only appears past 80%, and turns destructive at the limit.

api.name: keyboard
api.description: Send and newline. Composition events are checked first, so an IME confirming a candidate does not send.

demos.title: With context and a model picker

message.label: Message
message.description: One turn in a conversation. The two roles are shaped differently on purpose — a user message is a bubble, an assistant message is full-width prose, because a long answer in a bubble is unreadable.
message.usage:
import { Message } from '@/components/ui/message'

<Message role="user" name="Ada">How do the colour sets work?</Message>
<Message role="assistant" onRetry={retry} onVote={vote} copyText={text}>
  Every variant reads the same --ui-* set…
</Message>

api.name: role
api.description: Decides the shape: a trailing bubble, or full-width prose with an avatar.

api.name: actions
api.description: Copy, retry and vote row under the message.

api.name: copyText
api.description: What the copy button writes to the clipboard.

api.name: onRetry / onVote
api.description: Each adds its button only when provided.

api.name: MessagePending
api.description: The three-dot pulse, with role="status" and a screen-reader label — a purely visual animation says nothing about why the interface went quiet.

context-picker.label: Context Picker
context-picker.description: Picks what an assistant can see. A dropdown rather than a dialog, because attaching context happens mid-thought and a modal takes focus off the prompt you were writing.

api.name: sources
api.description: { id, label, group?, detail?, icon?, disabled? }

api.name: selected
api.description: Attached ids. Selected sources stay in the list with a tick rather than disappearing, so the menu does not reshuffle under the pointer.

api.name: onSelect / onDeselect
api.description: Attach and detach.

api.name: trigger
api.description: Replaces the default "Context" button.

tool-call.label: Tool Call
tool-call.description: One tool invocation inside an assistant turn. Collapsed by default — the arguments are long and the interesting part is that it ran — except a failure, which opens itself.
tool-call.usage:
import { ToolCall } from '@/components/ui/tool-call'

<ToolCall
  name="read_file"
  summary="src/lib/styles.ts"
  status="done"
  input={JSON.stringify(args, null, 2)}
  output={result}
/>

api.name: name
api.description: The tool identifier, in monospace.

api.name: status
api.description: A failure defaults to open, because that is the case you always want to read.

api.name: summary
api.description: Short line beside the name — the target, the query, the file.

api.name: input / output
api.description: Rendered in CodeBlocks, collapsed past 8 and 12 lines.

model-select.label: Model Select
model-select.description: Picks which model answers. A Select with the naming convention folded in, so "Opus · most capable" is scannable where a bare model id is not.
model-select.usage:
import { ModelSelect } from '@/components/ui/model-select'

<ModelSelect models={models} value={model} onValueChange={setModel} />

api.name: models
api.description: { id, name, note?, disabled? }

api.name: note
api.description: Capability or cost hint, joined to the name with a middot.

api.name: rest
api.description: Everything else forwards to Select — value, onValueChange, size, variant, error.

token-usage.label: Token Usage
token-usage.description: How much of a context window is spoken for. The colour crosses to amber at 75% and destructive at 90%, because the number only matters once it is close.

api.name: used / limit
api.description: Token counts. The share is clamped at 100%.

api.name: label
api.description: Text on the left.

api.name: showNumbers
api.description: The compact "18.4k / 200k" readout.

api.name: thresholds
api.description: Where the bar turns amber, then destructive.

suggestions.label: Suggestions
suggestions.description: Starter prompts, offered before the first message. Buttons rather than a list, because each one performs an action.

api.name: items
api.description: The prompts.

api.name: onSelect
api.description: Fires with the chosen prompt.

streaming-text.label: Streaming Text
streaming-text.description: Text revealed as it arrives, with a caret while it is still coming. Driven by elapsed time rather than a per-character interval, so it never drifts or dumps a backlog after a background tab.
streaming-text.usage:
import { StreamingText } from '@/components/ui/streaming-text'

<StreamingText text={answer} speed={240} onDone={scrollToBottom} />

api.name: text
api.description: The full string. Restarting the reveal is a matter of changing the `key`.

api.name: speed
api.description: Characters per second, measured against the clock rather than accumulated per frame.

api.name: streaming
api.description: False renders the whole string at once — for replaying a finished message.

api.name: onDone
api.description: Fires once when the reveal completes. Deliberately not a dependency of the animation, so an inline arrow cannot restart it.

api.name: reduced motion
api.description: Appears complete immediately under prefers-reduced-motion — the animation carries no information the text does not.

api.name: accessibility
api.description: A polite live region with aria-busy, so a screen reader hears the answer arrive instead of sitting in silence.

reasoning-block.label: Reasoning Block
reasoning-block.description: A model's intermediate reasoning, folded away by default — it is supporting evidence, not the answer, and a panel that opens itself pushes the answer below the fold.
reasoning-block.usage:
import { ReasoningBlock } from '@/components/ui/reasoning-block'

<ReasoningBlock duration={4.2}>
  The question asks about v4 specifically…
</ReasoningBlock>

api.name: streaming
api.description: Opens itself and shows a spinner while thinking is the only thing happening. A prop rather than something inferred from children, since that transition is the whole interaction.

api.name: duration
api.description: Seconds spent thinking, shown once finished.

api.name: defaultOpen
api.description: Defaults to whatever `streaming` is.

api.name: label
api.description: Header text once finished.

citations.label: Citations
citations.description: Numbered sources for a generated answer. A marker is a real anchor with an accessible name, because a bare superscript "3" is meaningless read aloud — exactly when checking a claim matters most.
citations.usage:
import { Citations, CitationMark } from '@/components/ui/citations'

Configuration moved into CSS.

api.name: citations
api.description: `{ id, title, url?, snippet?, source? }`.

api.name: CitationMark
api.description: The inline marker. `index` is 1-based to match the list, and the accessible name is "Source 3: <title>".

api.name: snippet
api.description: Shown in a hover preview. Everything it contains also appears in the list, since hover is not available to every reader.

api.name: anchoring
api.description: A citation without a URL links to its list entry by id, so the marker always goes somewhere.

api.name: scope
api.description: Namespaces the anchor ids. Two answers on one page each need their own, or both mint the same ids and the markers jump to the wrong list.

agent-steps.label: Agent Steps
agent-steps.description: An agent's plan with each step's state. The whole plan is shown from the start, including steps not yet reached — revealing them one at a time hides how much is left, which is what someone watching most wants to know.
agent-steps.usage:
import { AgentSteps } from '@/components/ui/agent-steps'

<AgentSteps steps={steps} title="Fixing the failing test" />

api.name: steps
api.description: `{ id, label, status, duration?, detail? }`.

api.name: status
api.description: Running shows a spinner; skipped strikes the label through.

api.name: detail
api.description: Expandable body — tool calls, output, an error.

api.name: relationship to ToolCall
api.description: ToolCall shows a single invocation with its arguments and result; this shows the sequence those calls belong to.

api.name: progress
api.description: The done-of-total counter is a polite live region, so completion is announced without stealing focus.

diff-proposal.label: Diff Proposal
diff-proposal.description: A model-proposed edit with accept and reject. The decision is reported, never applied — and once made, the actions are replaced by the outcome so a stale card cannot be clicked twice.

api.name: file
api.description: Same shape DiffView takes — use parseUnifiedDiff when you only have patch text.

api.name: rationale
api.description: Rendered above the diff. The reason for a change is what you read before deciding; after forty lines of diff nobody reads it.

api.name: decision / onDecide
api.description: Controlled or uncontrolled. The component never applies anything — it has no idea what your editor buffer is.

api.name: view
api.description: Passed through to DiffView.

model-comparison.label: Model Comparison
model-comparison.description: Two or more outputs side by side with a pick. Columns are equal width and height regardless of content, because a taller box reads as the better answer before a word of it is read.

api.name: outputs
api.description: `{ id, model, output, latency?, tokens?, cost?, badge? }`.

api.name: selected / onSelect
api.description: Controlled or uncontrolled pick.

api.name: responsive
api.description: Breakpoint the columns appear at. Below it they stack, where two columns would be too narrow to read.

api.name: metadata
api.description: Latency, tokens and cost sit below the answers — compared after them, not before.

confidence-meter.label: Confidence Meter
confidence-meter.description: How sure a model is, in five steps. Segmented on purpose — a smooth bar invites reading 0.834 as different from 0.851, which is not what a calibration score supports.

api.name: value
api.description: 0 to 1. Mapped to one of five bands.

api.name: label / showLabel
api.description: The band name is the accessible value too — a screen reader hears "high", not a percentage implying more precision than exists.

api.name: size
api.description: Segment height.

api.name: role
api.description: With aria-valuetext set to the band, since this is a measurement within a range rather than task progress.

feedback.label: Feedback
feedback.description: Thumbs up or down, with an optional reason. The rating sends on click and the comment is a separate follow-up — holding the rating hostage to a comment box is how feedback widgets collect nothing.

api.name: rating / onRate
api.description: Controlled or uncontrolled. Clicking the active thumb clears it, since the most common correction is having hit the wrong one.

api.name: onComment
api.description: Adds the comment box. Omit for rating only.

api.name: reasons
api.description: Quick-pick reasons offered after a thumbs down — one tap instead of a paragraph.

api.name: prompt
api.description: Leading text.

retrieval-results.label: Retrieval Results
retrieval-results.description: The chunks a retrieval step pulled, with relevance. Near-misses are dimmed rather than dropped — when an answer is wrong, "what did it nearly retrieve" is the useful question.
retrieval-results.usage:
import { RetrievalResults } from '@/components/ui/retrieval-results'

<RetrievalResults chunks={chunks} query={question} threshold={0.5} />

api.name: chunks
api.description: `{ id, score, content, source, page?, metadata? }` with score 0–1.

api.name: threshold
api.description: Below it a chunk is dimmed, never hidden.

api.name: scores
api.description: Rendered through ConfidenceMeter rather than as a number — a cosine similarity of 0.82 is not a calibrated probability.

prompt-template.label: Prompt Template
prompt-template.description: A prompt with {{variable}} placeholders and a form to fill them. Variables are parsed out of the template rather than declared separately, so the two cannot drift.
prompt-template.usage:
import { PromptTemplate } from '@/components/ui/prompt-template'

<PromptTemplate template={template} values={values} onValuesChange={setValues} />

api.name: template
api.description: Placeholders are `{{name}}`. Repeats of one name share a single input.

api.name: values / onValuesChange
api.description: Controlled or uncontrolled.

api.name: extractVariables
api.description: Exported, for validating a template before it is saved.

api.name: preview
api.description: Unfilled placeholders stay visible and highlighted — a prompt that quietly sends "Summarise  in  words" is worse than one that shows what is missing.

eval-results.label: Eval Results
eval-results.description: A model-versus-benchmark score matrix. The best result is marked per benchmark rather than overall — a model can lead on reasoning and trail on latency, and one winner badge hides that.

api.name: models
api.description: Column order.

api.name: benchmarks
api.description: `{ id, label, lowerIsBetter?, scores }` where scores maps a model to `{ value?, delta? }`.

api.name: lowerIsBetter
api.description: Flips which end wins and which direction of delta is good — latency and cost need it.

api.name: missing scores
api.description: A blank cell reads as zero, which is a different claim from "not run".

cost-breakdown.label: Cost Breakdown
cost-breakdown.description: Spend by model, with token volume beside it. The two routinely disagree — the cheap model handling 90% of calls is often 10% of the bill — and either number alone leads to the wrong optimisation.
cost-breakdown.usage:
import { CostBreakdown } from '@/components/ui/cost-breakdown'

<CostBreakdown rows={rows} period="August" budget={250} />

api.name: rows
api.description: `{ id, label, cost, inputTokens?, outputTokens?, calls?, color? }`. Input and output are kept apart because they are priced differently.

api.name: budget
api.description: Adds a budget line and flags an overage.

api.name: precision
api.description: Under a unit gets four decimals, larger amounts two. A per-call cost rounded to cents is all zeroes; an aggregate carried to four is noise, and the widest string the column has to hold.

api.name: column width
api.description: The currency prefix is locale-dependent — en-GB renders USD as "US$", three characters wider than en-US — so the amount column grows rather than clipping.

alert-triage.label: Alert Triage
alert-triage.description: An alert queue grouped by fingerprint. A flapping check fires two hundred times, and an ungrouped list buries every other alert underneath it — which is how real pages get missed.
alert-triage.usage:
import { AlertTriage } from '@/components/ui/alert-triage'

<AlertTriage alerts={alerts} onAcknowledge={ack} onSilence={silence} />

api.name: alerts
api.description: `{ id, title, severity, fingerprint?, count?, source?, firstSeen?, lastSeen?, acknowledged?, detail? }`.

api.name: fingerprint
api.description: Alerts sharing one collapse into a single row with an occurrence count. Falls back to the id.

api.name: onAcknowledge / onSilence
api.description: Report the ids of every member of the selected groups. Nothing is hidden optimistically — that would show two responders different pictures of one incident.

api.name: ordering
api.description: Critical first. Order within a group is the caller’s; only the roll-up is computed.

anomaly-chart.label: Anomaly Chart
anomaly-chart.description: A metric against its expected range, with outliers marked. The band is the point — 400ms at 03:00 may be an incident while 400ms at peak is Tuesday.

api.name: points
api.description: `{ value, expected?, label? }` where expected is a `[low, high]` pair for that moment.

api.name: detection
api.description: The component marks what falls outside the range you give it. It never invents a threshold of its own.

api.name: color / bandColor / anomalyColor
api.description: Any CSS colour.

api.name: rendering
api.description: The plot is stretched to fit its container; anomaly dots are drawn in a second, unstretched layer, since a circle inside that stretch would render as an ellipse.

root-cause-tree.label: Root Cause Tree
root-cause-tree.description: A causal chain from symptom to candidate causes, each with a confidence band. Built on Tree, so it inherits the keyboard model rather than growing a second one.

api.name: causes
api.description: `{ id, label, confidence?, detail?, children? }`, recursive.

api.name: confidence
api.description: 0 to 1, rendered as a band rather than a percentage — these come out of a correlation engine and are not calibrated probabilities.

api.name: defaultExpanded
api.description: Defaults to the top level.

api.name: keyboard
api.description: Arrow keys over visible rows, one tab stop for the whole tree.

runbook-steps.label: Runbook Steps
runbook-steps.description: Remediation steps, run one at a time and only in order. Offering "run" on step four while step two is untried invites exactly the mistake the runbook exists to prevent.
runbook-steps.usage:
import { RunbookSteps } from '@/components/ui/runbook-steps'

<RunbookSteps steps={steps} onRun={run} onSkip={skip} />

api.name: steps
api.description: `{ id, title, description?, status, confirm?, output? }`.

api.name: onRun / onSkip
api.description: Only the next unresolved step offers them, and nothing offers them while another step is running.

api.name: confirm
api.description: Per-step, because the step that restarts a database sits right beside the one that reads a log. Swaps the actions for an inline confirmation.

api.name: output
api.description: Result of a run — a Terminal, usually.

slo-budget.label: SLO Budget
slo-budget.description: An error budget and how fast it is burning. Shows the budget remaining rather than availability achieved — 99.4% against a 99.9% target sounds like a near miss and is a six-times overspend.
slo-budget.usage:
import { SloBudget } from '@/components/ui/slo-budget'

<SloBudget target={0.999} actual={0.9994} burnRate={0.6} />

api.name: target / actual
api.description: Ratios, not percentages — 0.999 and 0.9994.

api.name: burnRate
api.description: Multiple of the sustainable pace. "2.4×" answers "will we make it"; a raw percentage does not.

api.name: window
api.description: The period the budget covers, for the caption.

api.name: thresholds
api.description: Green, amber past three quarters spent, red once exhausted.

demos.title: Healthy and exhausted
demos.code:
<SloBudget target={0.999} actual={0.9994} burnRate={0.6} />
<SloBudget target={0.999} actual={0.994} burnRate={6.2} />

topology-map.label: Topology Map
topology-map.description: A service dependency graph with health. Laid out in dependency layers, not by a force simulation — during an incident nobody wants to re-find the database because the layout moved.

api.name: nodes
api.description: `{ id, label, status, dependsOn?, meta? }`.

api.name: layout
api.description: Deterministic: the same architecture renders in the same place every time, so the picture is worth learning.

api.name: cycles
api.description: Depth is computed with a visited set — service graphs have cycles, and a naive recursion over one hangs the tab.

api.name: edges
api.description: An edge takes the colour of the node it points at, so you follow the red to the cause.

on-call-schedule.label: On-call Schedule
on-call-schedule.description: A rotation across a window of days. Shifts are positioned proportionally rather than snapped to a day grid — rotations hand over at 09:00, and rounding shows the wrong person on call for most of two days.
on-call-schedule.usage:
import { OnCallSchedule } from '@/components/ui/on-call-schedule'

<OnCallSchedule shifts={shifts} start={weekStart} end={weekEnd} />

api.name: shifts
api.description: `{ id, person, start, end, layer?, color? }`. Layers become rows.

api.name: start / end
api.description: The window. Shifts are clipped to it rather than overflowing.

api.name: now
api.description: Draws the current-time marker and drives the "on call now" line.

api.name: on call now
api.description: The only question this is ever opened to answer — reading it off a bar chart during an incident is a poor trade.

money-input.label: Money Input
money-input.description: A currency field that reads and writes integer minor units. Money that has been through a float has already lost — the value that leaves this control is a whole number of cents.
money-input.usage:
import { MoneyInput } from '@/components/ui/money-input'

<MoneyInput value={cents} onValueChange={setCents} currency="USD" />

api.name: value / defaultValue
api.description: Minor units. `250` is $2.50, never `2.5`.

api.name: onValueChange
api.description: Fires with the integer value, or `undefined` when the field is cleared — which is not the same as zero.

api.name: currency
api.description: ISO 4217. Drives the symbol, its side, and the number of decimal places — JPY has none.

api.name: locale
api.description: Grouping and decimal separators. A German user typing `1.234,56` means 1234.56.

api.name: min / max
api.description: Minor units, clamped on blur rather than while typing, so you can still delete a digit.

demos.title: Round-tripping minor units
demos.code:
const [value, setValue] = useState(2450)

<MoneyInput value={value} onValueChange={setValue} currency="EUR" locale="de-DE" />

card-input.label: Card Input
card-input.description: Card number, expiry and CVC in one control, with brand detection and a Luhn check. Client-side validation catches the typo; it never claims the card is good.

api.name: onCardChange
api.description: Fires with `{ number, expiry, cvc, brand, valid }` on every keystroke. `valid` means the digits pass Luhn and the expiry is in the future — not that the card will authorise.

api.name: brand detection
api.description: From the issuer identification number, which also sets the expected length and the CVC length: Amex is 15 digits with a 4-digit code.

api.name: focus
api.description: Advances to expiry and then CVC as each segment fills, and steps back on backspace from an empty field.

api.name: security
api.description: The component holds the number in local state only, and never in a `name`d field that a form serialiser would sweep up.

payment-method.label: Payment Method
payment-method.description: Saved cards and accounts, with expiry warnings. A card expiring next month is the reason a subscription fails, and saying so before it does is the entire value of this list.
payment-method.usage:
import { PaymentMethodList } from '@/components/ui/payment-method'

<PaymentMethodList methods={methods} selected={id} onSelect={setId} />

api.name: methods
api.description: `{ id, kind, last4, brand?, expiry?, holder?, isDefault? }`. Only ever the last four digits — a full PAN has no business reaching a component.

api.name: expiry warning
api.description: Cards within 60 days of expiry are flagged, expired ones are marked and cannot be made default.

api.name: onSelect / onSetDefault / onRemove
api.description: Omit any of them to render that affordance not at all, rather than disabled.

api.name: now
api.description: Reference point for expiry, so tests are not time-dependent.

invoice-list.label: Invoice List
invoice-list.description: Billing history. Amounts are right-aligned and tabular, which is the whole reason this is not a generic list — a money column that does not line up cannot be scanned.

api.name: invoices
api.description: `{ id, number, date, amount, currency?, status, description?, url? }`.

api.name: currency
api.description: Not per list: an account that changed plan across a currency migration has both, and formatting the old ones with the new symbol is wrong in a way nobody notices until an audit.

api.name: status
api.description: Labelled badge, never colour alone.

api.name: url / onDownload
api.description: A URL renders a real download link; otherwise the callback fires.

payout-status.label: Payout Status
payout-status.description: Where a payout is and when the money lands. "Expected Thursday" is the thing people open this to find out; the status word alone never answers it.
payout-status.usage:
import { PayoutStatus } from '@/components/ui/payout-status'

<PayoutStatus amount={128_400} state="in_transit" expectedAt={date} />

api.name: amount
api.description: Minor units, matching LedgerTable, MoneyInput and Cart.

api.name: state
api.description: 'pending' | 'in_transit' | 'paid' | 'failed' | 'returned' | 'cancelled'.

api.name: expectedAt
api.description: The arrival date. Shown prominently for anything not yet paid, because it is the only question being asked.

api.name: failureReason
api.description: Shown for failed and returned payouts. A failure with no stated reason generates a support ticket every time.

ledger-table.label: Ledger Table
ledger-table.description: Double-entry lines with a running balance. Debits and credits get their own columns and are totalled separately, because a ledger where the two do not agree is the finding.

api.name: entries
api.description: `{ id, date, description, account?, reference?, debit?, credit? }`. Exactly one of debit or credit per line.

api.name: amounts
api.description: Integers throughout. Running balances accumulate, and a float error accumulates with them.

api.name: openingBalance
api.description: Minor units. The running balance starts here rather than at zero.

api.name: totals
api.description: Debit and credit columns are summed independently and shown in the footer, so an unbalanced set is visible rather than hidden in a net figure.

cart.label: Cart
cart.description: A basket with quantities and per-line totals. Stock limits are enforced at the stepper, not on submit — letting someone add a ninth of eight units and saying so at checkout is the worst possible order.
cart.usage:
import { Cart } from '@/components/ui/cart'

<Cart lines={lines} onQuantityChange={setQuantity} onRemove={remove} />

api.name: lines
api.description: `{ id, name, price, quantity, variant?, image?, max?, note? }`. Price is minor units per unit.

api.name: unit and line total
api.description: Once quantity exceeds one. Showing only the total makes it uncheckable; showing only the unit price makes the sum look wrong.

api.name: max
api.description: Caps the increment control and explains why in words underneath.

api.name: onRemove
api.description: Separate from decrementing, so reaching zero is never how something gets deleted.

api.name: quantity control
api.description: Not a free number field. A cart quantity is realistically 1–10, and a text input invites "12" where "1" was meant.

checkout-summary.label: Checkout Summary
checkout-summary.description: The order total, broken into its lines. A charge that is not yet known renders as "calculated at next step" rather than as £0.00 — showing zero for a charge you will apply is a promise you cannot keep.
checkout-summary.usage:
import { CheckoutSummary } from '@/components/ui/checkout-summary'

<CheckoutSummary subtotal={176_400} lines={lines} currency="GBP" />

api.name: subtotal
api.description: Minor units, before adjustments.

api.name: lines
api.description: `{ id, label, amount, note?, discount? }`. Every adjustment gets its own row — a total that silently folds in tax and shipping is the commonest cause of an abandoned basket.

api.name: amount: null
api.description: Renders as pending and marks the total as provisional.

api.name: total
api.description: From the rows shown, so it cannot disagree with them.

api.name: footer
api.description: Where the continue button goes.

demos.title: With a discount and an unknown charge

pricing-table.label: Pricing Table
pricing-table.description: Plans side by side. Every plan lists every feature, including the ones it lacks — omitting them makes the columns uneven and quietly hides what you would give up.

api.name: plans
api.description: `{ id, name, price, period?, currency?, description?, features, highlighted?, badge?, cta?, onSelect? }`.

api.name: features
api.description: `value` of true/false gives a tick or a dash; a string states a limit. Either way the row is present in every column.

api.name: highlighted
api.description: A border and a badge, never a size change — scaling one column up makes the others hard to read.

api.name: responsive
api.description: Breakpoint the columns appear at.

subscription-state.label: Subscription State
subscription-state.description: Plan, price and what happens next. A cancelled subscription with three weeks of access left is the case people most often get wrong, and a status badge alone never says it.
subscription-state.usage:
import { SubscriptionState } from '@/components/ui/subscription-state'

<SubscriptionState plan="Team" status="active" price={4900} renewsAt={renews} />

api.name: status
api.description: 'active' | 'trialing' | 'past_due' | 'canceled' | 'paused'. Each renders a different sentence, because each answers a different question.

api.name: endsAt
api.description: When access actually stops. For a cancelled subscription this is not the same as the renewal date, and conflating them is the bug.

api.name: trialEndsAt
api.description: Rendered as days remaining. "Ends 14 March" needs a calendar; "4 days left" does not.

api.name: past_due
api.description: The only state where a paying customer can lose access, and usually fixable in one click — so it gets a border and its own action.

api.name: price
api.description: Minor units per period. Whole amounts drop the decimals.

login-form.label: Login Form
login-form.description: Email and password, with somewhere for SSO buttons and an error. The error is announced, not just coloured — a failed sign-in that only turns red is invisible to a screen reader.
login-form.usage:
import { LoginForm } from '@/components/ui/login-form'

<LoginForm onSubmit={signIn} onForgot={reset} error={error} />

api.name: onSubmit
api.description: Called on submit with the two values. The form never navigates on its own.

api.name: error
api.description: Rendered in a live region above the fields and referenced by `aria-describedby`, so it is read on failure rather than merely seen.

api.name: providers
api.description: Slot for SSO or OAuth buttons, placed above the fields — where people who use them actually look.

api.name: loading
api.description: Disables the submit button and shows a spinner. The fields stay enabled, so a slow request does not eat a correction.

api.name: autocomplete
api.description: `username` and `current-password`, which is what lets a password manager fill both in one gesture.

demos.title: With SSO providers and a failure
demos.code:
<LoginForm
  error="Those credentials did not match an account."
  providers={<><Button variant="secondary">GitHub</Button><Button variant="secondary">Google</Button></>}
  onForgot={() => navigate('/reset')}
/>

two-factor-setup.label: Two-Factor Setup
two-factor-setup.description: Scan, verify, save recovery codes. The recovery step is a step, not a footnote: an authenticator lost with no codes saved is an account lost, and burying them behind a link is why that happens.
two-factor-setup.usage:
import { TwoFactorSetup } from '@/components/ui/two-factor-setup'

<TwoFactorSetup step={step} onStepChange={setStep} secret={secret} recoveryCodes={codes} />

api.name: step
api.description: 'scan' | 'verify' | 'recovery' | 'done'. Controlled, because enrolment usually spans a server round-trip.

api.name: secret
api.description: Base32, shown for manual entry with a copy button. A QR code is unreadable on the device displaying it.

api.name: recoveryCodes
api.description: Shown once, with copy and download. The step cannot be completed without an explicit acknowledgement that they are saved.

api.name: onVerify
api.description: Called with the six digits. Advancing is yours to decide — the component never assumes success.

api.name: qr
api.description: Your rendered QR. The kit does not ship a QR encoder for one screen.

demos.title: Full enrolment flow
demos.code:
const [step, setStep] = useState('scan')

<TwoFactorSetup step={step} onStepChange={setStep} secret={secret} recoveryCodes={codes} onVerify={verify} />

session-list.label: Session List
session-list.description: Active sign-ins, with the current one pinned and unrevokable from here. Signing yourself out of the session you are using is a footgun, so it is simply not offered.
session-list.usage:
import { SessionList } from '@/components/ui/session-list'

<SessionList sessions={sessions} onRevoke={revoke} onRevokeOthers={revokeAll} />

api.name: sessions
api.description: `{ id, device, browser?, os?, ip?, location?, lastActive?, current?, suspicious? }`.

api.name: current
api.description: Pins the session to the top and hides its revoke control.

api.name: suspicious
api.description: Your judgement, not the component's — it renders the marker, it does not decide what is suspicious.

api.name: onRevokeOthers
api.description: The "sign out everywhere" action. This is what someone reaching this screen after a scare actually wants.

api.name: location
api.description: Labelled as approximate. IP geolocation is routinely a hundred miles out, and presenting it as fact leads people to dismiss a real intrusion.

device-list.label: Device List
device-list.description: Devices trusted to skip the second factor, and when that trust lapses. A grant that expires in three days is worth seeing before you are asked for a code at an airport.

api.name: devices
api.description: `{ id, name, kind, os?, addedAt?, lastSeen?, trustedUntil?, current? }`.

api.name: trustedUntil
api.description: Expiry of the trust grant. Shown as a countdown while near, and marked expired once past — an expired grant is not a revoked device.

api.name: onRevoke
api.description: Omit to render a read-only list.

api.name: now
api.description: Reference for every relative time, so snapshots do not drift.

permission-matrix.label: Permission Matrix
permission-matrix.description: Roles against permissions, in a grid. Inherited grants are drawn differently from direct ones, because "why can this role still delete things" is the question a flat list of ticks cannot answer.
permission-matrix.usage:
import { PermissionMatrix } from '@/components/ui/permission-matrix'

<PermissionMatrix permissions={permissions} roles={roles} onToggle={toggle} />

api.name: permissions
api.description: `{ id, label, group?, description? }`. Groups become labelled row sections.

api.name: roles
api.description: `{ id, label, granted, inherited?, locked? }` — one column each.

api.name: inherited
api.description: Held via implication. Rendered distinctly and not directly revocable, because revoking it here would silently do nothing.

api.name: locked
api.description: For a role that cannot be edited at all — an Owner that must keep every permission.

api.name: onToggle
api.description: Omit for a read-only matrix, which is the right thing for a permissions reference page.

api-keys.label: API Keys
api-keys.description: Credentials, listed and revocable. A key is shown in full exactly once — after that only the prefix and last four, because a list that can reveal every key means a session holds every secret.

api.name: keys
api.description: `{ id, name, prefix, last4, created, lastUsed?, scopes?, secret? }`.

api.name: secret
api.description: Present only for a key just created. Its absence is what makes older keys unrevealable rather than a UI choice.

api.name: onRevoke
api.description: Confirmed inline beside the key — a modal with the list hidden behind it is how the wrong key gets revoked.

risk-score.label: Risk Score
risk-score.description: A score with the signals that produced it. The factors are the component, not a detail beside it — an analyst cannot approve or decline on "82", and an unexplained score is the one thing a regulator will ask you to justify.

api.name: score
api.description: Clamped to `max`. Yours to compute — the component scores nothing.

api.name: factors
api.description: `{ label, weight, detail? }`. Negative weights are mitigations and render in the positive tone.

api.name: bands
api.description: Thresholds and their names. Every band is labelled in words as well as coloured, because this ends up screenshotted into tickets and printed into case files.

api.name: bar scale
api.description: Factor bars are drawn against the largest contributor, not against 100, so five small signals still show their shape.

api.name: role
api.description: With `aria-valuetext` carrying both the number and the band name.

demos.title: A high score and a low one

fraud-verdict.label: Fraud Verdict
fraud-verdict.description: The decision at the end of a review: what was decided, on what basis, by whom. A settled verdict offers to reopen rather than accept a second one, because two conflicting verdicts on one case is the failure this shape prevents.
fraud-verdict.usage:
import { FraudVerdict } from '@/components/ui/fraud-verdict'

<FraudVerdict verdict="declined" reasons={reasons} decidedBy="A. Okafor" decidedAt={at} />

api.name: verdict
api.description: 'approved' | 'declined' | 'review' | 'pending'. Pending shows the actions; anything else shows who decided and when.

api.name: automated
api.description: Distinguishes a rule or model from a colleague. An analyst overriding a decision needs to know which they are disagreeing with.

api.name: reasons
api.description: Listed, not summarised. These get quoted in appeals and chargeback responses, and a paraphrase is not quotable.

api.name: onReopen
api.description: The only way past a settled verdict, so a case cannot quietly acquire two.

api.name: actions
api.description: Rendered only while pending.

ip-cluster.label: IP Cluster
ip-cluster.description: Accounts grouped by a shared address or device. The shape is the finding: one node fanning out to eight accounts is multi-accounting, eight accounts each on their own address is a shared ISP.

api.name: clusters
api.description: `{ id, value, kind?, network?, location?, members }`. Sorted largest-first, because this is a queue and the worst cluster belongs at the top.

api.name: network
api.description: Weighs the evidence. Carrier-grade NAT puts thousands of unrelated subscribers behind one mobile address — the label is what stops someone banning an apartment block.

api.name: members[].focus
api.description: Marks the account under review so it stands out inside its own cluster.

api.name: onSelect
api.description: Makes members real buttons. Omit for a read-only view.

fingerprint-diff.label: Fingerprint Diff
fingerprint-diff.description: Two device fingerprints, with only the differing attributes shown. The question is never what a device looks like — it is what changed between two sessions, and twenty-eight matching rows hide the two that matter.
fingerprint-diff.usage:
import { FingerprintDiff } from '@/components/ui/fingerprint-diff'

<FingerprintDiff attributes={attributes} leftLabel="Session A" rightLabel="Session B" />

api.name: attributes
api.description: `{ key, label?, left, right, significance? }`.

api.name: missing values
api.description: A `null` renders as "not reported", never as blank. A fingerprint that stopped reporting its canvas hash is itself a signal — usually an anti-detect browser.

api.name: significance
api.description: Marks the attributes worth escalating on. A changed timezone is not a changed WebGL vendor.

api.name: defaultShowMatching
api.description: Matching rows are collapsed behind a count, and always reachable.

date-range-compare.label: Date Range Compare
date-range-compare.description: A metric against the same metric last period, with the basis named. "+18%" is meaningless until you know against what — and against a partial period it is meaningless full stop.
date-range-compare.usage:
import { DateRangeCompare } from '@/components/ui/date-range-compare'

<DateRangeCompare label="Revenue" value={82_400} previous={71_900} basis="previous" />

api.name: value / previous
api.description: The two figures. The delta and its percentage are computed here, so they cannot disagree with the numbers shown.

api.name: basis
api.description: 'previous' | 'year' | 'custom' — spelled out in words beside the delta, never left implicit.

api.name: partial
api.description: Marks a range still in progress and mutes the delta. Nine days of a month against a full month is the most common dashboard falsehood there is.

api.name: goodDirection
api.description: Which way is good. Churn falling is green; use `none` for a metric with no better direction.

api.name: history
api.description: Optional sparkline. Shape often explains a delta that the single number cannot.

demos.title: Up and down against the previous period

cohort-table.label: Cohort Table
cohort-table.description: Retention by signup period, as a triangle. Cells are shaded by rate rather than by count, so a small cohort that retains well is not washed out by a large one that does not.

api.name: cohorts
api.description: `{ label, size, values }` where `values[0]` is the cohort period. Later periods may be missing — a cohort three months old has no month-six figure yet.

api.name: missing vs zero
api.description: A `null` renders as an empty cell, never as 0%. Drawing "not yet measured" as total churn is the classic cohort-chart lie.

api.name: periods
api.description: Columns rendered. Rows shorter than this end where their data does.

api.name: periodLabel
api.description: For weeks, days, or whatever the cohort period actually is.

api.name: shading
api.description: Each cell is a share of its own cohort size, so rows are comparable across wildly different cohort sizes.

ab-test-results.label: A/B Test Results
ab-test-results.description: Variants with lift, a confidence interval and a two-proportion z-test — plus the peeking warning, because stopping at the first significant reading is the failure that actually happens.

api.name: variants
api.description: { id, name, visitors, conversions, control? }. Exactly one should be the baseline.

api.name: the interval
api.description: "+12% lift" is not a result. "+12%, 95% CI [−3%, +27%]" is, and it says the opposite. Printing the point estimate alone manufactures certainty people ship on.

api.name: the maths
api.description: Pooled standard error for the p-value, unpooled for the interval — the standard pair, and why the interval can straddle zero while p sits just under 0.05.

api.name: the CI scale
api.description: The z-test gives an interval for the absolute difference in rates. Printed beside a relative lift it gets read as bounding that lift, which it does not — so it is divided by the control rate (the first-order delta-method interval), and the two columns are in the same units.

api.name: thin data
api.description: The normal approximation needs roughly ten conversions and ten non-conversions per arm. Below that it says "too few" rather than computing on data too thin to carry it.

api.name: targetSample
api.description: Enables the peeking warning. A fixed-horizon test read continuously is wrong far more often than its nominal alpha.

api.name: what it cannot tell you
api.description: Whether the metric is the one that matters, whether assignment was random, and whether the effect is worth the change.

retention-curve.label: Retention Curve
retention-curve.description: What fraction of each cohort is still here, period by period — normalised so growth cannot hide churn. Later cohorts are drawn shorter, not padded with zeroes.

api.name: cohorts
api.description: { name, size?, values }. Values are fractions of the cohort’s own starting size, so period 0 is always 1.

api.name: why not active users
api.description: Total actives rises while retention collapses, as long as acquisition outruns churn — which is what a business looks like just before it stops working.

api.name: flattening
api.description: A curve decaying to a horizontal asymptote means a stable core formed; one still falling at the right edge means there is no floor yet. That shape, not the day-1 number.

api.name: short cohorts
api.description: Padding unobserved periods with zeroes reads as catastrophic churn. It is the most common way this chart lies.

api.name: flattenThreshold
api.description: Period-over-period drop below which the curve counts as flat.

event-stream.label: Event Stream
event-stream.description: A live tail of analytics events with their payloads — the tool for debugging the tracking itself. Autoscroll pauses when you scroll away and the list is capped rather than unbounded.

api.name: events
api.description: { id, name, at, properties?, kind?, user? }. Newest first.

api.name: what it is for
api.description: Funnels show what was recorded; this shows what is arriving, with its payload — the only way to answer "did that click fire the event, and was it right" without a network panel.

api.name: autoscroll
api.description: A stream that yanks you to the newest row makes reading any event impossible. It follows only while you are already at the top.

api.name: limit
api.description: An unbounded live list is a memory leak with a UI. Dropped rows are counted, not silently forgotten.

api.name: aria-live
api.description: Announcing every arriving event makes a screen reader unusable. The count is announced politely instead.

segment-builder.label: Segment Builder
segment-builder.description: Build an audience from conditions, with precedence shown as nesting rather than implied by a word — and the output a structure, not a concatenated string.
segment-builder.usage:
import { SegmentBuilder } from '@/components/ui/segment-builder'

<SegmentBuilder fields={fields} value={segment} onChange={setSegment} />

api.name: value
api.description: Nested groups of conditions, each with one join. Not a string — so it compiles to SQL or an API filter with values still separated from operators, which is what keeps it parameterisable rather than concatenated.

api.name: precedence
api.description: "A or B and C" means two different audiences depending on how it binds. The join is set once at the head of a group and echoed read-only between its rows, so the box you see is the parse tree — a dropdown on every line is what makes a flat builder ambiguous.

api.name: nesting
api.description: The boundary of a group carries the precedence, so it is drawn as a filled box that deepens with depth rather than a margin you have to measure by eye.

api.name: incomplete rows
api.description: A condition with no value is a half-written thought. Treating it as absent means the segment quietly matches more people than the author believes — expensive for a marketing send.

api.name: fields
api.description: { key, label, type?, options?, operators? }. The type picks the operator list and the value control; `operators` replaces that list when the caller knows more than a type name conveys — a SQL dialect with ILIKE, a metric with a percentile comparison.

api.name: arity
api.description: "Is one of" was in the operator list from the start, rendered as a single select — which quietly made it a synonym for "is". A `many` operator now takes a list through [[tag-input]], and switching between arities clears the side that no longer applies rather than leaving a stale value to widen the segment later.

api.name: estimate
api.description: Supplied by the caller — only your backend knows how many people match.

demos.title: Team plans in DE or FR

attribution.label: Attribution
attribution.description: Credit for a conversion split across touchpoints, with the model as a control rather than a buried setting — because the disagreement between models is the whole finding.

api.name: journeys
api.description: { id, touchpoints: [{ channel, at }], value? }. Raw paths — the models are computed here.

api.name: the model is a control
api.description: Last-touch says paid search won; first-touch says the blog did; linear says everyone helped. Same journeys — the disagreement is entirely in the rule, and a number without its model is a claim dressed as a measurement.

api.name: five models
api.description: Time decay uses a configurable half-life; position based is 40/20/40 across first, middle and last.

api.name: not causal
api.description: Every model divides credit among touchpoints that were present. None establishes cause, and none can see the channels that never got a click — that is incrementality testing.

api.name: what it does show
api.description: A channel whose share collapses when you change the rule was never really driving conversions.

demos.title: Switch the model, watch the winner change

audit-log.label: Audit Log
audit-log.description: Who did what to which thing, when. Denied and errored attempts are kept and marked rather than filtered out — a log of successes only tells you nothing about the attack you are looking for.

api.name: events
api.description: `{ id, actor, action, target?, at, ip?, outcome?, detail? }`. The action is a verb, so a row reads as a sentence.

api.name: outcome
api.description: Marked, never filtered. A denied attempt is often the most interesting row on the page.

api.name: detail
