api.description: Anything structured — a before/after pair, a payload. Rendered as an expandable JSON view, collapsed by default.

api.name: searchable
api.description: Filters across actor, action and target at once. Which field a term belongs to is not something the reader should have to decide.

api.name: timestamps
api.description: Relative for scanning, exact on hover and in the `<time>` element — an audit log with only "2 hours ago" is not evidence.

moderation-queue.label: Moderation Queue
moderation-queue.description: Reported content with its report reasons and a decision. Sensitive items are blurred until revealed, because a moderator should choose when to look at the worst thing in the queue.
moderation-queue.usage:
import { ModerationQueue } from '@/components/ui/moderation-queue'

<ModerationQueue items={items} onDecide={decide} onBulkDecide={decideMany} />

api.name: items
api.description: `{ id, author, content, sensitive?, reportedAt, reportCount?, reasons?, status? }`.

api.name: sensitive
api.description: Blurs the content behind a reveal. The reason and report count stay visible, which is often enough to decide without looking.

api.name: reasons
api.description: Reason to count. Fourteen spam reports and one harassment report are a different case from the reverse.

api.name: onDecide
api.description: 'approve' | 'remove' for one item.

api.name: onBulkDecide
api.description: Enables selection. Omit it and each item is decided on its own, which is right for a small, high-stakes queue.

bulk-action-bar.label: Bulk Action Bar
bulk-action-bar.description: The bar that appears once rows are selected. It states the count in words next to the destructive button, because "Delete" and "Delete 4,812 records" deserve different amounts of hesitation.
bulk-action-bar.usage:
import { BulkActionBar } from '@/components/ui/bulk-action-bar'

<BulkActionBar count={selected.length} onClear={clear}>
  <Button size="sm" variant="colored" color="destructive">Delete</Button>
</BulkActionBar>

api.name: count
api.description: Selected rows. At zero the bar renders nothing at all rather than an empty shell.

api.name: onClear
api.description: Deselect everything. Always reachable — a selection you cannot escape is a trap.

api.name: children
api.description: The actions. Put the destructive one last, and let it say what it will destroy.

api.name: floating
api.description: Overlays the content instead of taking layout space, for a long table where the bar should follow the reader.

api.name: announcement
api.description: The count is announced on change, so a keyboard user selecting rows knows how many they have.

thread-list.label: Thread List
thread-list.description: An inbox of conversations. Unread is carried by weight and a count, not by colour alone, and the timestamp coarsens with age — a message from March does not need a clock time.
thread-list.usage:
import { ThreadList } from '@/components/ui/thread-list'

<ThreadList threads={threads} selected={id} onSelect={setId} />

api.name: threads
api.description: `{ id, title, preview?, fromMe?, at?, unread?, participants?, attachments?, muted? }`.

api.name: unread
api.description: A count, not a boolean. Two unread and forty unread are different situations, and the badge is what makes the row legible in monochrome.

api.name: fromMe
api.description: Prefixes the preview with "You:", which is how you tell "they replied" from "you are waiting" at a glance.

api.name: muted
api.description: Dims the row and suppresses the unread emphasis without hiding the count.

api.name: timestamps
api.description: Time today, weekday this week, date beyond that. Precision that stops being useful stops being shown.

demos.title: Selectable inbox
demos.code:
const [selected, setSelected] = useState('t1')

<ThreadList threads={threads} selected={selected} onSelect={setSelected} />

ticket-card.label: Ticket Card
ticket-card.description: A support ticket with its SLA. Breach risk is computed from the due time, not from how old the ticket is — a two-week ticket with a monthly SLA is fine, and an hour-old one may not be.
ticket-card.usage:
import { TicketCard } from '@/components/ui/ticket-card'

<TicketCard id="#4821" subject="Refund not received" status="open" priority="high" dueAt={due} />

api.name: status / priority
api.description: Separate axes. An urgent ticket that is resolved is not the same as a normal one that is open, and one badge cannot say both.

api.name: dueAt
api.description: The SLA target. Approaching and breached states are derived from it; age alone never triggers a warning.

api.name: requester / assignee
api.description: Unassigned is stated in words rather than left blank — an empty slot reads as a rendering bug.

api.name: replies
api.description: Reply count. A ticket with no replies and a passing SLA is the one to pick up.

typing-indicator.label: Typing Indicator
typing-indicator.description: Who is currently typing. The animation is decorative and hidden from assistive tech; the sentence beside it is the actual content, and it is what gets announced.

api.name: names
api.description: Empty renders nothing. One and two are named; three or more collapse to "several people", because a list of five names is longer than the messages.

api.name: showAvatars
api.description: Stacked avatars instead of names, for a narrow column.

api.name: motion
api.description: The dots stop animating under `prefers-reduced-motion`; the text stays, since it carried the meaning all along.

api.name: announcement
api.description: A live region set to polite, so it never interrupts a message being read.

attachment-preview.label: Attachment Preview
attachment-preview.description: A file chip with an icon chosen from the MIME type. Never from the extension: a `.dat` that is really a PDF should show a PDF, and a `.pdf` that is really an executable should not.
attachment-preview.usage:
import { AttachmentPreview } from '@/components/ui/attachment-preview'

<AttachmentPreview attachment={file} onRemove={remove} onDownload={download} />

api.name: attachment
api.description: `{ id, name, type?, size?, url?, thumbnail?, progress?, error? }`.

api.name: icon
api.description: Chosen from `type`, falling back to the extension only when no type is given.

api.name: progress
api.description: 0–1 while uploading. Omit once complete; a bar stuck at 100% is indistinguishable from one that stalled.

api.name: name
api.description: The extension is preserved when the name is trimmed, since it is the most informative part of a long filename.

api.name: compact
api.description: A single-line chip for an inline message, rather than a card in a list.

image.label: Image
image.description: An img that reserves its space, covers its own load with a skeleton, shimmer or blurred thumbnail, builds a srcset from a list of widths, and renders a fallback in the same box when the URL is dead.

api.name: src / alt
api.description: alt is required, deliberately. An image with no alt is either meaningful and unreadable, or decorative and should say so — pass alt="" for the second, which is a decision rather than an omission.

api.name: mask
api.description: What fills the frame until the image decodes. blur needs blurSrc and degrades to skeleton without it.

api.name: blurSrc
api.description: A tiny inline stand-in, blurred and scaled up under the real image. Worth it for generated images, which arrive slowly and often after their own preview.

api.name: widths / srcFor / sizes
api.description: Builds a srcset. The browser picks using sizes, the viewport and the device pixel ratio — facts this component does not have. srcFor defaults to a ?w= parameter.

api.name: ratio
api.description: Width over height. Puts the box on the page immediately, so a decoding image never shoves the rest of the page down.

api.name: fallback / errorLabel
api.description: Rendered in the same box on failure, so a dead URL costs the layout nothing.

api.name: priority
api.description: eager + fetchPriority="high", for the one image above the fold worth blocking on. Everything else stays lazy.

api.name: onStatusChange
api.description: For a gallery that wants to count what has landed.

demos.title: Masks, side by side
demos.code:
<Image src={src} alt="…" ratio={4 / 3} mask="skeleton" />
<Image src={src} alt="…" ratio={4 / 3} mask="shimmer" />
<Image src={src} alt="…" ratio={4 / 3} mask="blur" blurSrc={lqip} />

demos.title: When the URL is dead
demos.code: <Image src="/gone.jpg" alt="Missing" ratio={16 / 9} errorLabel="Could not load" />

audio-player.label: Audio Player
audio-player.description: A player built on the real <audio> element, so buffering, codecs, media keys, the OS lock screen and Bluetooth controls all keep working. State is read back off the element rather than mirrored, so anything else touching playback stays in sync.
audio-player.usage:
import { AudioPlayer } from '@/components/ui/audio-player'

<AudioPlayer src="/theme.mp3" title="Theme" artist="Astralyx" peaks={peaks} />

api.name: src / title / artist
api.description: The element does the playing; this draws the surface over it.

api.name: peaks
api.description: Precomputed amplitudes 0–1, drawn behind the scrubber. Computing them here would mean decoding the whole file on the main thread before the first frame.

api.name: scrubbing
api.description: Keyboard seeking, page-up jumps and screen-reader announcement are native. `timeupdate` is suspended while dragging, or playback yanks the thumb out of your hand.

api.name: state
api.description: Every listener reads back off <audio>, so a media key or the OS lock screen keeps this UI correct without going through it.

api.name: skipBy / showSkip
api.description: Seconds a skip button moves, and whether they render at all.

compare-slider.label: Compare Slider
compare-slider.description: Two images stacked, with a handle that wipes between them. Side-by-side thumbnails make the reader diff from memory; a wipe puts both states in the same pixels, so the difference is the only thing that moves.
compare-slider.usage: import { CompareSlider } from '@/components/ui/compare-slider' } after={} beforeLabel="Original" afterLabel="Upscaled" />

api.name: before / after
api.description: Any node, not just an img — the component stretches whatever you pass to fill the frame.

api.name: value / defaultValue / onValueChange
api.description: Controlled and uncontrolled.

api.name: clipping, not resizing
api.description: The overlay is clipped rather than resized. A resized image re-lays-out and re-samples on every pointer move, which buries subtle differences under scaling artefacts and janks the drag.

api.name: accessibility
api.description: The handle is a real slider in disguise, so arrows, Home and End work and it announces its position. The visible divider is decoration.

api.name: ratio
api.description: Reserves the box, so nothing shifts while the images decode.

demos.title: Before and after
demos.code: } after={} />

masonry.label: Masonry
masonry.description: A column layout for items of unequal height, built on CSS columns rather than a JS layout pass — so it packs before paint and reflows on resize for free. Items order top-to-bottom within a column, which is the trade.
masonry.usage:
import { Masonry } from '@/components/ui/masonry'

<Masonry columns={{ base: 1, sm: 2, lg: 3 }} gap={4}>
  {items.map((item) => <Card key={item.id}>{item.body}</Card>)}
</Masonry>

api.name: columns
api.description: Columns per breakpoint. Written out rather than interpolated, because Tailwind scans source text and `columns-${n}` produces nothing at build time.

api.name: gap
api.description: Applied as both the column gap and the item’s bottom margin — CSS columns have no row gap.

api.name: reading order
api.description: The honest trade for not running a JS layout pass. Fine for a gallery; wrong for a ranked list or a feed, where a plain grid or Kanban is the right answer.

api.name: break-inside
api.description: Applied to every item, so a card is never sliced across a column boundary — which is the default without it.

video-player.label: Video Player
video-player.description: A player with a scrubber, quality and subtitle menus. Controls are real buttons on a real timeline, so the keyboard reaches every one of them — a div-based scrubber never does.
video-player.usage:
import { VideoPlayer } from '@/components/ui/video-player'

<VideoPlayer src={src} poster={poster} qualities={qualities} subtitles={tracks} />

api.name: src / poster
api.description: Passed to the underlying `<video>`. The poster is what fills the frame before play, instead of a black rectangle.

api.name: qualities / quality / onQualityChange
api.description: Controlled: switching a rendition means changing the source, which is yours to do. Omit to hide the menu.

api.name: subtitles / subtitle
api.description: `null` is "off", which is a real selection and appears in the menu as one.

api.name: keyboard
api.description: Play/pause, seek, mute, fullscreen. The scrubber is a slider, so arrow keys seek from it too.

api.name: time display
api.description: A 40-minute video shows `12:04`, a 2-hour one shows `1:12:04`. Padding everything to hours wastes the width.

media-gallery.label: Media Gallery
media-gallery.description: A grid that opens into a lightbox. `alt` is required by the type rather than optional, because a gallery is exactly where missing alt text accumulates.

api.name: items
api.description: `{ id, src, alt, thumbnail?, caption? }`. `alt` is not optional.

api.name: columns
api.description: The count at full width; the grid steps down on narrow screens on its own.

api.name: lightbox
api.description: Opens in a `<dialog>` with `showModal()`, which gives focus trapping, Escape and inertness for free rather than reimplemented.

api.name: navigation
api.description: Arrow keys move between images while the lightbox is open, and focus returns to the tile you opened.

api.name: ratio
api.description: Tile aspect ratio. Tiles are uniform so the grid stays a grid; the full image is shown uncropped in the lightbox.

upload-list.label: Upload List
upload-list.description: Files in flight, with per-file progress and a retry for the ones that failed. A failed upload keeps its row rather than vanishing — silently dropping it is how people lose work.
upload-list.usage:
import { UploadList } from '@/components/ui/upload-list'

<UploadList uploads={uploads} onRetry={retry} onRemove={remove} onCancelAll={cancel} />

api.name: uploads
api.description: The same shape `AttachmentPreview` takes, so one list can carry files mid-upload and files already attached.

api.name: summary
api.description: Overall progress is weighted by file size, not by count — 3 of 4 files done means little when the fourth is 180 MB.

api.name: onRetry
api.description: Shown only on rows with an `error`.

api.name: onCancelAll
api.description: Appears while anything is still uploading. Omit for a list that cannot be interrupted.

pdf-viewer.label: PDF Viewer
pdf-viewer.description: A PDF in the browser’s own viewer with a toolbar around it. It delegates the rendering on purpose, and always shows a download link — because embedded PDFs fail routinely.
pdf-viewer.usage:
import { PdfViewer } from '@/components/ui/pdf-viewer'

<PdfViewer src="/invoice.pdf" title="Invoice 2026-04" pageCount={3} />

api.name: src
api.description: Framed, so it must be same-origin or serve permissive frame-ancestors. A cross-origin PDF that refuses framing shows the fallback, which is the correct outcome.

api.name: delegates rendering
api.description: Every browser ships a sandboxed, accessible, keyboard-navigable PDF viewer with search and printing. The alternative is ~350 kB of pdf.js plus a worker to arrive at a worse version of what is installed.

api.name: when to use pdf.js
api.description: Extracting text, drawing annotations, rendering a page to an image, a thumbnail rail. This component is honest that it is not that.

api.name: the fallback
api.description: iOS Safari has rendered only the first page, enterprise builds disable the plugin, and Content-Disposition: attachment means it never displays. A viewer without a download link fails silently and looks broken.

api.name: page / zoom
api.description: A hint, not a standard every viewer implements — Chrome and Firefox honour them, others ignore them.

api.name: vs FilePreview
api.description: `FilePreview` dispatches images, audio, text and code, and gives PDFs an honest "no preview". This is the branch it was missing.

image-cropper.label: Image Cropper
image-cropper.description: The step between picking an image and saving it. The crop is stored in natural image coordinates and exported with toBlob, so it survives a resize and uploads directly.
image-cropper.usage:
import { ImageCropper } from '@/components/ui/image-cropper'

<ImageCropper src={src} aspect={1} round onCrop={(blob) => upload(blob)} />

api.name: value / onChange
api.description: Natural image pixels, not displayed ones. A crop in screen pixels silently means something different after a resize, and produces a different output on a phone than on a desktop.

api.name: onCrop
api.description: `toBlob`, not `toDataURL`: base64 is a third larger, has to be built as one string, and usually gets converted back to a blob to upload anyway.

api.name: cross-origin
api.description: `crossOrigin="anonymous"` is set so a CORS-permissive server works; one that is not will throw at export, and `onError` reports it rather than leaving a dead button.

api.name: the gap it fills
api.description: A kit with a dropzone, a file input and an upload list still cannot set an avatar, because every avatar needs a square and every photo is a rectangle.

api.name: round
api.description: Cosmetic mask for avatars. The export is still a rectangle.

api.name: handles
api.description: Arrow keys resize, shift for a larger step — a drag handle that only answers a pointer is unusable without one.

bet-input.label: Bet Input
bet-input.description: A stake field with quick multipliers and a live return. Stakes are integer minor units and the max is clamped to the balance, so "all in" cannot stake money that is not there.
bet-input.usage:
import { BetInput } from '@/components/ui/bet-input'

<BetInput stake={stake} onStakeChange={setStake} balance={balance} odds={2.4} onPlace={place} />

api.name: stake
api.description: Minor units. Controlled, because the surrounding game usually owns it.

api.name: balance
api.description: Caps every quick action. Half and max are computed against it, so they can never exceed the funds available.

api.name: odds
api.description: Decimal odds. The potential return is shown live beneath the field — nobody should be doing that multiplication in their head.

api.name: min / max
api.description: Table limits. Enforced at the control rather than rejected on submit.

api.name: onPlace
api.description: Renders the place button. Omit for a stake field embedded in a larger slip.

demos.title: Stake with quick actions
demos.code:
const [stake, setStake] = useState(1000)

<BetInput stake={stake} onStakeChange={setStake} balance={24750} odds={2.4} onPlace={place} />

odds-display.label: Odds Display
odds-display.description: A selectable price in decimal, fractional or American. Decimal is the source of truth and the others are derived, so a format switch can never change what the bet actually pays.
odds-display.usage:
import { OddsDisplay } from '@/components/ui/odds-display'

<OddsDisplay label="Arsenal" odds={2.4} format="fractional" onSelect={select} />

api.name: odds
api.description: Decimal odds — 2.5 returns two and a half times the stake. Every other format is computed from this one.

api.name: format
api.description: 'decimal' | 'fractional' | 'american'. Fractional reduces to a readable denominator rather than an exact but absurd one.

api.name: previousOdds
api.description: Draws a movement arrow. A price drifting out is information a punter acts on.

api.name: suspended
api.description: Disables selection and says so. A suspended price that merely looks unselectable produces angry support tickets.

api.name: element
api.description: A real button, so selection is keyboard-reachable and announces its pressed state.

multiplier-chart.label: Multiplier Chart
multiplier-chart.description: The rising curve of a crash-style round. The crash is a state, not an animation that ends — the frozen curve and the final figure stay on screen so a player who looked away still sees what happened.
multiplier-chart.usage:
import { MultiplierChart } from '@/components/ui/multiplier-chart'

<MultiplierChart values={values} current={current} crashed={crashed} cashedOutAt={cashout} />

api.name: values
api.description: Samples over the round, starting at 1. The caller drives the tick; the component never runs a timer of its own.

api.name: current
api.description: The live figure, shown large. Falls back to the last sample.

api.name: crashed
api.description: Freezes the curve and switches to the crash colour. It is a state you stay in, not a flash.

api.name: cashedOutAt
api.description: Marks where the player got out, so the outcome is legible against the crash point.

api.name: scale
api.description: The vertical range grows with the curve but never shrinks mid-round; a rescaling axis makes a rising line look flat.

round-history.label: Round History
round-history.description: Recent results as a strip. It carries an explicit note that past rounds do not predict the next one, because a row of results is read as a pattern whether or not one exists.
round-history.usage:
import { RoundHistory } from '@/components/ui/round-history'

<RoundHistory rounds={rounds} lowBelow={2} highAbove={10} />

api.name: rounds
api.description: `{ id, value, at?, played?, detail? }`, newest first.

api.name: lowBelow / highAbove
api.description: Thresholds for the low and high tones. Game-specific, so they are props rather than baked in — 2× is a loss in one game and a win in another.

api.name: played
api.description: Rings the rounds the player took part in, which is the only way to read your own run out of a shared strip.

api.name: note
api.description: Overrides the default independence notice. It is rendered by default rather than opt-in.

api.name: format
api.description: For scores or currency instead of a multiplier.

leaderboard.label: Leaderboard
leaderboard.description: Ranked scores with movement since the last period, and the current user pinned even when they are nowhere near the top. A board you cannot find yourself on is a board you stop opening.

api.name: entries
api.description: `{ id, name, score, avatar?, previousRank?, isCurrentUser?, meta? }`. Sorted here, so a caller cannot ship a board that is out of order.

api.name: ties
api.description: Equal scores share a rank and the next rank skips, which is how every sport does it. Two players in "3rd" are not 3rd and 4th.

api.name: isCurrentUser
api.description: Highlights the row, and pins it below the cut with its true rank when it falls outside `limit`.

api.name: previousRank
api.description: Drives the movement arrow. Absent means new to the board, which is drawn differently from "unchanged".

api.name: formatScore
api.description: For points, times, or currency. Defaults to a grouped number.

campaign-card.label: Campaign Card
campaign-card.description: An affiliate offer with its performance. EPC leads, not revenue — £40,000 and £4,000 cannot be ranked without knowing the traffic behind each, and earnings per click is the only comparable figure.
campaign-card.usage:
import { CampaignCard } from '@/components/ui/campaign-card'

<CampaignCard name="Summer sale" status="active" clicks={18402} conversions={412} revenue={38210} />

api.name: clicks / conversions / revenue
api.description: The three raw figures. Conversion rate and EPC are derived from them here, so the card can never print a rate that contradicts its own numbers.

api.name: status
api.description: 'active' | 'paused' | 'ended' | 'pending'. Anything not active is dimmed, so a paused offer does not read as a live one.

api.name: payout
api.description: The commission terms in words — "30% rev share", "$25 CPA". Not a number, because these are rarely just a number.

api.name: history
api.description: Optional sparkline. A campaign at £1,700 a day that was at £800 last week is a different proposition from one that was at £3,000.

utm-builder.label: UTM Builder
utm-builder.description: Builds a tagged campaign URL. Values are lower-cased with underscores for spaces, because analytics tools treat Summer Sale, summer sale and summer_sale as three separate campaigns and nobody reconciles them later.

api.name: baseUrl
api.description: The destination. Existing query parameters are preserved — a link that already carries a referral code keeps it.

api.name: normalisation
api.description: Lower-cased, spaces to underscores. Cleaning at the point the link is made is the only place it reliably happens.

api.name: encoding
api.description: Built with `URL`, not string concatenation. A campaign name containing an ampersand would silently truncate every parameter after it.

api.name: onUrlChange
api.description: Fires when the finished URL is copied.

postback-config.label: Postback Config
postback-config.description: A server-to-server postback URL, validated against its macros. A postback missing {click_id} returns 200 and attributes nothing — this says so before it ships rather than in a reconciliation weeks later.
postback-config.usage:
import { PostbackConfig } from '@/components/ui/postback-config'

<PostbackConfig url={url} onUrlChange={setUrl} macros={macros} status="ok" />

api.name: macros
api.description: `{ token, description, required? }`. Clicking one appends it to the URL, which beats retyping braces.

api.name: validation
api.description: Required macros that are missing, macros that are not in your list, and plain `http://` are each called out separately.

api.name: url / onUrlChange
api.description: Controlled or uncontrolled. Uncontrolled is fine for a preview; a real config screen owns the value.

api.name: status / lastFired
api.description: Delivery health. "Firing, last 4 minutes ago" is the answer to the only question anyone opens this screen with.

revenue-share-table.label: Revenue Share Table
revenue-share-table.description: How a payout splits between parties. The unallocated remainder gets a named row instead of leaving the reader to subtract, and a split exceeding 100% is called out rather than quietly rendered.
revenue-share-table.usage:
import { RevenueShareTable } from '@/components/ui/revenue-share-table'

<RevenueShareTable rows={rows} gross={48210} currency="USD" />

api.name: rows
api.description: `{ id, party, share, note? }` where share is 0–1.

api.name: gross
api.description: The figure being split. Each party's amount is computed from it, so a percentage can never sit beside an amount that contradicts it.

api.name: remainder
api.description: What is left over gets a row of its own. A split reaching only 90% is normal — the house keeps the rest — and it should be visible.

api.name: over-allocation
api.description: Shares totalling more than 100% render as an "Over-allocated" row in the destructive tone. That is a configuration error, not a display problem.

map-embed.label: Map Embed
map-embed.description: A map on CARTO's near-monochrome basemap. A full-colour street map fights everything drawn on top of it; a greyscale ground lets the marker be the only saturated thing on screen.
map-embed.usage:
import { MapEmbed } from '@/components/ui/map-embed'

<MapEmbed lat={51.5074} lng={-0.1278} label="Trafalgar Square, London" />

api.name: tiles
api.description: OpenStreetMap's keyless tiles by default. CARTO's Dark Matter and Positron need an API key, so the monochrome look here comes from a CSS filter instead. Pass `(z, x, y) => url` for your own or a keyed provider — OSM's usage policy asks their servers not carry production traffic.

api.name: theme
api.description: 'dark' inverts a greyscale raster to a dark ground; 'light' desaturates it. 'auto' renders both layers and lets CSS pick, so the theme toggle costs no tile requests.

api.name: filter
api.description: Overrides the CSS treatment. `null` leaves tiles alone — right when your provider already serves a monochrome style.

api.name: rendering
api.description: Plain `` tiles in a grid — no iframe, no mapping library, no third-party JavaScript or cookies. The remaining exposure is the tile requests, the same as any remote image.

api.name: interaction
api.description: A static view. Anything needing pan and zoom wants MapLibre; this is deliberately not that.

api.name: eager
api.description: Set false to hold the tiles behind a click, which is where a consent gate goes.

api.name: attribution
api.description: Overrides the CARTO/OpenStreetMap credit. It is rendered by default because both providers require it.

location-picker.label: Location Picker
location-picker.description: Pick a place by searching, or by typing coordinates. Both routes stay open: search covers the common case, the fields cover the field site or mooring that no geocoder knows.
location-picker.usage:
import { LocationPicker } from '@/components/ui/location-picker'

<LocationPicker value={value} onValueChange={setValue} onSearch={geocode} />

api.name: onSearch
api.description: Your geocoder. A component library has no business picking one — they need keys, terms differ wildly, and several forbid storing results.

api.name: stale responses
api.description: Requests are debounced and tagged by sequence, so the answer for "Berl" cannot land last and beat the one for "Berlin".

api.name: showCoordinates
api.description: The manual fallback. Not hidden behind an "advanced" toggle, because the people who need it are the ones who cannot find it there.

api.name: showMap
api.description: Renders a `MapEmbed` preview of the chosen point on the monochrome basemap.

address-input.label: Address Input
address-input.description: A postal address whose shape follows the country. A US form asks for a State and a ZIP; a UK one asks for a County and a Postcode; Japan puts the postal code first. Shipping the US layout everywhere is how forms reject valid addresses.

api.name: value
api.description: `{ country, line1, line2, city, region, postalCode }`. Structured, not a single textarea, so it can be validated and shipped.

api.name: country-driven labels
api.description: Region and postal-code labels, requiredness and field order all follow the selected country. Hong Kong and the UAE have no postal codes at all.

api.name: validation
api.description: No postal-code regexes. They are famously wrong — Eircodes, BFPO, new UK districts — and a form that refuses a real address is worse than one that accepts a typo.

api.name: autoComplete
api.description: Which is the only reason a browser can fill the whole address from one tap.

demos.title: Country-aware fields
demos.code:
const [address, setAddress] = useState({ ...emptyAddress, country: 'US' })

<AddressInput value={address} onValueChange={setAddress} />

coordinate-input.label: Coordinate Input
coordinate-input.description: Latitude and longitude, accepting decimal degrees or DMS. A latitude above 90 is reported as "is this a longitude?" rather than "out of range" — swapped pairs are the most common coordinate bug there is.

api.name: value
api.description: `{ lat, lng }`. `null` while the fields do not parse to a valid pair.

api.name: input formats
api.description: Both `51.5074` and `51°30'26.6"N` parse. Rejecting the second means the user converts by hand, which is where a digit gets dropped.

api.name: paste
api.description: Pasting `51.5074, -0.1278` into either field fills both — a comma-separated pair is how coordinates travel.

api.name: precision
api.description: About 11cm. More digits imply an accuracy no consumer GPS has.

demos.title: Round-tripping a pair
demos.code:
const [value, setValue] = useState({ lat: 51.5074, lng: -0.1278 })

<CoordinateInput value={value} onValueChange={setValue} />

timezone-select.label: Timezone Select
timezone-select.description: An IANA timezone picker showing each zone's current offset and local time. Zones are named by city, never by abbreviation — "CST" is Central, China and Cuba Standard Time.

api.name: options
api.description: `Intl.supportedValuesOf("timeZone")`, so the list is whatever the browser actually supports rather than a table that rots each time a government moves a DST boundary.

api.name: offsets
api.description: A zone's offset is a function of the date. A list built in January is wrong for half the year.

api.name: zones
api.description: Restrict the list. A booking form rarely needs all four hundred.

api.name: showLocalTime
api.description: The zone's current wall-clock time — usually the fastest way to recognise the right one.

api.name: search
api.description: The region stays in the label, so `Europe/London` is findable by "Europe" as well as by "London".

request-builder.label: Request Builder
request-builder.description: Method, URL, headers, query and body. Query parameters are edited as rows and the assembled URL is shown beneath — hand-editing a query string is where encoding bugs come from.
request-builder.usage:
import { RequestBuilder } from '@/components/ui/request-builder'

<RequestBuilder method={method} url={url} params={params} onSend={send} />

api.name: params / headers
api.description: `{ id, name, value, enabled? }`. Rows toggle off rather than only delete — that is the actual workflow.

api.name: assembled URL
api.description: Built with `URL`, so values are encoded. An `&` inside a value would otherwise become a parameter boundary.

api.name: body section
api.description: A GET body is legal in the RFC and widely stripped by proxies. Offering it invites an afternoon of debugging.

api.name: onSend
api.description: Omit to render a request editor with no send control.

response-viewer.label: Response Viewer
response-viewer.description: Status, timing, size, headers and body. The three headline figures share one line because they are read together — a 200 that took 4 seconds is a different result from one that took 40ms.
response-viewer.usage:
import { ResponseViewer } from '@/components/ui/response-viewer'

<ResponseViewer status={200} durationMs={412} sizeBytes={8214} body={json} />

api.name: body
api.description: A JSON body gets the tree view; anything else gets highlighted text. Rendering JSON as a wall of text is honest and useless.

api.name: headers
api.description: Lower-cased and sorted for display — HTTP header names are case-insensitive and servers are inconsistent, which breaks an A–Z scan.

api.name: durationMs
api.description: Turns amber past a second.

api.name: sections
api.description: Not tabs: the three panels differ hugely in height, so a shared tab panel resizes the card on every switch and the strip moves out from under the pointer. Stacking also lets headers and body be read together.

demos.title: A 200 with headers and a body

endpoint-list.label: Endpoint List
endpoint-list.description: API routes, grouped and filterable. The method badge is fixed-width because a route table is scanned down the method column, and a ragged left edge makes that scan impossible.

api.name: endpoints
api.description: `{ id, method, path, summary?, group?, auth?, deprecated?, status? }`.

api.name: deprecated
api.description: Struck through but kept. Removing a deprecated route from the list is how a client keeps calling it for another year.

api.name: filtering
api.description: The method is part of the haystack, so "post /users" filters the way people type.

api.name: auth
api.description: Draws a lock. Whether a route needs credentials is the second thing anyone looks for.

schema-viewer.label: Schema Viewer
schema-viewer.description: JSON Schema as a tree. Required fields are marked on the field itself rather than left in the parent's `required` array — cross-referencing that list is the one job a renderer should do for you.

api.name: schema
api.description: A plain JSON Schema object. No `$ref` resolution — dereference before passing it in.

api.name: constraints
api.description: `format`, `enum`, `pattern`, length and range shown beside the type. That a string must match a UUID pattern is the interesting part; "string" is not.

api.name: oneOf / anyOf
api.description: Rendered as branches, never flattened — a flattened union looks like an object with contradictory fields.

api.name: deprecated
api.description: Struck through and badged.

webhook-inspector.label: Webhook Inspector
webhook-inspector.description: Inbound deliveries with payload and response. Signature status is its own field, never folded into the status code — a 200 with an invalid signature is a forged request your handler accepted.

api.name: deliveries
api.description: `{ id, event, at, status?, durationMs?, payload?, responseBody?, signature?, attempt? }`.

api.name: signature
api.description: Separate from the status. A delivery that returned 200 with an invalid signature is called out explicitly.

api.name: both directions
api.description: What arrived and what you answered. A webhook failure is a disagreement between the two, and storing only the payload cannot say which side was wrong.

api.name: onReplay
api.description: Omit for a read-only log.

curl-command.label: Curl Command
curl-command.description: A request as a runnable curl command, shell-quoted and with secrets masked. This output gets pasted into tickets, and an Authorization header pasted into a ticket is a leaked credential.
curl-command.usage:
import { CurlCommand } from '@/components/ui/curl-command'

<CurlCommand method="POST" url={url} headers={headers} body={body} />

api.name: redact
api.description: Header names whose values are masked. Defaults cover Authorization, Cookie, api-key and x-*-token.

api.name: quoting
api.description: Single-quoted with `'\''` for embedded quotes. A JSON body pasted raw truncates at the first apostrophe in someone's surname.

api.name: body
api.description: An object is JSON-encoded before quoting.

api.name: line breaks
api.description: Backslash continuations — a 400-character single line cannot be reviewed.

demos.title: A POST with headers and a body

http-status.label: HTTP Status
http-status.description: A status code with its reason phrase. Colour follows the class, never the individual code — grading a 503 as worse than a 500 invents a severity ordering that does not exist.

api.name: status
api.description: The code. Reason phrases for the common ones are built in.

api.name: phrase
api.description: Overrides the built-in phrase — for a server that sends its own.

api.name: colour
api.description: One green for every 2xx, one red for every 5xx. 3xx is informational, not success: a redirect is not a completed request, and green hides a redirect loop.

api.name: showPhrase
api.description: Off gives a bare code, for a dense table.

note-graph.label: Note Graph
note-graph.description: A vault of linked notes laid out by force — the Obsidian-shaped view. Nodes are sized by how many links touch them, hovering dims everything outside the neighbourhood, and orphans are drawn hollow rather than hidden.
note-graph.usage:
import { NoteGraph } from '@/components/ui/note-graph'

<NoteGraph notes={notes} links={links} onSelect={(note) => open(note.id)} />

api.name: notes / links
api.description: { id, title, group?, size? } and { source, target }.

api.name: size
api.description: Derived from link count, damped by a square root. Sizing by word count or edit date draws your typing habits instead of your structure.

api.name: orphans
api.description: A note nothing links to is the most actionable thing the view can surface — either miscategorised or forgotten — so hiding it to tidy the picture removes the point.

api.name: hover
api.description: At a few hundred nodes the hairball is unreadable at rest. Focus makes it legible for the cost of one class.

api.name: labelFrom / showAllLabels
api.description: Titles are drawn for hubs and for whatever you are hovering, unless you ask for all of them.

api.name: layout
api.description: From `useForceGraph`. Deterministic seeding, so a reload is the same picture and a server render matches its hydration. Dragging pins a note.

knowledge-graph.label: Knowledge Graph
knowledge-graph.description: Entities and the named relations between them. Where a note graph answers what is connected, this answers how — and the edge label carries as much meaning as the nodes, so relations are labelled and directed.
knowledge-graph.usage:
import { KnowledgeGraph } from '@/components/ui/knowledge-graph'

<KnowledgeGraph entities={entities} relations={relations} onSelect={open} />

api.name: entities / relations
api.description: { id, label, type? } and { source, target, label? }. The relation label is the reason this exists.

api.name: direction
api.description: `employs` and `employed by` are not the same fact. A knowledge graph that loses direction is a set of vague associations.

api.name: entities as pills
api.description: These graphs are read entity-first — you are looking for a name, not a hub — and a circle with a caption underneath makes you match shapes to text.

api.name: showRelationLabels
api.description: Off once the graph is dense enough that the labels collide.

api.name: type
api.description: Colours the pill and builds the legend. Any vocabulary you like.

markdown.label: Markdown
markdown.description: Rendered markdown with a switch to the source. It builds React nodes and never sets innerHTML, so a document you did not write cannot execute — and the RAW toggle is there because rendered output hides exactly what you look at when it renders wrongly.

api.name: children
api.description: The markdown source.

api.name: no innerHTML
api.description: Every small renderer converts to an HTML string and injects it, which turns any document you did not write into script execution. Building elements means there is no string for a payload to survive in.

api.name: link safety
api.description: Only http(s), mailto and relative URLs become links; anything else — `javascript:` above all — renders as plain text.

api.name: toggle / defaultRaw
api.description: Rendered markdown hides hard versus soft breaks, `*` versus `_`, a real table versus an aligned one. Source is one click away and copyable.

api.name: supported
api.description: ATX headings, bold, italic, strikethrough, inline code, links, images, fenced code, lists, blockquotes, rules and tables. Setext headings, reference links and footnotes are not — a full CommonMark implementation is a library, not a component.

markdown-editor.label: Markdown Editor
markdown-editor.description: A real textarea, a toolbar that edits the selection through setRangeText — so the browser undo stack survives — and the Markdown component as its preview.
markdown-editor.usage:
import { MarkdownEditor } from '@/components/ui/markdown-editor'

<MarkdownEditor value={text} onChange={setText} defaultMode="split" />

api.name: value / onChange
api.description: The markdown source. Controlled or uncontrolled.

api.name: a plain textarea
api.description: Rich editors reimplement undo, IME composition, spellcheck, autocorrect, mobile keyboards and every accessibility affordance a textarea gets free — and get the undo stack wrong first.

api.name: setRangeText
api.description: The toolbar edits through the element, so ctrl-Z after clicking Bold does what you expect. Rewriting `value` from React state does not.

api.name: preview
api.description: An editor whose preview differs from the reader’s view teaches a formatting model your readers will not see — including where [[markdown]] stops.

api.name: wrapping
api.description: With text selected the markers go around it; with nothing selected the caret lands between them; applying the same marker again unwraps it.

api.name: shortcuts
api.description: Tab is deliberately left alone — trapping it breaks keyboard navigation out of the field.

scatter-plot.label: Scatter Plot
scatter-plot.description: Two measured variables plotted against each other, with an optional least-squares trend line and Pearson’s r. Points can carry a third dimension as area and a fourth as colour.
scatter-plot.usage:
import { ScatterPlot } from '@/components/ui/scatter-plot'

<ScatterPlot points={points} trend xLabel="Spend" yLabel="Conversion %" />

api.name: points
api.description: { x, y, size?, group?, label? }. Both axes are measured values with their own scale.

api.name: vs Chart scatter
api.description: `Chart`’s scatter variant spaces `number[]` evenly along an index. Here x is a value, which is what makes the relationship visible at all.

api.name: trend
api.description: Ordinary least squares, with Pearson’s r. r measures linear association only — a parabola scores near zero, and one outlier moves it a long way.

api.name: size
api.description: Scaling the radius makes a doubled value look four times bigger. Area is proportional, so it reads honestly.

api.name: points as elements
api.description: The plot is stretched to fill its box, which turns an SVG circle into an ellipse. Positioned elements stay round at any aspect ratio.

api.name: xDomain / yDomain
api.description: Fixed bounds. Defaults to the data range with 5% padding so nothing sits on the axis.

demos.title: Spend against conversion, with a fit

radar-chart.label: Radar Chart
radar-chart.description: Several measures for one subject on axes radiating from a centre. Good for recognising a profile’s shape; documented plainly as the wrong chart when the reader needs to compare values.
radar-chart.usage:
import { RadarChart } from '@/components/ui/radar-chart'

<RadarChart axes={axes} series={series} max={100} />

api.name: axes / series
api.description: { key, label, max? } and { name, values: Record<key, number> }.

api.name: when not to use it
api.description: Area grows with the square of the value, so a 20% better profile looks 44% bigger. Axis order is arbitrary but changes the shape. For comparing values, a grouped bar chart is measurably better.

api.name: max
api.description: Shared ceiling. Axes on different scales produce a shape that means nothing; per-axis `max` exists for when the units genuinely differ.

api.name: uniform scaling
api.description: No `preserveAspectRatio: none` — a sheared radar is unreadable.

api.name: fillOpacity
api.description: Lower it when shapes overlap heavily.

sankey.label: Sankey
sankey.description: Flow between stages, where band width is the quantity moving. Nodes are layered by longest path so every link runs forward, and a cycle is reported rather than drawn as something plausible.

api.name: nodes / links
api.description: { id, label, color? } and { source, target, value }.

api.name: vs Funnel
api.description: A funnel shows the same drop-off as shrinking bars. A Sankey shows where the loss went, which is usually the actual question.

api.name: layering
api.description: Derived, not taken from input order — laying nodes out in the order they were listed produces backward links and a tangle.

api.name: cycles
api.description: Depth is undefined inside a loop, so a cycle raises `onError` instead of being drawn wrongly.

api.name: ribbons
api.description: The plot is stretched to fill its box and a stroke under a non-uniform transform scales unevenly — the band width would change with the container’s aspect ratio, which is a lie about the quantity.

treemap.label: Treemap
treemap.description: Part-to-whole as nested rectangles sized by area, laid out with the squarify algorithm so tiles stay close to square instead of degenerating into slivers.

api.name: nodes
api.description: { id, label, value?, children?, color? }. Parents sum their children.

api.name: squarified
api.description: The strip layout produces rectangles hundreds of times longer than they are wide — unlabellable, incomparable, hard to hit. Squarify keeps the worst aspect ratio in each row as low as it can.

api.name: area
api.description: People judge area far less accurately than length. Right for "what is big, roughly, and what is inside what"; wrong for "is A bigger than B" when they are close.

api.name: labels
api.description: A label that does not fit is removed rather than ellipsised into nothing. The value stays reachable through the tooltip.

api.name: depth
api.description: 1 flattens the hierarchy to its top level.

box-plot.label: Box Plot
box-plot.description: Quartiles, Tukey whiskers and outliers — the distribution an average hides. Quartiles use linear interpolation, so they agree with what your analytics stack reports.
box-plot.usage:
import { BoxPlot } from '@/components/ui/box-plot'

<BoxPlot series={[{ name: 'us-east', values: latencies }]} />

api.name: series
api.description: { name, values? } for raw samples, or { name, summary } when only the five numbers came back from the warehouse.

api.name: whiskers
api.description: Tukey, not min/max. Whiskers to the extremes let one bad sample stretch the chart and fold outliers into the range, making them invisible.

api.name: quantiles
api.description: R type-7 / numpy default, so the numbers match your analytics stack rather than disagreeing by a few milliseconds.

api.name: horizontal
api.description: Rows instead of columns. Better when the series names are long.

api.name: built from elements
api.description: Every part is an axis-aligned rectangle or line, and median thickness, cap widths and outlier dots stay exact in CSS pixels at any size.

gantt.label: Gantt
gantt.description: Work on a timeline: drag a bar to reschedule and its edges to change the start or end, with a computed critical path and dependency conflicts surfaced as you create them.
gantt.usage:
import { Gantt } from '@/components/ui/gantt'

<Gantt tasks={tasks} onChange={setTasks} criticalPath today={new Date()} />

api.name: tasks
api.description: { id, label, start, end, progress?, dependsOn?, milestone? }.

api.name: vs Kanban / Timeline / Stepper
api.description: Kanban shows state and hides time. A timeline shows moments, not spans. A stepper shows order, not overlap. Only this shows how long, and at the same time as what.

api.name: criticalPath
api.description: The longest dependency chain is derived from the data. Marking it by hand is how a Gantt goes stale — someone slips a task, nobody re-marks the path, and it points at the wrong risk.

api.name: onChange / onTaskChange
api.description: Supplying either makes the chart editable; omitting both makes it read-only. A read-only Gantt is a printout of a plan, and the reason to look at one is usually that something needs moving.

api.name: dragging
api.description: The body moves the task and keeps its duration; the edges change the start and the end independently. Handles are 8px, which is the difference between resizing and moving by accident.

api.name: keyboard
api.description: Arrows move by one snap, shift-arrow changes the end, and the dates are announced through `aria-valuetext`. A chart editable only by pointer is not editable at all for a good number of people.

api.name: snapMinutes
api.description: A day. Dragging to arbitrary millisecond boundaries produces a plan nobody can read back.

api.name: conflicts
api.description: Recomputed against the drag rather than the saved data, so an impossible schedule looks impossible while you are making it.

api.name: monochrome
api.description: A plan is read for structure — what is long, what overlaps, what is late — and arbitrary per-task colour adds a legend without adding information. The critical path is ringed and a conflict is outlined in dashes, so neither state is carried by colour alone.

api.name: today
api.description: A vertical marker. Omitted by default rather than assumed.

demos.title: A release plan, critical path marked

scheduler.label: Scheduler
scheduler.description: A week of days with events laid out against the hours and edited in place — drag to move across days, drag an edge to change the end, drag empty grid to create. Overlaps split into columns rather than stacking.
scheduler.usage:
import { Scheduler } from '@/components/ui/scheduler'

<Scheduler events={events} onChange={setEvents} onCreate={make} dayStart={8} dayEnd={20} />

api.name: events
api.description: { id, title, start, end, color?, allDay? }.

api.name: vs Calendar
api.description: `Calendar` picks a date; this shows what is in it. Conflating them produces a date picker with a broken agenda glued on.

api.name: overlaps
api.description: Two meetings drawn on top of each other means one is invisible — and the hidden one is the one you miss. Clusters are split into as many columns as they need.

api.name: timezone
api.description: Keying by UTC date puts a 23:00 event on the wrong day for anyone west of Greenwich — common, and hard to spot from the timezone it was written in.

api.name: onChange / onEventChange
api.description: Supplying either makes the grid editable. A calendar you cannot drag on is a printout.

api.name: dragging
api.description: The body moves the event across hours *and* days; the bottom edge changes the end; a drag on empty grid draws a new one. The grab offset is kept, so the event does not jump its top to the cursor.

api.name: onCreate
api.description: Return an event to add it, or nothing to decline — so a click-drag can open your own dialog instead.

api.name: snapMinutes
api.description: The unit calendars are actually kept in. Without a grid a drag produces 10:07–11:04.

api.name: keyboard
api.description: Up and down move by a snap, left and right move between days, shift-arrow changes the end.

api.name: monochrome
api.description: Adjacent columns are separated by a border in the page background rather than by colour, so a clash stays readable at any theme and in print.

api.name: dayStart / dayEnd
api.description: Crops to working hours; eight of the twenty-four rows carry all the information in most calendars.

demos.title: A working week, with a clash

org-chart.label: Org Chart
org-chart.description: A reporting hierarchy drawn top-down with connectors, built from flat { id, managerId } rows. Orphans and multiple roots are rendered rather than dropped; cycles are reported.
org-chart.usage:
import { OrgChart } from '@/components/ui/org-chart'

<OrgChart nodes={people} onSelect={(person) => open(person.id)} />

api.name: nodes
api.description: Flat `{ id, name, title?, managerId }` — how every HR system, directory and database actually stores it. Requiring pre-nested input pushes the same recursion into every caller.

api.name: vs Tree
api.description: A tree is an indented list, right for a filesystem. An org chart is read for spans — how many report to this person, are these two peers — and siblings side by side answer both at a glance.

api.name: orphans
api.description: A vacant manager slot, a contractor, a transfer pointing at a deleted record. Dropping those rows makes the chart quietly wrong.

api.name: cycles
api.description: A reports to B reports to A is detected by reachability and surfaced through `onError` rather than recursed into.

api.name: stackAfter
api.description: Past this many children a node lays them out in a column with a spine, rather than a very long horizontal rule.

demos.title: A team, with an unmanaged contractor

storage-usage.label: Storage Usage
storage-usage.description: A quota and what is filling it. The bar is scaled to the quota, not to what is used, so free space reads as free space — a bar normalised to the total consumed is always full, which is backwards for a component answering “how much room is left”.

api.name: segments / quota
api.description: { id, label, bytes, color? }. Omit the quota for an unmetered store and the bar scales to the total instead.

api.name: over quota
api.description: An object store keeps accepting writes and billing for them; pinning the bar at 100% hides the one number someone is about to be charged for.

api.name: minimum segment
api.description: “Logs are tiny” and “there are no logs” must not render identically.

bucket-list.label: Bucket List
bucket-list.description: Object-storage buckets, with public access rendered as a warning rather than as one small grey tag among five. Every storage breach of the last decade is a bucket nobody realised was world-readable.

api.name: buckets
api.description: { name, region?, size?, objects?, public?, badges?, createdAt? }.

api.name: public
api.description: Drawn as a destructive badge with a warning glyph, not a tag. This is the fact the list exists to surface.

api.name: region
api.description: Immutable and expensive to get wrong — a bucket in the wrong region is a migration, not a setting.

object-list.label: Object List
object-list.description: Objects in a bucket, with the prefix hierarchy object stores only pretend to have. There are no folders in S3-shaped storage — `a/b/c.png` is one flat key — so keys deeper than the current prefix collapse into a prefix row with a count.

api.name: objects
api.description: { key, size?, modified?, storageClass?, archived? }. Keys are flat; the folders are derived.

api.name: prefix / onPrefixChange
api.description: Controlled navigation. Uncontrolled by default.

api.name: archived
api.description: Not immediately readable — it needs a restore request and hours. A list showing only size and date makes it look available.

api.name: searching
api.description: A filter that still hides matches behind folders is not a search.

api.name: groupByPrefix
api.description: Exported, for building your own layout on the same grouping.

asset-grid.label: Asset Grid
asset-grid.description: A media library as a selectable grid, built on this kit’s Image so every tile gets a placeholder, a reserved box and a failure state. A broken asset stays in the grid — it is exactly the one someone came to find and replace.
asset-grid.usage:
import { AssetGrid } from '@/components/ui/asset-grid'

<AssetGrid assets={assets} value={selected} onValueChange={setSelected} />

api.name: assets
api.description: { id, src?, name, type?, size?, modified?, meta? }. No src falls back to a glyph for the MIME type.

api.name: value / onValueChange
api.description: Controlled selection. Omit both for a read-only library; the tiles then call onOpen instead.

api.name: broken assets
api.description: A library that hides failures makes a rotted URL invisible while its reference is still live in production.

api.name: minTile / ratio
api.description: The grid is auto-fill, so tiles reflow to the container rather than to a fixed column count.

demos.title: Picking assets, one of them broken

file-preview.label: File Preview
file-preview.description: One file rendered as whatever it actually is — image, text, audio, or an honest “no preview” panel. The MIME type decides, never the extension: a .png served as text/html is the oldest upload attack there is.

api.name: file
api.description: { name, type?, size?, url?, text?, language? }. `text` is already fetched — this renders, it does not load.

api.name: type over extension
api.description: The store’s MIME type decides. The extension is consulted only when there is no type at all, never as an override.

api.name: maxChars
api.description: A 40MB log rendered into the DOM freezes the tab, and a preview only has to answer whether you want the file.

api.name: audio / video
api.description: Audio uses this kit’s AudioPlayer; video uses a native <video>, which brings buffering, captions and OS controls with it.

backup-list.label: Backup List
backup-list.description: Snapshots, and whether any of them would actually restore. A backup nobody has restored is a hypothesis, so an untested one is drawn as a warning rather than as a success.
backup-list.usage:
import { BackupList } from '@/components/ui/backup-list'

<BackupList backups={backups} newestAge="6 hours ago" onRestore={restore} />

api.name: backups
api.description: { id, createdAt, size?, kind?, verified?, status?, meta? }. `createdAt` is pre-formatted.

api.name: verified
api.description: A restore has actually been tested. Unverified is a warning, because the failure mode of backups is finding out at the worst moment that they have been empty for a month.

api.name: newestAge
api.description: Stated in the header rather than left to be worked out from timestamps — “how much data would we lose” is the only question anyone brings here.

api.name: no backups
api.description: An empty list is rendered as a failure, not as an empty box.

slow-query-log.label: Slow Query Log
slow-query-log.description: The queries costing you the most, ranked by total time rather than mean. The 9-second report running twice a day is easy to find; the 40ms lookup running four thousand times a minute is the one saturating the database.

api.name: queries
api.description: { id, statement, calls, meanMs, p95Ms?, rows?, seqScan?, meta? }. Statements should be normalised by the caller so the same query aggregates into one row.

api.name: rankByTotal
api.description: mean × calls. Turn it off to rank by mean, which is the ordering most tools use and the one that hides the real problem.

api.name: seqScan
api.description: No index was used — the most actionable finding here, and invisible in the timings alone.

index-list.label: Index List
index-list.description: The indexes on a table and which are dead weight. An unused index is written on every insert and makes the planner’s job harder — but a primary key with no scans is not flagged, because suggesting you drop one is advice that loses data.

api.name: indexes
api.description: { name, columns, unique?, primary?, size?, scans?, meta? }. Column order matters for a composite index and is preserved.

api.name: scans === 0
api.description: Dead weight — unless it is the primary key, which earns its keep enforcing uniqueness whether or not anything reads through it.

api.name: duplicateIndexes
api.description: Same columns in the same order. Exported so a migration check can fail on it.

demos.title: An unused index and a duplicate

replication-status.label: Replication Status
replication-status.description: A primary and its replicas with how far behind each one is, in seconds and bytes. Seconds say how stale a read is; bytes say whether it is catching up or falling further behind — a replica idling on 200MB of unsent log shows 0s until traffic arrives.

api.name: primary / replicas
api.description: Replica is { id, name, lagSeconds?, lagBytes?, state?, readable?, region?, meta? }.

api.name: state
api.description: A disconnected replica is drawn as a failure, not as very high lag — one needs patience, the other needs someone.

api.name: no replicas
api.description: Rendered as “no read redundancy”, rather than as an empty list.

connection-pool.label: Connection Pool
connection-pool.description: What is checked out, idle and waiting. A pool at 100% with nothing queued is exactly the right size; the same pool with twelve waiting is an outage forming — so waiters are drawn beyond the bar rather than folded into it.
connection-pool.usage:
import { ConnectionPool } from '@/components/ui/connection-pool'

<ConnectionPool active={18} idle={4} max={25} waiting={0} />

api.name: active / idle / max
api.description: Checked out, open but unused, and the ceiling. Idle is shown rather than hidden: two active and thirty idle is paying to hold thirty sockets against a connection limit.

api.name: waiting
api.description: Requests queued for a connection — the number that signals trouble. Drawn past the end of the bar, because it is demand the pool cannot meet.

api.name: waitMs
api.description: Mean time before a connection is handed over.

demos.title: Healthy, and saturated
demos.code:
<ConnectionPool active={18} idle={4} max={25} />
<ConnectionPool active={25} idle={0} max={25} waiting={12} />

csv-preview.label: CSV Preview
csv-preview.description: A parsed CSV before you import it, showing the rows that will break the import. A preview that renders the first ten rows of a clean file has shown you nothing — mismatched column counts are what abort an import halfway.
csv-preview.usage:
import { CsvPreview } from '@/components/ui/csv-preview'

<CsvPreview columns={columns} rows={rows} malformed={[4]} totalRows={18_402} />

api.name: columns / rows
api.description: Already parsed. This renders; it does not parse — quoted fields with commas and newlines are a real parser’s job, and a naive split mangles exactly the files that need previewing.

api.name: malformed
api.description: Row indices whose column count did not match the header. Surfaced above the table, since it is the reason to open a preview.

api.name: confidence
api.description: Inference reported rather than asserted: 998 integers and 2 blanks is an integer column with nulls; 500 integers and 500 dates is a mess someone has to look at.

demos.title: A file with a bad row

data-quality.label: Data Quality
data-quality.description: A column profile: how complete, how varied, and what the values look like. Sample values are the fastest way to spot that a “date” column holds three different formats — no summary statistic catches that.

api.name: columns
api.description: { name, type?, nullFraction?, distinct?, total?, min?, max?, samples? }.

api.name: distinct
api.description: One distinct value is a constant masquerading as data; one per row is an id, not a dimension. Both are flagged, because both break what a chart expects.

api.name: samples
api.description: Real values. The fastest way to see mixed formats hiding behind a clean-looking type.

demos.title: A constant, an id and a mostly-empty column

query-editor.label: Query Editor
query-editor.description: A SQL editor that asks before running an UPDATE or DELETE with no WHERE clause. That is the most expensive mistake anyone makes in a query console, and it is trivial to detect.
query-editor.usage:
import { QueryEditor } from '@/components/ui/query-editor'

<QueryEditor value={sql} onValueChange={setSql} onRun={run} />

api.name: highlighting
api.description: The editor is a `CodeBlock` in editable mode, so SQL is highlighted as it is typed. A console where every statement is one grey block is a console people paste out of.

api.name: guard
api.description: UPDATE or DELETE without a WHERE, and DROP/TRUNCATE/ALTER, require a second click before `onRun` fires.

api.name: shortcutKeys
api.description: Rendered with `Kbd`, split on `+`. Cmd/Ctrl+Enter runs — anyone who has used a query console expects it, and reaching for a button breaks the loop. `null` hides the hint.

api.name: statement count
api.description: Running a multi-statement buffer does something different from running one, and that should not be a surprise.

api.name: onRun
api.description: Omit to render a read-write editor with no execution.

query-constructor.label: Query Constructor
query-constructor.description: A SELECT assembled a clause at a time — sources with a join button, columns, filter, then order, group and limit — with the finished statement underneath. Reads both ways: paste a SELECT and the blocks fill in. Values compile to bound parameters and identifiers are allow-listed against the schema.

api.name: tables
api.description: { name, columns } where columns are `SchemaColumn` — the same type [[schema-table]] takes, so one schema description feeds both.

api.name: vs QueryEditor
api.description: The editor is for people who know SQL and want a console. This is for people who know the question and not the dialect. They are meant to sit beside each other, and the generated statement pastes straight into the editor.

api.name: values
api.description: A value never enters the SQL string — it is emitted as `$1` (or `?`) and returned in `params`. That is what makes the output safe to execute.

api.name: identifiers
api.description: No driver can parameterise a table or column name, so the defence is a list: every identifier is looked up in the schema you passed and anything absent is dropped. A name cannot reach the query unless it was already in your schema.

api.name: follows the schema
api.description: Pickers only offer columns of the tables in play, qualified as `table.column`. Changing the source table clears the choices that named the old one instead of leaving a query that will not run.

api.name: joins
api.description: A `references` on a column is a join the schema already knows about, so it is suggested rather than retyped.

api.name: where
api.description: The same nested-precedence problem, so the same component — solving it twice would give two answers to "what does A or B and C mean".

api.name: what it will not build
api.description: Sub-queries, CTEs, window functions and unions. Past a certain complexity a builder is slower than typing, which is what the editor is for.

api.name: reads both ways
api.description: The Paste SQL panel parses a statement back into the controls, seeded with the current one so it doubles as "edit this as text". A builder that only compiles is a dead end — you can construct a query but never open the one you already have.

api.name: the parser
api.description: Tokeniser plus recursive descent over the same subset it emits, so a compile/parse round trip is lossless. Bare columns are qualified against the tables in scope, and `a AND b OR c` is read as `(a AND b) OR c` rather than flattened into something that means something else.

api.name: pasted SQL is not trusted
api.description: A literal in a pasted WHERE becomes a bound parameter when it compiles back, and a table you did not declare is dropped with a reason rather than carried through.

api.name: one block per decision
api.description: Each clause is a titled card holding only its own controls, and each carries its own action — which is why joining a table is a button on Sources rather than a control floating between clauses. Order, group and limit sit in a row, because three small choices do not each deserve a full-width band.

api.name: removing a table
api.description: Dropping a join also clears that table from the columns, the filter, the ordering and the grouping, rather than leaving a statement that names a table it no longer joins.

api.name: dialect
api.description: One switch for everything that differs: quoting (`"x"`, `` `x` ``, `[x]`), placeholders (`$1`, `?`, `@p1`), boolean literals versus 1 and 0, and the operator list. A provider switcher sits with the statement because it is the statement it changes.

api.name: IN
api.description: Compiles to `IN ($1, $2, $3)` with one placeholder per item — the list is bound, never spliced. `SegmentBuilder` grew a `many` arity for it, so "is one of" is finally a list input rather than a single select.

api.name: provider-only operators
api.description: `ILIKE` and `~` on PostgreSQL, `REGEXP` and `SOUNDS LIKE` on MySQL, `GLOB` on SQLite. Opening a query on a provider that lacks one drops that condition and says which operator and which provider.

api.name: SQL Server has no LIMIT
api.description: It compiles to `OFFSET 0 ROWS FETCH NEXT @p1 ROWS ONLY`, which is a syntax error without an ORDER BY — so a limit with no ordering is reported rather than emitted.

api.name: functions
api.description: How a function gets used: declare `{ name, families?, returns?, dialects? }` and it is offered as `fn(table.column)` wherever a column can go, in the columns, the filter, the ordering. An undeclared name cannot reach the statement — the same allow-list that protects table names.

api.name: onCompile
api.description: Fires when the statement changes, keyed on the output rather than the callback identity so an inline arrow does not loop.

demos.title: Team users in DE or FR, joined to plans

query-plan.label: Query Plan
query-plan.description: An EXPLAIN tree with cost bars drawn from self cost, not total. Every root holds 100% of total by definition, so a total-cost bar makes the root look like the problem in every query ever profiled.

api.name: plan
api.description: `{ id, operation, relation?, estimatedRows?, actualRows?, cost?, actualMs?, children? }`.

api.name: misestimateFactor
api.description: Ratio past which estimate-vs-actual is flagged. That mismatch is the most useful number in a plan — it means stale statistics, and it is why the planner chose a nested loop.

api.name: seqScanRows
api.description: Row count above which a sequential scan is marked. A seq scan on a small table is optimal; over two million rows it is usually a missing index.

api.name: bars
api.description: Total minus children — the node that is actually spending the time.

schema-table.label: Schema Table
schema-table.description: Columns, keys and indexes. Foreign keys name their target inline, because `owner_id` tells you nothing about whether it points at users or accounts — which is exactly what you opened the schema to find out.
schema-table.usage:
import { SchemaTable } from '@/components/ui/schema-table'

<SchemaTable name="users" columns={columns} indexes={indexes} />

api.name: columns
api.description: `{ name, type, nullable?, primaryKey?, references?, default?, comment? }`.

api.name: nullable
api.description: "not null" is printed. A blank in a nullable column reads as missing information, when the constraint is the fact.

api.name: indexes
api.description: Columns in order. An index on `(a, b)` cannot serve a query filtering only on `b`, and a set-like display hides that.

api.name: references
api.description: e.g. `users.id`. Rendered inline against the column.

migration-list.label: Migration List
migration-list.description: Applied and pending migrations, sorted by version. A migration applied after a later version is flagged — that is the signature of two branches merged without a rebase, and it means this schema matches no single branch.

api.name: migrations
api.description: `{ version, name, state, appliedAt?, duration?, irreversible?, error? }`.

api.name: ordering
api.description: Never by array order. Migrations are timestamp-named precisely so they sort deterministically, and trusting the supplied order shows a rebase artefact as the real sequence.

api.name: out of order
api.description: Applied after a higher version — a merge without a rebase.

api.name: irreversible
api.description: Knowing there is no down-path before you run something is the difference between a rollback and a restore from backup.

connection-string.label: Connection String
connection-string.description: A DSN parsed into the parts that matter for its driver. A file-backed database has a path and no host, user or port — pretending every database is Postgres is what makes most of these components useless outside it.

api.name: value
api.description: URL-style (`postgres://…`, `sqlite:///…`) or the semicolon key=value style SQL Server and ODBC use. A string that parses as neither is reported, not half-rendered.

api.name: drivers
api.description: Adds to or replaces the built-in profiles by scheme. A profile declares which fields exist, their labels, whether the path is a file, the default port, and which parameters to flag.

api.name: file-backed drivers
api.description: Show a path and nothing else. A relative path is flagged, because it resolves against the working directory of whatever starts the process rather than the config file.

api.name: masking
api.description: A DSN carries a live password mid-string, and this is the screen people paste into tickets.

api.name: warnings
api.description: `sslmode=disable` on Postgres, `encrypt=false` on SQL Server, `tls=false` on MongoDB — plus an unencoded password containing `@` `/` `?` or `#`, which silently reassigns the host.

build-log.label: Build Log
build-log.description: Steps with their own output and timing bars. Failed steps open by default and successful ones stay closed — nobody opens a build log to read the steps that worked.

api.name: steps
api.description: `{ id, name, status, duration?, output?, defaultOpen? }`.

api.name: default open
api.description: Expanding everything means scrolling past 4,000 lines of dependency installation to find the error.

api.name: duration bars
api.description: The step making the build slow is visible without reading every number — the second reason anyone opens a build log.

api.name: running
api.description: A number that ticks while you read it is harder to compare than one that is absent until final.

bundle-treemap.label: Bundle Treemap
bundle-treemap.description: Bundle size by module, laid out by compressed size. Raw bytes overstate text-heavy modules dramatically — a 400KB locale file that gzips to 12KB dominates a raw treemap and barely matters on the wire.

api.name: modules
api.description: `{ name, size, gzip? }`. Sizes in bytes.

api.name: useGzip
api.description: Lay out by compressed size when available. Toggle it in the composer to see the locale file take over.

api.name: layout
api.description: Not slice-and-dice: long thin slivers cannot be compared by eye or clicked, which defeats the shape.

api.name: why a treemap
api.description: A sorted bar chart answers "what is largest". A treemap answers "what is this bundle made of", which is the question when a build doubles.

coverage-report.label: Coverage Report
coverage-report.description: Coverage per file, ranked by uncovered lines rather than by percentage. A 400-line file at 92% has 32 untested lines; a 12-line file at 60% has 5 — and percentage ranks the small one first.

api.name: files
api.description: `{ path, statements, branches, functions, lines, uncovered? }` — ratios 0–1.

api.name: metric
api.description: Statement coverage flatters: a file can hit every statement and miss half its branches, which is where the bugs are.

api.name: threshold
api.description: Drawn as a line on every bar, so "below target" is visible per row without reading numbers.

api.name: uncovered
api.description: Expands to the actual line numbers — the thing you need to act.

benchmark-table.label: Benchmark Table
benchmark-table.description: Ranked results with variance. A difference inside the combined error bars is reported as "within noise" rather than as a win — printing "1.03× faster" from two noisy runs is how performance myths start.

api.name: results
api.description: `{ name, value, error?, samples? }`. `error` is a standard deviation or margin, in the same unit as `value`.

api.name: inconclusive
api.description: Overlapping error bars against the leader. Refusing to call that a win is the point of the component.

api.name: higherIsBetter
api.description: ops/sec: true. Nanoseconds per op: false. "2.4×" is ambiguous without it, and both directions are normal.

api.name: scale
api.description: Linear bars turn a 1000× spread into one full bar and nine invisible ones.

flame-graph.label: Flame Graph
flame-graph.description: Width is time, depth is stack. Frames stay in call order rather than being sorted by cost — reordering them destroys the shape a flame graph exists to show.

api.name: root
api.description: `{ name, value, children? }` where value is total time including children.

api.name: zoom
api.description: Ancestors stay as a breadcrumb. Losing your place while zooming is what makes most flame graph implementations frustrating.

api.name: self time
api.description: A frame 400ms wide spending 3ms in itself is not the problem — its child is. Total alone cannot tell you which.

api.name: sub-pixel frames
api.description: Thousands of sliver rectangles cost real render time and show nothing.

lighthouse-score.label: Lighthouse Score
