lighthouse-score.description: Category rings with the metrics behind them. A performance score of 62 is not actionable; "LCP 4.1s" is — so the metrics are shown, not hidden behind the summary.

api.name: categories
api.description: `{ id, label, score, metrics? }` with score 0–100.

api.name: bands
api.description: Matching the reference tool. Inventing our own would make a green here mean something different from a green in the report the number came from.

api.name: metrics
api.description: The score summarises them; only the metrics can be acted on. `poor: true` tints one.

api.name: ring
api.description: Not a conic gradient — it prints, scales, and takes the theme's own colours.

regex-tester.label: Regex Tester
regex-tester.description: A pattern against a test string, with matches highlighted and capture groups listed. Zero-length matches are guarded — `/a*/g` matches empty at every position and hangs a naive exec loop.

api.name: pattern / flags / input
api.description: All three are controlled or uncontrolled independently, so you can pin the pattern and let the test string be edited.

api.name: errors
api.description: An unfinished pattern is the normal state while typing, so a syntax error is a hint — the previous match set is not discarded.

api.name: groups
api.description: Numbered and named. A pattern that matches but captures the wrong thing is the failure people actually hit, and a highlight cannot show it.

api.name: zero-length
api.description: lastIndex is advanced manually — the bug in most hand-rolled regex testers.

merge-conflict.label: Merge Conflict
merge-conflict.description: Both sides of a conflict with a resolution per hunk. "Keep both" is offered because it is frequently right — two people adding a different import conflict textually and agree semantically.
merge-conflict.usage:
import { MergeConflict } from '@/components/ui/merge-conflict'

<MergeConflict path={path} hunks={hunks} onResolve={resolve} />

api.name: hunks
api.description: `{ id, ours, theirs, base?, context? }`.

api.name: layout
api.description: Not side by side. Conflict hunks are rarely the same height, so columns desynchronise and you compare line 4 against line 9.

api.name: resolutions
api.description: Controlled or uncontrolled. Nothing resolves itself — a conflict UI that quietly defaults to one side is how code disappears in a merge.

api.name: unresolved count
api.description: It does not go down until a choice is made.

symbol-outline.label: Symbol Outline
symbol-outline.description: A file's symbols as a tree, in file order rather than alphabetical. An outline is a map of the document you are reading; re-sorting it makes the outline and the editor disagree about where things are.

api.name: symbols
api.description: `{ id, name, kind, line?, exported?, children? }`.

api.name: filtering
api.description: Flattening to matched leaves loses the class a method belongs to, and `render` alone is useless when six components define one.

api.name: exported
api.description: Draws a dot. "Is this part of the public surface" is what an outline gets used for, and the name cannot answer it.

api.name: order
api.description: Never alphabetical.

changelog-entry.label: Changelog Entry
changelog-entry.description: A release grouped by change type, with breaking changes hoisted to the top whatever order they came in. Everything else in a changelog is optional reading; a breaking change is not.
changelog-entry.usage:
import { ChangelogEntry } from '@/components/ui/changelog-entry'

<ChangelogEntry version="2.4.0" date={date} changes={changes} />

api.name: changes
api.description: Groups: breaking, security, added, changed, fixed, deprecated, removed.

api.name: group order
api.description: Rendered in a fixed sequence rather than object key order, so two releases are visually comparable.

api.name: version
api.description: People navigate a changelog by version; a date-led entry forces a translation step every time.

api.name: yanked
api.description: Dims the entry and states plainly that it was withdrawn.

jwt-inspector.label: JWT Inspector
jwt-inspector.description: Decodes a token into header, payload and signature. Decoding is not verification and the component says so — a green tick without the signing key would be actively dangerous.

api.name: token
api.description: Three base64url segments. A malformed token is reported, not half-rendered.

api.name: exp / nbf / iat
api.description: Shown as real times. A bare epoch integer is the most misread field in a token — off-by-1000 between seconds and milliseconds costs an afternoon.

api.name: alg: none
api.description: The classic JWT vulnerability, and it looks like an ordinary field in a JSON dump.

api.name: signature
api.description: This gets screenshotted into tickets, and a token with its signature is a live credential.

container-list.label: Container List
container-list.description: Running containers with state, image tag and resource use. Restart count is shown whenever it is non-zero — a container "running" with 47 restarts is crash-looping, and its state says everything is fine.

api.name: containers
api.description: `{ id, name, image, tag?, state, startedAt?, restarts?, ports?, cpu?, memory? }`.

api.name: restarts
api.description: Not only when unhealthy. A crash loop hides behind a green "running".

api.name: tag
api.description: `:latest` is the detail that explains why two hosts are running different code.

api.name: actions
api.description: Start is absent on a running container rather than disabled — a greyed control on every row is noise.

port-table.label: Port Table
port-table.description: Published ports with their bind address. `0.0.0.0:5432` and `127.0.0.1:5432` are the difference between a database on the internet and a database on the machine — printing only the number hides that.

api.name: ports
api.description: `{ id, port, targetPort?, protocol?, address?, process?, tls?, service? }`.

api.name: address
api.description: Bound to every interface is highlighted; loopback is not.

api.name: exposure
api.description: That combination is the actual finding. Either alone is often fine.

api.name: service names
api.description: 5432 means nothing to someone who does not already know it is Postgres.

env-diff.label: Env Diff
env-diff.description: Two environments side by side, values masked by default. A variable missing from one side is drawn differently from one whose value merely differs — "not set" and "set to something else" have different causes.
env-diff.usage:
import { EnvDiff } from '@/components/ui/env-diff'

<EnvDiff left={staging} right={production} leftLabel="Staging" rightLabel="Production" />

api.name: left / right
api.description: `{ key, value, secret? }`. A `value` of `undefined` means not set.

api.name: masking
api.description: This is the screen someone opens when staging differs from production, and the screen that gets screenshotted into a shared channel with a password in it.

api.name: whitespace
api.description: Values differing only in whitespace are flagged — a trailing newline in a secret is invisible and takes a service down.

api.name: ordering
api.description: Missing and differing rows above identical ones, which are collapsed behind a count.

queue-monitor.label: Queue Monitor
queue-monitor.description: Depth, throughput and whether the queue is keeping up. Depth alone says nothing — 40,000 draining at 5,000/s is fine, 300 draining at 2/s is an incident.
queue-monitor.usage:
import { QueueMonitor } from '@/components/ui/queue-monitor'

<QueueMonitor name="emails" depth={1920} arrivalRate={42} completionRate={61} />

api.name: arrivalRate / completionRate
api.description: Together they give the drain estimate. Set completions below arrivals in the composer to watch it flip to "growing".

api.name: deadLettered
api.description: Never folded into `failed`. A retryable failure is noise; an exhausted job is lost work a human must decide about.

api.name: oldestAt
api.description: Age of the oldest waiting job, not average wait — averages hide the one job stuck behind a poison message.

api.name: history
api.description: Optional depth sparkline.

cache-stats.label: Cache Stats
cache-stats.description: Hit rate with the numbers behind it. 99% on 40 requests a day is noise and 80% on 4 million is a cost centre, so volume sits beside the percentage.
cache-stats.usage:
import { CacheStats } from '@/components/ui/cache-stats'

<CacheStats hits={3_812_400} misses={214_800} evictions={8_120} />

api.name: hits / misses
api.description: The rate is derived from them, so it cannot disagree with the counts printed underneath.

api.name: evictions
api.description: A miss means the key was never there; an eviction means the cache threw it away. Sizing problem, not warming problem — and a different fix.

api.name: history
api.description: Hit rate over time, 0–1 per sample.

api.name: bytes / keys
api.description: Optional footprint figures.

rate-limit-meter.label: Rate Limit Meter
rate-limit-meter.description: A quota with its reset time given equal weight. "9,800 of 10,000" is alarming; "resets in 40 seconds" makes it fine — showing the first without the second sends people to build a cache they do not need.
rate-limit-meter.usage:
import { RateLimitMeter } from '@/components/ui/rate-limit-meter'

<RateLimitMeter limit={10000} remaining={1840} resetAt={reset} windowSeconds={3600} />

api.name: remaining
api.description: Not used. Both are on screen, but remaining is what a caller acts on — inverting it costs a subtraction every glance.

api.name: windowSeconds
api.description: Enables the burn-rate projection: whether the quota runs out before the reset. Drop `remaining` low with a long window left to see it fire.

api.name: resetAt
api.description: Given equal prominence to the count.

api.name: meter
api.description: With a window-elapsed marker for comparing spend against time.

demos.title: Room to spare, and nearly out
demos.code:
<RateLimitMeter limit={5_000} remaining={4_120} resetAt={resetsAt} />
<RateLimitMeter limit={5_000} remaining={80} resetAt={resetsAt} />

websocket-frames.label: WebSocket Frames
websocket-frames.description: A frame log with the delta between frames. Protocol bugs are about the gap — a heartbeat that stopped arriving is obvious as a 30-second delta and invisible as a list of clock times.

api.name: frames
api.description: `{ id, direction, opcode?, data, at, bytes? }`.

api.name: direction
api.description: Never colour alone — a frame log gets screenshotted into monochrome tickets, and "what did we send just before it broke" is the whole point. Rows stay flush so the payload column keeps a straight left edge.

api.name: showControl
api.description: Ping every 15 seconds buries the four frames that matter. Turn it on in the composer to see the difference.

api.name: delta
api.description: Gap from the previous visible frame; over 30s is tinted.
